# Undeclared Family Members Policy Ended September 10, 2026

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/undeclared-family-members-public-policy-expired-september-2026
Category: Family Sponsorship
Published: 2026-09-13
Author: Go Far Global Team

> > This is for people who were not declared or examined when their sponsor became a permanent resident, and who hoped to be sponsored as a spouse, partner, or dependent child.

# Undeclared Family Members Policy Ended September 10, 2026

*As of September 12, 2026.* Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) ended the temporary public policy that could exempt certain previously undeclared family members from the sponsorship bars in Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) paragraphs 117(9)(d) and 125(1)(d). The policy ended on September 10, 2026 and was not renewed.

> This is for people who were not declared or examined when their sponsor became a permanent resident, and who hoped to be sponsored as a spouse, partner, or dependent child. IRCC still applies the expired policy only to eligible applications it received from May 31, 2019 through September 10, 2026.

## TL;DR

Ended September 10, 2026 and not renewed | IRCC still applies it to eligible applications received May 31, 2019 through September 10, 2026 | New receipts from September 11, 2026 face IRPR 117(9)(d) and 125(1)(d) | Sponsor had to be a resettled refugee, protected person, or family-class / SCLPC sponsored relative | Economic-class sponsors were never in this policy

## Did the undeclared family members public policy end on September 10, 2026?

**Short answer:** Yes. IRCC's [applicant page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/who-you-can-sponsor/undeclared-family.html) now shows Status: Expired. The [official public policy text](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/public-policies/certain-sponsored-foreign-nationals-excluded.html) is archived. Both pages, with details dated September 11, 2026, state that the policy allowing certain undeclared family members to be sponsored ended on September 10, 2026. IRCC has not published a replacement instrument on those pages. The expired instrument ran under section 25.2 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA). It took effect on September 10, 2023 or the signature date, whichever came last, and ended on September 10, 2026. Earlier 2019 and 2021 windows are not a reason to treat a new file as covered.

## Who could be sponsored under the expired policy?

**Short answer:** Previously undeclared family members may have been eligible if they applied to be sponsored as a spouse, common-law partner, conjugal partner, or dependent child, they were not declared or examined when the sponsor became a permanent resident, and the sponsor obtained permanent residence through one of four routes IRCC listed. Those routes are resettled refugee (Convention refugee or a person in similar circumstances), protected person, family-class sponsored spouse, partner, or dependent child, or Spouse or Common-Law Partner in Canada (SCLPC) class sponsored spouse or common-law partner. The [applicant page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/who-you-can-sponsor/undeclared-family.html) uses past tense because the policy has ended. Meeting those bullets does not decide a file. Completeness, admissibility, and the grandfather window still matter.

| Sponsor's permanent residence path | In this public policy? |
|---|---|
| Resettled refugee (Convention refugee or similar circumstances) | Yes, if the other conditions were met |
| Protected person | Yes, if the other conditions were met |
| Family-class sponsored spouse, partner, or dependent child | Yes, if the other conditions were met |
| SCLPC sponsored spouse or common-law partner | Yes, if the other conditions were met |
| Express Entry, Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), or other economic class | No |

## Who was not eligible under this public policy?

**Short answer:** IRCC says previously undeclared family members were not eligible if declaring or examining them at the time would have made the sponsor ineligible for the class under which the sponsor immigrated. The [applicant page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/who-you-can-sponsor/undeclared-family.html) gives examples: the sponsor immigrated as a spouse while already married or in a common-law relationship with the undeclared person; the sponsor came as a dependent child while married or in a common-law relationship; or the sponsor came under a program that required them to be single with no dependants. The archived policy also kept all other admissibility and eligibility rules, required the usual family-class or SCLPC fees, and kept Quebec sponsorship undertakings where the sponsor lives in Quebec.

## Were economic-class sponsors covered?

**Short answer:** No. The sponsor pathways in the [archived public policy](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/public-policies/certain-sponsored-foreign-nationals-excluded.html) are refugee, protected-person, family-class, and SCLPC routes only. A sponsor who obtained permanent residence through [Express Entry](/immigration/express-entry), a [provincial nominee](/immigration/provincial-nominee), or another economic-class program was not in this exemption. Do not treat an economic-class history as a way around IRPR 117(9)(d) or 125(1)(d). Ordinary [family immigration](/immigration/family-immigration) and [spousal sponsorship](/immigration/sponsorship/spousal) rules still apply, including the undeclared-family bars unless another lawful pathway exists.

## What happens to applications received from May 31, 2019 through September 10, 2026?

**Short answer:** IRCC will continue to apply the public policy to eligible applications it received between May 31, 2019 and September 10, 2026. That window is on both the [expired applicant page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/who-you-can-sponsor/undeclared-family.html) and the [archived policy text](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/public-policies/certain-sponsored-foreign-nationals-excluded.html). It is a receipt window, not a promise that every file in the range qualifies. The application had to be eligible under the policy's conditions. Timing, completeness, and the sponsor's permanent residence class still control the assessment. This article does not decide your file. Check [processing times](/immigration/processing-times) for the sponsorship stream you actually filed.

| When IRCC received the application | This expired public policy |
|---|---|
| May 31, 2019 through September 10, 2026, and you met the conditions | IRCC can still assess you under the exemption |
| On or after September 11, 2026 | Not available |
| Filed, but the sponsor was economic class | Never in this policy |

## What do new applications face after September 10, 2026?

**Short answer:** Applications IRCC receives on or after September 11, 2026 do not get this exemption. [IRPR paragraph 117(9)(d)](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/sor-2002-227/section-117.html) says a foreign national is not a member of the family class by virtue of their relationship to a sponsor if, at the time of the sponsor's own permanent residence application, that foreign national was a non-accompanying family member and was not examined. [IRPR paragraph 125(1)(d)](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/sor-2002-227/section-125.html) says the same for the SCLPC class. Other admissibility and eligibility rules still apply. The expired policy never waived every IRCC requirement. Humanitarian and compassionate consideration under IRPA section 25(1) is a separate statutory pathway. IRCC's two pages for this expiry do not publish H&C instructions for this situation.

When you apply for permanent residence you must declare all family members, even if they are not coming with you. IRCC lists spouse, common-law partner, dependent children, and grandchildren who are dependent children of your dependent children. They must also complete medical exams and pass background and security checks so they can be eligible to be sponsored later where the law allows.

## What does "family reunification" mean?

**Short answer:** In Canadian immigration practice, family reunification usually means using published family-class or related pathways so close relatives can join a citizen or permanent resident in Canada, for example [spousal sponsorship](/immigration/sponsorship/spousal) or other [sponsorship](/immigration/sponsorship) streams. The undeclared-family temporary public policy was a time-limited exemption from specific regulatory bars for certain previously undeclared spouses, partners, or dependent children in those streams. It ended on September 10, 2026. It was not a general family-reunification opening, and it was not parent or grandparent intake. See IRCC's [expired applicant page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/who-you-can-sponsor/undeclared-family.html) for the classes it actually named.

## Can I bring my family to us?

**Short answer:** It depends on your status in Canada, the relative's relationship to you, and the live IRCC rules for that class. This expired public policy only helped certain previously undeclared spouses, partners, or dependent children where the sponsor had obtained permanent residence through the refugee, protected-person, or family / SCLPC routes listed above. Economic-class sponsors were never in this policy. New applications received on or after September 11, 2026 do not get this exemption. If IRCC already received an eligible file from May 31, 2019 through September 10, 2026, that receipt window is the one IRCC said it will still apply. Confirm the live pages before you act, and use ordinary [family immigration](/immigration/family-immigration) rules for any new sponsorship.

## How can a Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) help?

**Short answer:** Go Far Global, a Toronto Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm, can check whether IRCC received a sponsorship application from May 31, 2019 through September 10, 2026, map the sponsor's permanent residence pathway against the historical classes, and explain what IRPR 117(9)(d) and 125(1)(d) mean for a new receipt after expiry. We do not invent eligibility or promise a renewed public policy. If the relative is a spouse or partner, we review the file against current [spousal sponsorship](/immigration/sponsorship/spousal) rules rather than stretching an archived instrument.

If you want that read on your documents, [book a consultation](/book). Other updates: [news](/news).

## Frequently asked questions

### Which family members can sponsor you in Canada?

Sponsorship runs the other way. A Canadian citizen or permanent resident (the sponsor) sponsors an eligible foreign national. Under the expired undeclared-family policy, the foreign national had to apply as a spouse, common-law partner, conjugal partner, or dependent child, and the sponsor had to fall within the permanent residence pathways IRCC listed. Parent and grandparent sponsorship is a different program and was not this public policy.

### Will there be parent sponsorship programs in Canada in 2026?

Parent and grandparent sponsorship is separate from the undeclared-family temporary public policy that ended September 10, 2026. This article does not invent Parent and Grandparent Program (PGP) intake dates. See our note on [IRCC pausing parent and grandparent sponsorship in 2026](/news/ircc-pauses-parent-grandparent-sponsorship-2026) and confirm current IRCC openings before you plan a PGP file.

# Work Permit Holders Can Study Without a Study Permit (2026)

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/work-permit-holders-study-without-study-permit-2026
Category: Work Permit
Published: 2026-09-10
Author: Go Far Global Team

> > This is for foreign workers already in Canada who want a short licence, trade, or training course.

# Work Permit Holders Can Study Without a Study Permit (2026)

*As of September 12, 2026.* Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) brought a new temporary public policy into force on September 4, 2026 that lets a valid work permit holder study a course or program of six months or less without a study permit, including when that course runs past the stay authorized on first entry.

> This is for foreign workers already in Canada who want a short licence, trade, or training course. It is not a new way to enter Canada, and it is not a substitute for a [study permit](/immigration/study-permit) on a program longer than six months.

## TL;DR

In force September 4, 2026, expires December 31, 2027 | You need a valid work permit and a program of 6 months or less | IRCC signed the policy on August 5, 2026 | 1,554,470 people in Canada held only a work permit as of June 30, 2026 | Full-time study under this policy does not count toward Canadian Experience Class (CEC) work experience

## Can I study while being on a work permit in Canada?

**Short answer:** Yes, if you hold a valid [work permit](/immigration/work-permit) and the course or program is six months or less. IRCC’s [worker instructions](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/special-instructions/workers-study-without-study-permit.html), posted with a September 9, 2026 page date, say you may study without a study permit for six months or less, or until the work permit expires, whichever comes first. The legal instrument is the [temporary public policy](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/public-policies/study-without-study-permit-2026-2.html) signed in Ottawa on August 5, 2026 by Minister Lena Metlege Diab. It took effect 30 days after signature, on September 4, 2026. It expires on December 31, 2027, and IRCC may revoke it earlier without notice. You still have to keep the work conditions that are not about studying, and you still need a study permit for any program longer than six months.

## Who is eligible under the September 2026 public policy?

**Short answer:** The only eligibility condition in the instrument is that the foreign national holds a valid work permit. There is no June 2023 application-date cutoff, and there is no occupation list. The [public policy text](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/public-policies/study-without-study-permit-2026-2.html) then limits the exemption to a course or program of six months or less, and it exempts you only from the part of [Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) paragraph 188(1)(c)](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/sor-2002-227/section-188.html) that says the short course must finish within the stay authorized on first entry. That is the point for workers who later extended. The exemption lasts until your work permit expires, or until the policy expires or is revoked, whichever comes first. Other admissibility rules still apply.

| Test | What IRCC requires |
|---|---|
| Status | Valid work permit |
| Program length | 6 months or less |
| How long you can study | 6 months, or until the work permit expires, whichever is first |
| Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) | Not required if you meet this policy, as of September 4, 2026 |
| Start date | September 4, 2026 |
| End date | December 31, 2027, unless revoked sooner |
| People in Canada with only a work permit, June 30, 2026 | [1,554,470](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/reports-statistics/statistics-open-data/immigration-stats/students-workers.html) |

## Can I study for 6 months on a work permit?

**Short answer:** Yes. Six months or less is the duration cap on this public policy, and it is also the duration already written into [IRPR 188(1)(c)](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/sor-2002-227/section-188.html) for studying without a study permit. The standing regulation still says the short course must be completed within the period of stay authorized upon entry. Work permit holders often stay far past that first stamp because they extended. This policy lifts that “original entry” timing rule for people with a valid work permit, so a six-month course can run to the end of the current permit, not only to the first entry date. If the course is longer than six months, this policy does not cover it. Apply for a [study permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit.html) instead, and check [processing times](/immigration/processing-times) before you enrol.

## What did the expired June 2023 policy cover, and what is different now?

**Short answer:** The earlier policy of the same name ran from June 27, 2023 to June 27, 2026 and is now [archived](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/public-policies/study-without-study-permit.html). It only covered people whose work permit application IRCC received on or before June 7, 2023, including some workers on maintained status under IRPR 186(u). In exchange it waived all of IRPR 188(1)(a) through (d), so longer programs were in play for that narrow group. The 2026 successor flips the trade: any valid work permit, but only six months or less, and only the original-entry timing in 188(1)(c) is waived. The June expiry write-up is at [Study without a study permit: policy ending June 2026](/news/study-without-study-permit-policy-ending-june-2026). That page is the old cohort. This page is the new rule.

| | 2023 policy (expired) | 2026 policy (in force) |
|---|---|---|
| Who | Work permit filed on or before June 7, 2023 | Any valid work permit |
| Program length | Not capped at 6 months in the instrument | 6 months or less |
| What is waived | IRPR 188(1)(a) to (d) | The original-entry timing in 188(1)(c) |
| Dates | June 27, 2023 to June 27, 2026 | September 4, 2026 to December 31, 2027 |

## Do Quebec workers need a CAQ under this policy?

**Short answer:** No, if they meet the federal policy. IRCC’s [worker instructions](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/special-instructions/workers-study-without-study-permit.html) say workers in Quebec are eligible to study in Quebec without a study permit under this temporary public policy as of September 4, 2026, and that they do not need a Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) issued by the Ministère de l’Immigration, de la Francisation et de l’Intégration (MIFI) if they meet the eligibility criteria. IRCC states that the temporary CAQ exemption and the federal policy both took effect on September 4, 2026. Provincial quebec.ca pages can still mention the older June 7, 2023 work-permit application cohort. That is a different instrument. Confirm the live provincial page the week you enrol. This exemption still does not cover a program longer than six months. If the course is longer, the usual Quebec and federal [study permit](/immigration/study-permit) rules apply.

## How do I prove I am allowed to study without a study permit?

**Short answer:** Show the school your valid work permit. IRCC’s instructions say the learning institution may ask you to prove you are eligible to study without a study permit, and if they ask, the proof is the valid work permit. There is no extra IRCC letter. IRCC’s [September 9, 2026 notice](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/economic-growth-public-services-contributions-temporary-workers.html) said the department would begin notifying eligible work permit holders that week. A missing email does not cancel the policy if you already hold a valid work permit and the program is six months or less. If the school will not accept the work permit as proof, [apply for a study permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit.html).

## What happens to Canadian Experience Class (CEC) points if I study full-time?

**Short answer:** Work you do during full-time studies under this policy does not count toward [Canadian Experience Class](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/canadian-experience-class.html) eligibility, and it does not count as Canadian work experience points on the Express Entry [Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/check-score/crs-criteria.html). That warning is on the [worker instructions](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/special-instructions/workers-study-without-study-permit.html). It matches the standing CEC rule that work gained while you were a full-time student does not count, even on a co-op term. IRCC’s news notice also said full-time studies will still require a study permit. Read those two sentences together: a six-month course can be full-time on paper, but a multi-year diploma is not this policy, and full-time study can freeze the work hours you hoped to use for [Express Entry](/immigration/express-entry). Check your CRS on the [CRS calculator](/tools/crs-calculator) and the [Canadian Experience Class hub](/immigration/express-entry/canadian-experience-class) before you enrol if permanent residence is the goal.

## Can I start a co-op placement while studying without a study permit?

**Short answer:** Maybe, and it depends on the employer and occupation on your current work permit. IRCC says that if you want a co-op work placement while you study without a study permit, you may need a new [employer-specific work permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/permit-inside.html) before the placement starts. You need that new permit only if the co-op employer or occupation is different from your current employer or occupation. In that case you would hold two valid work permits at once: the original permit that lets you use this public policy, and a second permit that matches the co-op. [Open work permit](/immigration/work-permits/open-work-permit) holders do not need to apply for a new work permit for the co-op. You still have to stay inside the six-month program cap. A co-op that turns the studies into a longer program is a study permit file, not this exemption. For the ordinary student-placement rules, see [co-op work permits](/immigration/work-permits/co-op).

## Does studying on a work permit lead to a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)?

**Short answer:** No. A Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) is for people who held a study permit and completed an eligible program at a designated learning institution. IRCC’s [PGWP eligibility page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html) and the [study permit eligibility page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/eligibility.html) both treat the study permit as the starting document. This public policy lets you skip the study permit for a short course. Skipping the study permit also skips the PGWP path. If a PGWP is part of the plan, apply for the study permit first, confirm the school and program are PGWP-eligible, then complete that program. See the [PGWP hub](/immigration/work-permits/pgwp). Short licensing or training taken on a work permit is for the job you already have, not for a new open work permit after graduation.

## What are the new rules for work permits in Canada in 2026?

**Short answer:** This September 2026 measure is one 2026 work-permit rule, and it is not an entry pathway. IRCC’s [September 9, 2026 notice](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/economic-growth-public-services-contributions-temporary-workers.html) frames it as a way for workers already in Canada, including tradespeople, nurses, and laboratory technicians, to take short licensing or training while they keep working. The same notice says the government still wants the temporary population under 5% of Canada’s total by the end of 2027. Other 2026 work and study rules sit elsewhere: student co-op work permits were dropped for eligible post-secondary students on April 1, 2026 on the [work as a student](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work.html) page, and PGWP and spousal open work permit cuts from 2024 and 2025 are still in force. None of those changes lets a new worker arrive from abroad on the strength of this study exemption.

You do not have to meet work permit conditions that are about studying. You do have to agree hours with your employer if the course cuts into the contract. That is on the [worker instructions](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/special-instructions/workers-study-without-study-permit.html). A closed work permit still ties you to the named employer. This is not a transfer, not an open work permit, and not a [provincial nominee](/immigration/provincial-nominee) shortcut.

We check expiry dates against the December 31, 2027 policy end, flag CEC and CRS damage if the course is full-time, and file a study permit when the program is too long for this exemption. If a spouse or child is on a separate permit, we map [family immigration](/immigration/family-immigration) status so one person’s course does not strand the rest of the file. For workers who still need a study permit, we prepare the application against current [study permit](/immigration/study-permit) rules rather than stretching this policy past six months.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can a work permit holder study without a study permit?

Yes, under this temporary public policy, if the work permit is valid and the course or program is six months or less. The exemption is only from [IRPR 188(1)(c)](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/sor-2002-227/section-188.html) original-entry timing. It is not a rewrite of every study-without-permit rule. It expires December 31, 2027 unless IRCC revokes it sooner.

### Can I study at IRCC without a study permit?

IRCC does not run academic programs. If the question is whether you can study in Canada without a study permit while holding a work permit: yes, for six months or less, if you hold a valid work permit, under the policy in force from September 4, 2026 to December 31, 2027 unless revoked. Longer programs need a study permit.

### Can I study for 6 months on a work permit?

Yes. Six months or less is the cap on this public policy. Your window also ends if the work permit expires first. See the section above on [IRPR 188(1)(c)](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/sor-2002-227/section-188.html).

### What are the new rules for international students to work in Canada in 2026?

Those rules are for people on a study permit, not for work permit holders using this policy. As of April 1, 2026, eligible post-secondary international students no longer need a separate co-op work permit for a required placement, according to IRCC’s [work as a student](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work.html) page. Off-campus hours during a regular academic session are still capped in the regulations. Do not mix that student-work package with this worker-study exemption.

### Can I study online in Canada without a study permit?

This public policy does not split online and in-person. If you hold a valid work permit and the program is six months or less, the [worker instructions](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/special-instructions/workers-study-without-study-permit.html) apply to the program of study, not to the classroom format. A person outside Canada taking a fully online course is not using a Canadian work permit, so this policy is not the tool. If the program is longer than six months, apply for a study permit.

### Can I study online while on a closed work permit in Canada?

Yes, if you still meet the two tests: valid work permit, program of six months or less. IRCC says you do not have to meet work permit conditions that are about studying. You still have to meet the job conditions. If the course cuts your hours, you need your employer’s agreement. A closed permit does not become an open permit because the course is online.

### Can I get PR after 2 year study in Canada?

Not through this policy. A two-year program is longer than six months, so you need a study permit, and any later permanent residence file would run through [Express Entry](/immigration/express-entry), a [provincial nominee](/immigration/provincial-nominee), or another program you actually qualify for. Six months of short training on a work permit does not create a two-year study record or a PGWP.

# Duolingo blocked for Iranian IDs: Canada school offers vs IRCC tests

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/duolingo-iran-english-tests-canada-pr-2026
Category: Express Entry
Published: 2026-09-04
Author: Go Far Global Team

> IRCC Express Entry English tests: CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training, PTE Core | Duolingo and TOEFL are not on that list | ETS: TOEFL and GRE stopped inside Iran; Iranian nationals may sit...

# Duolingo Iran Ban: Canada PR Tests and University Admission 2026

*As of September 3, 2026.* This week's test news is not an Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) rule change. It can still stop an Iranian applicant from getting into a Canadian school. Educational Testing Service (ETS) stopped TOEFL and GRE sittings inside Iran after the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) suspended General License G. Duolingo's help article "Is The Duolingo English Test available in Iran?" says the Duolingo English Test is unavailable in Iran and for users with Iranian IDs. Many Canadian universities accept that at-home test for admission. IRCC does not accept it for Express Entry. If the school will not issue a letter of acceptance without Duolingo, you cannot file a study permit. The English tests on the live IRCC permanent residence list remain CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training, and PTE Core.

## TL;DR

IRCC Express Entry English tests: CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training, PTE Core | Duolingo and TOEFL are not on that list | Study permit needs a letter of acceptance from a designated learning institution (DLI); IRCC does not collect Duolingo | University of Toronto undergraduate DET: overall 120 and Production 120 (tests on or after July 1, 2024) | Waterloo undergraduate DET after July 1, 2024: overall 120, Literacy 125, Production 125 | ETS: TOEFL and GRE stopped inside Iran; Iranian nationals may sit them outside Iran | Extra TOEFL/GRE score reports for people located in Iran: order by September 8, 2026 | Post-graduation work permit (PGWP) language tables also omit Duolingo

## Do IRCC accept Duolingo?

**Short answer:** No. IRCC's [Express Entry language test](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/language-test.html) page (date modified June 22, 2026) names the approved English tests: Canadian English Language Proficiency Index Program (CELPIP) General, International English Language Testing System (IELTS) General Training, and Pearson Test of English (PTE) Core. Duolingo is not on that list. TOEFL is not on that list. GRE is not a language test IRCC uses for Express Entry. A Duolingo score cannot be typed into an Express Entry profile as proof of Canadian Language Benchmarks (CLB). If you only have Duolingo, you still need one of the three approved English tests, or an approved French test, before you can rely on the file for [Express Entry](/immigration/express-entry).

The Iran news this week is a test-vendor problem, not a new IRCC instrument. [ETS's update on testing in Iran](https://www.ets.org/iran-testing-update.html) says OFAC suspended General License G, which had authorized TOEFL and GRE testing and related educational services in Iran. ETS stopped those services in Iran to comply with U.S. sanctions law. All future TOEFL and GRE appointments within Iran will be cancelled. Appointments paid through an ETS account get a full refund to the original payment method. Iranian nationals may still take TOEFL or GRE outside Iran, subject to registration rules and seat availability. If you already have scores and you are located in Iran, ETS says to order extra score reports by September 8, 2026. After that date ETS cannot process new score-report requests for test takers located in Iran at this time. There is no confirmed resume date.

That ETS path is for university admissions that ask for TOEFL or GRE. It is not a substitute for CELPIP, IELTS General Training, or PTE Core on a permanent residence file.

## Which English language tests are accepted for Canada PR?

**Short answer:** For Express Entry, IRCC accepts three English tests and two French tests. English: CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training, PTE Core. French: Test d'évaluation de français (TEF) Canada and Test de connaissance du français (TCF) Canada. IRCC measures English with CLB and French with Niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens (NCLC). IRCC does not accept IELTS One Skill Retake for Express Entry. You must take the named version. Results must be less than 2 years old when you complete the Express Entry profile and when you submit the permanent residence application. Expired results mean a refused application. Enter the scores, certificate number, and test PIN if the profile asks for them.

Minimums depend on the program, not on Duolingo bands.

| Program | English minimum IRCC names | French minimum IRCC names |
|---|---|---|
| Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP) | CLB 7 in all 4 abilities | NCLC 7 in all 4 abilities |
| Canadian Experience Class (CEC), TEER 0 or 1 | CLB 7 in all 4 abilities | NCLC 7 |
| CEC, TEER 2 or 3 | CLB 5 in all 4 abilities | NCLC 5 |
| Federal Skilled Trades | Speaking and listening CLB 5; reading and writing CLB 4 | Speaking and listening NCLC 5; reading and writing NCLC 4 |
| FSWP second official language | CLB or NCLC 5 | CLB or NCLC 5 |

TEER is Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities in the National Occupational Classification (NOC). If you are aiming at FSWP, read the [67-point grid](/news/federal-skilled-worker-67-points-eligibility-2026) next. Use the [Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) calculator](/tools/crs-calculator) after you have real approved-test scores, not a Duolingo screenshot.

A [post-graduation work permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility/language-results.html) (PGWP) filed on or after November 1, 2024 also needs proof of English or French. IRCC prints conversion tables for CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training, PTE Core, TEF Canada, and TCF Canada. Duolingo is not in those tables. The only language exception IRCC names on that page is graduation from a PGWP-eligible flight school. Applications submitted before November 1, 2024 do not have to meet those minimums.

IRCC does not run the tests or publish where seats are open. Book with the test agency. If you cannot sit a test in Iran, sit it in a country that still offers CELPIP, IELTS General Training, or PTE Core, then keep the report valid for the 2-year window.

## Is Duolingo accepted for PR in Canada?

**Short answer:** No for economic immigration through Express Entry. The approved-test list above is the list. Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) streams that use Express Entry still need those IRCC tests in the federal profile. A province can ask for extra language proof, but it cannot make Duolingo an Express Entry document. Citizenship is a different list. The [citizenship help answer](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=572&top=5) (date modified September 1, 2026) names CELPIP General, CELPIP General-LS, IELTS General, PTE Core, and several French diplomas and tests. It then says IRCC does not accept any other third-party test results, even if they are similar. Duolingo is not named there either.

Study is the lane this week's ban actually hits. See the student-visa and university questions below.

## Is Duolingo valid for Canada student visa?

**Short answer:** Not as an IRCC document. A study permit is not issued on a Duolingo score. IRCC's [who can apply](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/eligibility.html) page says you must be enrolled at a designated learning institution (DLI). The [document list](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents.html) always requires a letter of acceptance (LOA) from that school. Post-secondary schools must validate the LOA. If they do not, IRCC returns the file and refunds the fee. In most cases you also need a provincial or territorial attestation letter (PAL/TAL) after you accept the offer. None of those IRCC fields is a Duolingo PDF. The school decides which English test unlocks the offer. If Duolingo was the only test that school listed, and you can no longer sit it with an Iranian ID, you do not get the LOA, and you do not get a study permit. That is an admissions block, then an IRCC block.

Ask the school in writing which substitute it will take: IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT outside Iran, or another listed test. Book that test before the offer deadline. Then file the [study permit](/immigration/study-permit) with the LOA the school actually issues. Check the [DLI list](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/prepare/designated-learning-institutions-list.html) so the school is eligible.

## Which universities are accepted by Duolingo?

**Short answer:** Duolingo does not accept universities. Universities accept the test. Duolingo publishes an [accepting institutions](https://englishtest.duolingo.com/test_takers/accepting_institutions) list. Its [Canada blog](https://blog.englishtest.duolingo.com/is-the-duolingo-english-test-accepted-in-canada/) says many Canadian institutions take the Duolingo English Test for admission, including all Anglophone U15 schools in some capacity for undergraduate admissions. That is Duolingo's claim. Confirm the live program page for your intake. Two pages we fetched on September 3, 2026 still list DET for undergraduates: the [University of Toronto](https://future.utoronto.ca/english-language-requirements) and the [University of Waterloo](https://uwaterloo.ca/future-students/admissions/english-language-requirements). Both also list IELTS Academic and TOEFL iBT. Those two remain usable if DET is closed to your ID.

| Gate | What the page actually lists | Iranian ID / Iran sitting |
|---|---|---|
| IRCC Express Entry | CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training, PTE Core | IRCC did not change the list this week |
| IRCC study permit | LOA from a DLI, then PAL/TAL in most cases. No language test uploaded to IRCC | No LOA, no permit |
| University of Toronto undergraduate | DET: overall 120 and Production 120 (tests on or after July 1, 2024). IELTS Academic 6.5, no band below 6.0. No IELTS Indicator. No IELTS One Skill Retake | DET blocked if you must use an Iranian ID. IELTS Academic and TOEFL remain on the U of T page |
| University of Waterloo undergraduate | DET after July 1, 2024: overall 120, Literacy 125, Production 125, subscores required. IELTS Academic 6.5 overall; Waterloo accepts IELTS One Skill Retake | Same DET ID problem. Waterloo still lists IELTS Academic and TOEFL iBT |
| PGWP after November 1, 2024 | CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training, PTE Core, TEF Canada, TCF Canada tables | Duolingo is not in those tables |

TOEFL is a school test, not an Express Entry test. ETS still lets Iranian nationals sit TOEFL outside Iran. If your school wants TOEFL, travel to a centre that is open. Order extra score reports by September 8, 2026 if you are located in Iran and you already have a TOEFL or GRE on file.

## Which university of Canada accepts Duolingo?

**Short answer:** Several do, program by program. Do not treat a 2024 blog list as your offer. Open the English-language page for that faculty and that term. University of Toronto undergraduate still publishes DET cutoffs and tells you to send results to "University of Toronto - Undergraduate" with your U of T applicant number. Waterloo undergraduate still publishes DET cutoffs and tells you to select "University of Waterloo - Undergraduate." If those pages later drop DET, the printed cutoff is dead. If they keep DET and you cannot take it, use the other tests on the same page. IELTS for these schools is Academic, not the General Training version IRCC wants for Express Entry. Sitting Academic for admission does not give you an Express Entry language document. You may need two tests: Academic or TOEFL for the LOA, then General Training, CELPIP-General, or PTE Core later for PR or a PGWP.

A cancelled DET sitting is not an IRCC refusal. It is a missing school document. Email the admissions office now, name the Iranian-ID limit, and ask which listed test they will take before the deadline.

## Is Duolingo harder than IELTS?

**Short answer:** IRCC does not grade which test is harder. It names versions. For Express Entry you need IELTS General Training, not Academic, and not One Skill Retake. Duolingo is not an IRCC Express Entry test, so a "harder than IELTS" debate does not change a permanent residence file. If a Canadian school accepts Duolingo for admission, that school sets its own cutoff. IRCC will not convert a Duolingo score into CLB for Express Entry or for the PGWP tables.

People mixing this week's U.S. test news with IELTS are mixing vendors. ETS is TOEFL and GRE. Duolingo is the Duolingo English Test. IELTS is British Council and IDP. IRCC's June 22, 2026 language page still lists IELTS General Training. I did not find an IRCC page that copies the Duolingo Iranian-ID limit onto IELTS. If a booking site returns an error, that is a test-centre or identity rule from that vendor, not an IRCC draw. Screenshot the error, check the vendor, and still plan CELPIP-General or PTE Core if IELTS seats are tight.

CELPIP-General is the Canadian computer test IRCC names. Compare formats on our [CELPIP vs IELTS](/news/celpip-vs-ielts-canada-2026) page. Book the one you can actually sit while the 2-year clock still covers your invitation.

## Is DELF accepted for Canada PR?

**Short answer:** Not for Express Entry. The Express Entry approved French tests are TEF Canada and TCF Canada. Diplôme d'études en langue française (DELF) and Diplôme approfondi de langue française (DALF) appear on IRCC's [citizenship third-party test list](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=572&top=5), together with TCF, TCF pour le Québec, TEF, TEFAQ, and TEF Intégration, Résidence et Nationalité. That page is citizenship. It is not the Express Entry document page. Do not upload DELF as your Express Entry language test. If you want French points in the pool, sit TEF Canada or TCF Canada. Score charts for those tests are on our [TEF](/news/tef-canada-score-chart-clb-2026) and [TCF](/news/tcf-canada-score-chart-clb-express-entry-2026) pages.

French remains a real alternative if English seats are hard to book. IRCC still scores NCLC the same way it scored it last month. This week's OFAC change is about U.S. vendors in Iran, not about TEF or TCF.

We are Go Far Global, a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm. If a Duolingo ID limit is blocking an LOA, or a cancelled TOEFL date is blocking a profile, [book a consultation](/book). Bring the school name, the English page, the test date, and whether you need a [study permit](/immigration/study-permit), Express Entry, or a PGWP. Also see [work permit](/immigration/work-permit), [provincial nominee](/immigration/provincial-nominee), [family immigration](/immigration/family-immigration), [processing times](/immigration/processing-times), and [news](/news).

# Federal Skilled Worker 67 Points: Eligibility and Jobs 2026

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/federal-skilled-worker-67-points-eligibility-2026
Category: Express Entry
Published: 2026-09-04
Author: Go Far Global Team

> FSWP 67/100 selection grid, separate from CRS | Skilled work: Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities (TEER) 0, 1, 2, or 3 | At least 1 year continuous or 1,560 hours in the last 10...

# Federal Skilled Worker 67 Points: Eligibility and Jobs 2026

*As of September 3, 2026.* The Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP) is the Express Entry stream for people whose skilled work was mostly abroad. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) uses a 100-point grid. You need 67 points or more to enter the pool. That 67 is not your Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score. CRS is the later ranking used in rounds of invitations.

## TL;DR

FSWP 67/100 selection grid, separate from CRS | Skilled work: Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities (TEER) 0, 1, 2, or 3 | At least 1 year continuous or 1,560 hours in the last 10 years, paid | Language: Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB) 7 in all 4 abilities or you are not eligible | Plan to live outside Quebec | Proof of funds for 1 person: $15,263 (table updated July 7, 2025) unless Canadian Experience Class (CEC) or you have a valid job offer and authorization to work

## Who is eligible for the federal skilled worker program in Canada?

**Short answer:** You may qualify if you meet every minimum on IRCC's [Federal Skilled Worker Program](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html) page (date modified June 22, 2026) and then score 67 or more out of 100 on the selection factors. Minimums: paid skilled work in National Occupational Classification (NOC) TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3; the same NOC as your primary occupation; duties that match the lead statement and most main duties; work obtained in the last 10 years in Canada or abroad; at least 1 year continuous or 1,560 hours total at 30 hours per week; approved English or French tests with a score in writing, reading, listening, and speaking; Canadian secondary or post-secondary credentials, or a foreign credential plus an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA); and a plan to live outside Quebec. Volunteer work and unpaid internships do not count. Hours above 30 per week do not count extra.

If you score under 67, you do not qualify for this program. If you score 67 or more, you may submit an Express Entry profile. Invitations still depend on CRS and the round type. Check the grid on a [CRS calculator](/tools/crs-calculator) after you know you clear 67, not instead of 67.

| Selection factor | IRCC maximum |
|---|---:|
| Language skills | 28 (first official language 24, second official language 4) |
| Education | 25 |
| Skilled work experience | 15 |
| Age | 12 |
| Arranged employment | 10 |
| Adaptability | 10 |
| Pass mark | 67 / 100 |

Age points lock on the day IRCC gets the permanent residence application: 12 points at 18-35, then down each year to 0 at 47 and older. Experience points: 9 for 1 year, 11 for 2-3 years, 13 for 4-5 years, 15 for 6 or more years. Second official language is 4 points only with at least CLB 5 in all 4 abilities.

## What jobs qualify for the FSWP?

**Short answer:** IRCC does not publish a closed "FSWP job list." The job must be TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 in the NOC, and it must be the primary occupation you use on the file. IRCC describes skilled workers as managers and supervisors, and people in jobs that usually need a university degree, a college diploma, or apprenticeship training. Find your NOC first, then confirm TEER. Your primary occupation may not be your most recent job. Choose the NOC that matches the work you actually did. IRCC says a mismatch delays processing and puts you against the wrong program.

Count 1,560 hours as: one full-time job at up to 30 hours per week for 12 months; part-time that adds up to 1,560 hours (for example 15 hours per week for 24 months); or full-time at more than one job totalling 30 hours per week for 12 months. Student work can count if it was paid, continuous, and otherwise eligible. Self-employed work can count toward selection-factor experience points. The occupation still has to be TEER 0-3.

| How you get 1,560 hours | IRCC example |
|---|---|
| One full-time job | Up to 30 hours/week for 12 months |
| Part-time | 15 hours/week for 24 months, or any mix that totals 1,560 |
| Several full-time jobs | 30 hours/week for 12 months across more than one job |

Arranged employment can add up to 10 points if the offer is continuous, paid, full-time (minimum 30 hours/week), not seasonal, for at least 1 year, in TEER 0-3, and you fit one of IRCC's four Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) or LMIA-exempt situations. A job offer is not mandatory to enter as a Federal Skilled Worker.

## Which skilled worker is in demand in Canada?

**Short answer:** The FSWP page does not name 2026 shortage occupations. Eligibility is the TEER 0-3 test plus the 67-point grid, not a government in-demand list. Express Entry also runs category-based rounds. Those categories are announced on the rounds of invitations pages, round by round. A category round can invite people already in the pool who match that category. It does not rewrite FSWP minimums. If a consultant shows you a 2026 "most in-demand jobs" graphic with no IRCC URL, treat it as marketing.

Language is often the practical bottleneck. Below CLB 7 in any of the four abilities, the first-official-language table says you are not eligible to apply. CLB 7 is 4 points per ability (16 if all four sit at 7). CLB 8 is 5 each. CLB 9 or higher is 6 each. Take a test IRCC lists on [language test results](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/language-test.html).

Proof of funds is another gate. IRCC updated the settlement table on July 7, 2025, using 50% of the low income cut-off. You need [proof of funds](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/proof-funds.html) for FSWP and for the Federal Skilled Trades Program unless you are invited under CEC or you are authorized to work in Canada and have a valid job offer. Keep the figure current in the profile. IRCC asked pool candidates to update no later than July 28, 2025.

| Family members | Funds you need (CAD), updated July 7, 2025 |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | $15,263 |
| 2 | $19,001 |
| 3 | $23,360 |
| 4 | $28,362 |
| 5 | $32,168 |
| 6 | $36,280 |
| 7 | $40,392 |
| Each extra person | $4,112 |

Count yourself, your spouse or common-law partner, and dependent children, even if they are Canadian citizens or not travelling with you. Equity in real property is not proof. You need bank letters on letterhead with the details IRCC lists.

## What occupations are eligible for the Federal skilled worker Program?

**Short answer:** Eligible occupations are skilled jobs in TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 that you actually performed, in the last 10 years, as paid work, for at least 1,560 hours, matching the NOC lead statement and most main duties. There is no extra IRCC annex of named FSWP titles. Quebec-bound applicants use Quebec's programs, not this one. You may count work gained while living in Quebec if you can prove you do not plan to settle there. Provincial nominees must settle in the province that nominated them.

Foreign education needs an [ECA for immigration purposes](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html). The report must be less than 5 years old when you complete the profile and when you apply. In most cases you assess only the highest credential. To claim points for two or more credentials, assess each one. A Canadian degree or diploma does not need an ECA.

Adaptability is a 10-point cap. IRCC lets you combine items such as a spouse or common-law partner at CLB 4 in all 4 abilities (5 points), two academic years of full-time study in Canada (5), or the same study by your spouse (5). Language tests used for those spouse points are valid for 2 years and must be valid on the day you apply for permanent residence. Full-time study means at least 15 hours of classes per week in a program at least 2 years long, in good academic standing.

After 67, you still need a competitive CRS and an invitation. Use the [Express Entry](/immigration/express-entry) hub and our [Federal Skilled Worker program page](/immigration/express-entry/federal-skilled-worker). We are Go Far Global, a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm. If you want the 67-point grid and CRS read on your documents, [book a consultation](/book). Watch draws and [processing times](/immigration/processing-times). Other pathways: [provincial nominee](/immigration/provincial-nominee), [work permit](/immigration/work-permit), [study permit](/immigration/study-permit), [family immigration](/immigration/family-immigration), and [news](/news).

# Hong Kong Pathway Closed Aug 31, 2026: PR Files, OWP, Wait Times

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/hong-kong-pr-pathway-closed-august-31-2026
Category: News
Published: 2026-09-03
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) stopped accepting new applications under the permanent residence pathways for Hong Kong residents on 31 August 2026.

# Hong Kong Pathway Closed Aug 31, 2026: PR Files, OWP, Wait Times

*As of September 3, 2026.*

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) stopped new applications under the Hong Kong pathway to Canadian permanent residence on 31 August 2026. Files accepted on or before that date stay in the queue. The applicant open work permit remains until May 2029. Google's live People Also Ask for this topic is about what the pathway is, whether it is humanitarian and compassionate (H&C), Stream B rules, processing time, and open work permits. Those questions are answered below from IRCC pages, not from rumour.

## TL;DR

New Hong Kong PR applications closed on 31 August 2026 | IRCC still processes files accepted on or before that date | As of 30 June 2026: 30,315 applications (48,560 people), more than 8,600 approvals (13,485 people), about 13,370 already granted PR | IRCC does not publish a dedicated Hong Kong-pathway wait on the program page | Applicant open work permits run to May 2029. The graduate Hong Kong open work permit expired 7 February 2025

## What is Hong Kong PR pathway in Canada?

**Short answer:** It was a temporary public policy, launched in 2021, that let eligible Hong Kong nationals already in Canada apply for permanent residence based on recent Canadian study (Stream A) or Canadian work (Stream B). You had to apply from inside Canada. Quebec was excluded. It was never Express Entry and never an overseas visa. IRCC's [28 August 2026 notice](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/hongkong-permanent-residence-pathways-closing-new-applications.html) confirmed new applications would stop on 31 August 2026. The live hub is now titled Closed. Processing of applications accepted on or before that date continues.

You needed a Hong Kong Special Administrative Region passport, or a United Kingdom British National (Overseas) passport issued to a person born, naturalized or registered in Hong Kong. The official description is on [Permanent residence pathways for Hong Kong residents](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/hong-kong-residents-permanent-residence.html), stamped 1 September 2026.

## Is HK Pathway under H&C?

**Short answer:** IRCC's public program pages call it a temporary public policy, not a classic inland humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) application under section 25. You did not file a separate H&C form to use Stream A or Stream B. IRCC's 2026 deputy minister binder still lists the Hong Kong measure under Humanitarian and Compassionate Programs, with intake running until August 2026 and processing underway. Admissions for many special in-Canada measures draw from the Humanitarian and Compassionate and Other category of the levels plan. That is inventory and planning language. It is not the same as starting a new H&C application today.

The [binder](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/transparency/transition-binders/deputy-minister-2026/humanitarian-compassionate-programs.html) also says processing times for many special-measures in-Canada H&C files are rising because of high demand and low admissions space. That helps explain why Hong Kong pathway files can sit a long time without IRCC posting a single "Hong Kong pathway" clock on the program page.

## How long does it take to process a Hong Kong pathway stream application?

**Short answer:** IRCC does not publish a dedicated Hong Kong-pathway processing time on the closed program pages. Use the [IRCC processing-times tool](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html) and your account messages. The only official volume snapshot in the close notice is dated 30 June 2026: about 30,315 applications (48,560 people) received, more than 8,600 applications (13,485 people) approved, and about 13,370 people already granted permanent residence. That leaves a large remaining inventory. IRCC has not given a month count for those leftover files.

Media have reported waits stretching past 2027 or longer. That is not an IRCC posted time. Treat it as reporting, not a departmental guarantee. What IRCC will say on the [after you apply](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/hong-kong-residents-permanent-residence/after.html) page is the process: completeness check, acknowledgement of receipt (AOR), biometrics, medical exam, then a decision. Incomplete files can be returned. Criminal, security, or family-status issues add time. Update your address. Pay the Right of Permanent Residence Fee (RPRF) when IRCC is ready to confirm status. Check the live amount on the [fee list](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/fees.asp).

## What are the requirements for becoming eligible for the Hong Kong Pathway Stream B?

**Short answer:** Stream B was the Canadian work-experience stream. Before the close, you had to hold a valid HKSAR or BN(O) passport as IRCC defines it, be physically present in Canada when you applied and when you became a permanent resident, hold valid temporary resident status, intend to live outside Quebec, and show Canadian Language Benchmarks (CLB) or Niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens (NCLC) level 5 in all four skills. In the 3 years before applying you needed at least 1,560 hours of paid work in Canada and a Canadian work permit held for at least 1 year. Hours as a full-time student, self-employment, work outside Canada, leave, an extended absence, or unemployment did not count. You could apply under only one stream. These rules are on [who can apply](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/hong-kong-residents-permanent-residence/eligibility.html). They do not reopen intake.

Stream A was the in-Canada graduate stream. Same passport, presence, status, Quebec, and language rules. You had to have graduated from a Canadian [designated learning institution](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/prepare/designated-learning-institutions-list.html) in the 3 years before applying, with at least 50% of the program in Canada, and a diploma of at least 2 years, a degree, or a graduate credential of at least 1 year. A graduate diploma also needed a prior diploma or degree finished in the 5 years before that program started.

| Rule | Stream A (graduates) | Stream B (work) |
|---|---|---|
| Where you applied | Inside Canada | Inside Canada |
| Passport | HKSAR or BN(O) as defined by IRCC | Same |
| Language | CLB / NCLC 5 in all 4 skills | CLB / NCLC 5 in all 4 skills |
| Quebec | Intend to live outside Quebec | Same |
| Core proof | Canadian DLI credential in the last 3 years | 1,560 paid hours in Canada in the last 3 years, and a work permit held at least 1 year |

If you lived in Quebec, you had to prove intent to settle elsewhere. IRCC lists a statutory declaration, job proof, family ties, or a lease on the [documents](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/hong-kong-residents-permanent-residence/documents.html) page.

## Can Hong Kong residents get an open work permit in Canada?

**Short answer:** Not through the old graduate public policy. That open work permit for recent Hong Kong graduates expired on 7 February 2025 and is [closed to new applicants](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/special-instructions/hong-kong-graduates.html). The permit that is still open, until May 2029, is only for people who already applied for permanent residence under one of the two Hong Kong pathways, held a work or study permit within the 3 years before IRCC received that PR file, are in Canada, and are eligible for a work permit. It is valid for up to 3 years. The work permit fee on the official page is CAD $155.

You cannot use that remaining policy if the PR application was refused, withdrawn, or returned. A spouse, common-law partner, or dependent child over 18 can apply for an open work permit with you if they were included on the PR application. Apply in the IRCC secure account. If your status expired less than 90 days ago and you are still in Canada, you may restore status when you apply. Full rules: [open work permit for Hong Kong PR applicants](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/hong-kong-residents-permanent-residence/open-work-permit.html).

Apply before your current permit expires so you keep maintained status, the rule IRCC describes when you [extend your stay](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay.html) in time. IRCC puts a letter in your account for employers. Someone selling a fresh "Hong Kong OWP" as a way to land and then file PR is selling a closed product.

## If you already applied, is your file still being processed?

**Short answer:** Yes, if IRCC accepted the application on or before 31 August 2026. The close stops new intake. It does not cancel complete files already in. The [28 August notice](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/hongkong-permanent-residence-pathways-closing-new-applications.html) says processing of applications received on or before that date continues. Incomplete files can still be returned or refused for missing documents or unpaid fees.

How to apply pages remain online for people who already started a file, including [IMM 5067](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/guide-5067-hong-kong-permanent-residence-pathways.html) and the [how to apply](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/hong-kong-residents-permanent-residence/apply.html) steps. They are not an invitation to start a new PR application.

## What other permanent residence options are left?

**Short answer:** The Hong Kong public policy is closed to new PR applications. Remaining routes are ordinary ones: [Express Entry](/immigration/express-entry) if you meet the Canadian Experience Class or another federal program, a [provincial nominee](/immigration/provincial-nominee) if a province will nominate you, [family sponsorship](/immigration/family-immigration) if a spouse or partner can sponsor, or a regular [work permit](/immigration/work-permit) or [study permit](/immigration/study-permit). None of those is automatic because you held a Hong Kong passport.

Express Entry still uses the Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS). This closed pathway does not add CRS points. If you already work in Canada on a valid permit, keep that permit legal while you build a federal or provincial file. We are Go Far Global, a licensed Canadian immigration firm. If your Hong Kong PR file is in and your permit date is close, or you need a different pathway now that intake has ended, [book a consultation](/book).

# BC PNP 2026: 5,254 Nominations Explained

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/bc-pnp-2026-allocation-cut
Category: News
Published: 2026-08-23
Author: Go Far Global Team

> > This guide is for skilled workers and graduates hoping for a British Columbia nomination in 2026. It explains why the allocation is tighter, who is still eligible, and what to do if you miss out.

# BC PNP 2026: 5,254 Nominations Explained

*As of August 23, 2026.* British Columbia has 5,254 Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) nominations for 2026, well below the 9,000 the province asked for and below the 6,214 it ended 2025 with, even as national PNP numbers rose sharply.

> This guide is for skilled workers and graduates hoping for a British Columbia nomination in 2026. It explains why the allocation is tighter, who is still eligible, and what to do if you miss out.

## TL;DR

British Columbia received 5,254 PNP nominations for 2026 | The province had requested 9,000 | National PNP allocations rose from 55,000 in 2025 to 91,500 in 2026 | About 10,000 of the national total is reserved for physicians and French-speaking newcomers | A tighter provincial share means higher scores and fewer, more targeted draws

## Why was the BC PNP allocation cut for 2026?

The British Columbia allocation is tighter because Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) sets each province's nomination ceiling under the federal [2026-2028 Immigration Levels Plan](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/corporate-initiatives/levels/supplementary-immigration-levels-2026-2028.html), and British Columbia's share came in at 5,254. That figure sits far below the 9,000 the province requested and below the 6,214 nominations it finished 2025 with. National PNP numbers actually grew, from 55,000 in 2025 to 91,500 for 2026, but roughly 10,000 of that total is carved out for physicians and French-speaking candidates, and the rest is split across every province and territory. British Columbia simply did not get the larger share it wanted.

## How many nominations does BC PNP have in 2026?

British Columbia has 5,254 base nominations for 2026 under the [Provincial Nominee Program (PNP)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html). To put that in context, the province ran 2025 with a base of 4,000 that was topped up to 6,214 during the year, so its 2026 starting point is above the old base but below where 2025 finished. The table below shows the 2026 base allocations for the provinces and territories that published figures early in the year. These are nomination ceilings, not admission numbers, and provinces can receive top-ups later.

| Province or territory | 2026 base allocation |
|---|---:|
| Ontario | 14,119 |
| Alberta | 6,403 |
| British Columbia | 5,254 |
| Saskatchewan | 4,761 |
| Yukon | 282 |

## Who is still eligible for BC PNP in 2026?

British Columbia still runs the same core pathways under BC PNP Skills Immigration, so most skilled workers and graduates remain eligible on paper. The main streams cover skilled workers with a British Columbia job offer, health authority workers, entry-level and semi-skilled workers in specific sectors, and international graduates and post-graduates from Canadian institutions. There is also an Entrepreneur Immigration stream for people starting or buying a business. A smaller allocation does not change who can enter the pool, but it does mean the province leans harder on targeted draws for priority sectors such as health care, child care, construction, and technology, rather than large general draws.

## How does the cut change your odds of a nomination?

A smaller allocation usually pushes selection scores up and narrows who gets invited. When British Columbia has fewer nominations to give, it tends to hold more frequent but smaller targeted draws aimed at specific occupations, and general draws become less generous. That rewards candidates with a strong British Columbia job offer, in-demand occupations, higher wages, and stronger language scores, and it squeezes out borderline profiles that might have cleared a larger draw. If you are relying on British Columbia alone, treat a nomination as competitive rather than likely, and strengthen the factors you control, starting with your job offer and your Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) inputs like language and work experience.

## What are your options if you miss BC PNP in 2026?

If a British Columbia nomination looks out of reach, you still have several federal and provincial routes. Express Entry runs its own draws for the Canadian Experience Class and category-based selection, and a strong CRS score can land you permanent residence without any provincial nomination. Other provinces run their own PNP streams with different occupation lists, so a candidate shut out in British Columbia may qualify in Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, or the Atlantic provinces. Canadian work experience also raises your CRS over time, so another year on a valid work permit can move you into range. A Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) can map which of these fits your occupation and score.

## Frequently asked questions

### Will there be a BC PNP draw in 2026?

Yes. British Columbia continues to run BC PNP draws in 2026, but with a smaller allocation the province favours targeted draws for priority occupations over large general rounds. Expect regular but smaller invitations focused on health care, construction, child care, and technology roles tied to a British Columbia job offer.

### What is the PNP allocation for 2026?

Nationally, IRCC set the 2026 PNP allocation at 91,500 nominations, up from 55,000 in 2025, with about 10,000 reserved for physicians and French-speaking newcomers. British Columbia's share of that total is 5,254 base nominations.

### What are the BC PNP occupations in demand for 2026?

British Columbia prioritizes occupations tied to its labour shortages, which continue to centre on health care, construction and skilled trades, early childhood education and child care, and technology. The province runs targeted draws for these groups, and a job offer in one of them is the strongest single factor for a nomination.

### Which province is easiest to get PR in 2026?

There is no universally easy province, because each one selects for its own labour needs and job offers. A tighter British Columbia allocation can make provinces with larger 2026 allocations, such as Ontario and Alberta, relatively more open for some occupations, but the right province depends on your specific job offer, occupation, and score rather than headline allocation size.

- [Provincial Nominee Program: About the process](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html), IRCC
