# PEI PNP Draw 2026: How the Expression of Interest System Works

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/pei-pnp-draw-2026
Category: Provincial Nominee Program
Published: 2026-07-23
Author: Go Far Global Team

> A plain-English guide to the PEI PNP draw: how Prince Edward Island scores Expression of Interest profiles, which categories get invited, when draws happen, and how to get an invitation to apply.

*As of July 23, 2026.*

If you are watching the "PEI PNP draw" to plan your move to Canada, this guide explains how Prince Edward Island actually selects candidates, what the numbers mean, and how to put yourself in the strongest position. Go Far Global is a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm in Toronto, and we walk clients through provincial draws every week.

## What is a PEI PNP draw and how does it work?

**Short answer:** A Prince Edward Island Provincial Nominee Program (PEI PNP) draw is a periodic selection round where the province's Office of Immigration invites the highest-scoring candidates from its Expression of Interest (EOI) pool to apply for a provincial nomination. You first submit an EOI profile, the province scores it, and at each draw it sends invitations to the top-ranked profiles. A draw is not the application itself. It is the gate you clear before you can file a full nomination application. The [Provincial Nominee Program (PNP)](/immigration/provincial-nominee) lets provinces nominate workers they want, one of the [provincial routes recognized by the Government of Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html), and PEI runs its share through this EOI draw model.

## How does Prince Edward Island rank and score Expression of Interest candidates?

**Short answer:** PEI scores each EOI profile on a points grid worth up to 100 points, then ranks the pool from highest to lowest and invites from the top down. The grid rewards factors that predict success in the province: age, education, official-language ability in English or French, skilled work experience, a valid PEI job offer or employer connection, and adaptability factors such as prior study or work on the Island. Unlike the federal Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS), your exact EOI score is not shown to you, and the province does not publish the minimum in advance. That is why two candidates with similar resumes can see different outcomes from one round to the next.

| EOI scoring factor | Why PEI counts it |
|---|---|
| Age | Rewards candidates in their prime working years |
| Education | Higher credentials earn more points |
| Language ability | English or French test scores across reading, writing, speaking, and listening |
| Skilled work experience | Relevant occupational experience, often tied to a PEI role |
| PEI job offer or employer connection | A genuine full-time offer strengthens most Labour Impact profiles |
| Adaptability and PEI ties | Prior study, work, or close family on the Island |

## Which PEI PNP categories get invited in a draw?

**Short answer:** PEI draws invite candidates across three broad categories: Express Entry, Labour Impact, and Business Impact. Express Entry candidates already hold a federal Express Entry profile and qualify for a program like the Federal Skilled Worker or Canadian Experience Class. Labour Impact targets skilled, critical, and intermediate-experience workers with a PEI employer. Business Impact, the Work Permit stream, targets entrepreneurs who will own and operate a PEI business. Most monthly rounds focus on the labour and Express Entry pools, while business candidates are invited on a separate cadence. Knowing which category you fit shapes your documents, your timeline, and your realistic odds.

| PEI PNP category | Who it targets | Route to permanent residence |
|---|---|---|
| Express Entry | Candidates with an eligible federal Express Entry profile | Nomination adds 600 CRS points to the federal profile |
| Labour Impact | Skilled, critical, and intermediate workers with a PEI employer | Paper-based, non-Express Entry application |
| Business Impact (Work Permit) | Entrepreneurs who will own and run a PEI business | Work permit, then nomination, then permanent residence |

## How often does PEI hold PNP draws, and when is the next one?

**Short answer:** PEI typically holds one draw per month, usually in the middle of the month, and posts each round on the Office of Immigration website. For 2026 the province set out a monthly calendar; as reported for recent months, rounds fell on the third Thursday, with upcoming dates listed for August 20, September 17, October 15, November 19, and December 17, 2026. Treat any specific future date as provisional until you confirm it on the province's official [Expression of Interest Draws page](https://www.princeedwardisland.ca/en/information/office-of-immigration/expression-of-interest-draws), because the Office of Immigration can add, move, or cancel a round. Do not build a filing plan around a single expected date.

## What score do you need to get invited in a PEI PNP draw?

**Short answer:** There is no fixed, published cut-off for a PEI PNP draw. Because the province ranks the live EOI pool and invites from the top, the effective minimum shifts with every round based on who is in the pool and how many invitations go out. As reported for the July 16, 2026 round, PEI issued invitations to 195 candidates across its Express Entry and Labour Impact categories, but the province did not release a single threshold number. For authoritative figures on any given round, check the official [Expression of Interest Draws page](https://www.princeedwardisland.ca/en/information/office-of-immigration/expression-of-interest-draws) rather than third-party trackers, which sometimes disagree on counts. Focus on maximizing your points, not on guessing the line.

## What happens after you receive a PEI PNP invitation to apply?

**Short answer:** An invitation to apply (ITA) from a PEI draw lets you submit a full provincial nomination application, not a permanent residence (PR) application. You upload documents, prove your points, and if PEI approves, you receive a provincial nomination. From there the path splits. If you were invited through the Express Entry category, your nomination adds 600 CRS points to your federal profile, which effectively guarantees a federal invitation for PR. If you were nominated outside Express Entry, you apply to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) through the [paper-based, non-Express Entry process](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html). Either way, the nomination is the province's endorsement, and IRCC makes the final PR decision.

## Who is eligible for PNP in PEI?

**Short answer:** You are generally eligible if you are of working age, genuinely intend to live in PEI, and fit one of the program categories. For Labour Impact you usually need a full-time job offer from a PEI employer plus relevant work experience and language ability. For the Express Entry category you must already hold an eligible federal Express Entry profile. For Business Impact you need business ownership or management experience, a minimum net worth, and a plan to actively run a PEI business. PEI also weighs your education, settlement funds, and connection to the Island. Meeting the minimums lets you submit an EOI through the [province's Expression of Interest System](https://eoi.princeedwardisland.ca/ieoi/login); it does not guarantee an invitation, because draws still rank the whole pool.

## Will there be a PNP draw today?

**Short answer:** Probably not on any random day, because PEI holds only about one draw per month, not daily. The Office of Immigration schedules rounds roughly mid-month, so most calendar days have no PEI draw at all. The only reliable way to know is the province's official Expression of Interest Draws page, which posts each round after it happens. Third-party "draw today" alerts are guesses. If you are in the pool, you do not need to refresh a tracker, because PEI notifies invited candidates through their EOI account and email. Keep your profile accurate and your documents ready so that whenever the next round lands, you can act quickly instead of scrambling.

## How long does it take to get a PNP nomination for PEI?

**Short answer:** Plan for several months from invitation to nomination, though timelines vary by category and file complexity. After a draw, you submit your full nomination application, and the province reviews your documents, employer details, and points before issuing a decision. Straightforward Labour Impact files with a clean job offer often move faster than business files that require a settlement plan and a site visit. The part you control is your own readiness: candidates who already hold police certificates, language results, reference letters, and proof of funds shave weeks off the process. Once PEI issues the nomination, a separate federal stage with IRCC begins for permanent residence.

## Is it easier to get PR in Prince Edward Island?

**Short answer:** In some ways yes, because PEI's EOI grid can reward candidates who would score lower under the federal Express Entry CRS, especially those with a local job offer or a genuine tie to the Island. A provincial nomination is powerful: through the Express Entry route it adds 600 CRS points, which almost always secures a federal PR invitation. That said, "easier" is relative. PEI expects a real intention to settle and work on the Island, and it invites from the top of its pool, so weaker profiles can wait through many rounds. It is a strong path for the right candidate, not a shortcut for everyone.

## Is it easy to get PR in PEI?

**Short answer:** No, not automatically, but it is achievable with the right profile and preparation. PEI receives more interest than it can nominate, so submitting an EOI is only the first step, and many profiles sit in the pool without an invitation. Candidates who do well usually have a valid PEI job offer, solid language scores, and a credible plan to live in the province long term. The business route adds capital, net-worth, and active-management requirements. Because the province does not publish a cut-off, you cannot self-verify that you will be invited; you can only maximize your points and keep your profile current. A licensed RCIC helps you target the category where you are most competitive.

## How long does PEI PNP processing take?

**Short answer:** Budget roughly a year or more end to end, split across two stages. The provincial nomination stage typically takes a few months from application to decision, depending on category and completeness. The federal permanent residence stage is separate: as third-party trackers note, IRCC can take on the order of 12 to 15 months to finalize a paper-based provincial nominee application, while Express Entry-aligned nominations are often faster. Processing times change constantly, so confirm current federal estimates on the IRCC website and current provincial expectations on the PEI Office of Immigration site. The biggest controllable delay is incomplete documentation, so assemble your civil, police, medical, and financial documents early.

## What was the last PNP draw?

**Short answer:** For PEI specifically, the recent mid-2026 rounds followed the province's usual monthly pattern; as reported, PEI held a round on July 16, 2026 that issued 195 invitations across the Express Entry and Labour Impact categories. Because "last draw" changes every month and different trackers report slightly different figures, treat any single number as provisional and confirm it on the province's official Expression of Interest Draws page, which is the authoritative record. Other provinces run their own PNP draws on separate schedules, so a "last PNP draw" headline may refer to Ontario, British Columbia, or another province rather than PEI. Always check which province and which category a reported draw belongs to.

## Is 450 points enough for Canada PR?

**Short answer:** It depends on the system you mean. In the federal Express Entry pool, a CRS score of 450 is competitive in some category-based rounds but often below the cut-off in general rounds, which have frequently required higher scores. PEI's EOI grid is different: it tops out at 100 points and is not the same as CRS, so a "450" does not exist in the provincial system. The connection matters because a PEI Express Entry nomination adds 600 CRS points, which lifts almost any profile well past federal cut-offs. If your CRS sits around 450 and you are stuck, a provincial nomination can be the difference maker. Use our [CRS calculator](/tools/crs-calculator) to see where you stand.

## How can Go Far Global help you get invited in a PEI PNP draw?

**Short answer:** We assess your profile against every PEI category, tell you honestly where you are competitive, and build the file that maximizes your EOI points before you enter the pool. As a licensed RCIC firm, Go Far Global handles your Expression of Interest, your nomination application, and the federal PR stage, and we keep your profile current so you are ready the moment a round lands. If PEI is not your strongest route, we will say so and map a better one. [Book a consultation](/book) and we will turn "watching the draws" into a concrete plan, and follow our [latest immigration news](/news) for draw updates.

## Sources

- Government of Canada, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, "Immigrate as a provincial nominee": https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html
- Province of Prince Edward Island, Office of Immigration, "Expression of Interest Draws": https://www.princeedwardisland.ca/en/information/office-of-immigration/expression-of-interest-draws
- Province of Prince Edward Island, Office of Immigration, "Prince Edward Island Expression of Interest System" (login): https://eoi.princeedwardisland.ca/ieoi/login

# New Brunswick PNP Draw 2026: How the NBPNP Selection Rounds Work

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/new-brunswick-pnp-draw-2026
Category: Provincial Nominee Program
Published: 2026-07-23
Author: Go Far Global Team

> A plain-English guide to how New Brunswick PNP draws work in 2026, including the NBPNP streams, the Expression of Interest pool, recent draw results, and where to verify every official figure.

*As of July 23, 2026.*

If you are watching for the next New Brunswick Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) draw, this guide from Go Far Global, a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm in Toronto, explains how the province's selection rounds actually work, which streams get invited, and where to confirm every official figure.

## What is a New Brunswick PNP draw?

**Short answer:** A New Brunswick PNP draw is a selection round in which Immigration New Brunswick (ImmigrationNB) invites candidates from its pool to apply for a provincial nomination toward permanent residence. New Brunswick runs the New Brunswick Provincial Nominee Program (NBPNP) in partnership with the federal government. Candidates submit an Expression of Interest (EOI), and the province periodically reviews the pool and issues an Invitation to Apply (ITA) to those who match its current labour market and demographic priorities. A nomination alone does not grant permanent residence. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) makes the final decision on the permanent residence application, as the [Government of Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html) confirms.

## How does New Brunswick choose who to invite?

**Short answer:** New Brunswick invites candidates based on provincial priorities, targeted occupations, and its remaining nomination allocation, not a single published cut-off score. Per the [Government of New Brunswick invitation page](https://www2.gnb.ca/content/gnb/en/corporate/promo/immigration/immigrating-to-nb/invitations-to-apply.html), ImmigrationNB reviews the EOIs in the pool and may issue an invitation, and meeting the basic eligibility criteria does not guarantee one. Each round targets specific pathways and sectors, such as healthcare, education, construction, information technology, and transportation. Because the province selects against changing needs, the profile it invites can shift from one round to the next. Candidates already sitting in the federal Express Entry pool can also receive a New Brunswick letter of interest that leads to a nomination.

## Which streams get invited in a New Brunswick PNP draw?

**Short answer:** New Brunswick draws invite candidates mainly through the NB Skilled Worker stream, the NB Express Entry stream, and the NB Strategic Initiative, with a Business Immigration stream and two pilots rounding out the program. Most economic rounds pull from the Skilled Worker and Express Entry streams, while Strategic Initiative rounds frequently target French-speaking (Francophone) candidates. The province also selects applications through the separate Atlantic Immigration Program (AIP), which is employer-driven and sits outside the NBPNP pool. Each stream carries its own eligibility rules, so the stream you qualify for decides which draws you can appear in. Most pathways require a genuine New Brunswick tie, such as a job offer, local work experience, or study in the province.

| NBPNP stream | Who it targets | Typical requirement |
|---|---|---|
| NB Skilled Worker | Workers with NB experience, NB graduates, priority-occupation hires | A qualifying NB job offer or current NB employment |
| NB Express Entry | Skilled workers in the federal Express Entry pool | A valid IRCC Express Entry profile plus a New Brunswick connection |
| NB Strategic Initiative | French-speaking skilled workers and priority candidates | A Francophone profile aligned to provincial priorities |
| NB Business Immigration | Entrepreneurs and investors | A business plan, relevant experience, and settlement funds |

The [Government of New Brunswick streams page](https://www2.gnb.ca/content/gnb/en/corporate/promo/immigration/immigrating-to-nb/nb-immigration-program-streams.html) lists each pathway in full. To compare options across the country, see our [Provincial Nominee Program](/immigration/provincial-nominee) overview.

## What were the recent 2026 New Brunswick PNP draw results?

**Short answer:** New Brunswick held frequent selection rounds through 2026, often clustering several draws across different streams within a few days. In the first rounds of the year, held January 13 to 15, 2026, the province issued 379 invitations across its programs, and between March 3 and 6, 2026 it issued 622, per its published archive. The most recent rounds posted at the time of writing were a cluster held June 2 to 4, 2026. Totals and dates change with every round, so always confirm the live numbers on the province's own selection rounds page rather than relying on any third party.

Selected verified rounds, per the [Government of New Brunswick 2026 draw archive](https://www2.gnb.ca/content/gnb/en/corporate/promo/immigration/immigrating-to-nb/invitations-to-apply/previous-invitations-2026.html):

| Round period (2026) | Programs | Invitations |
|---|---|---|
| January 13 to 15 | NBPNP and AIP | 379 |
| March 3 to 6 | NBPNP and AIP | 622 |

These are only two of many rounds the province ran in 2026. For the full list and authoritative, up to date totals, check the province's [invitation and selection rounds](https://www2.gnb.ca/content/gnb/en/corporate/promo/immigration/immigrating-to-nb/invitations-to-apply.html) page, which New Brunswick updates after each round.

## How do you enter the New Brunswick PNP pool?

**Short answer:** You enter by submitting an Expression of Interest through Immigration New Brunswick's online portal, after which your profile joins the candidate pool and stays valid for 365 days. There is no fee to sit in the pool, and an EOI is not an application for nomination on its own. The province draws from this pool when it holds a selection round, so a complete, accurate EOI that reflects a real New Brunswick connection gives you the best chance of an invitation. If the province invites you, you then submit a full nomination application within the deadline stated in your ITA. A nominee who applies through Express Entry earns 600 additional points, which the [Government of Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees/express-entry.html) confirms effectively secures a federal invitation.

## What is the PNP score for New Brunswick?

**Short answer:** New Brunswick does not publish a single public cut-off score for its provincial draws the way a Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) number works in federal Express Entry. Instead, ImmigrationNB selects candidates from its Expression of Interest pool based on provincial labour market priorities, targeted occupations, and its remaining nomination allocation. Meeting a stream's eligibility does not guarantee an invitation. If you apply through the NB Express Entry stream, your federal CRS score is what matters in the IRCC pool, and a New Brunswick nomination adds 600 points, which effectively guarantees a federal invitation to apply. Some streams have historically weighed internal factors such as age, language, education, and work experience, but the province does not release a live draw cut-off. For authoritative selection details, always check the province's official invitation and selection rounds page before assuming any number.

## When was the last PNP draw in New Brunswick?

**Short answer:** New Brunswick does not follow a fixed calendar, and it often holds several rounds close together across different streams, including Skilled Worker, Express Entry, Strategic Initiative, and the separate Atlantic Immigration Program. At the time of writing, the most recent rounds posted on the province's official archive were a cluster held between June 2 and June 4, 2026. Because dates and totals change constantly, the only reliable source for the true last draw is the Government of New Brunswick invitation and selection rounds page, which the province updates after each round. We link it in the Sources section below so you can confirm the current figure yourself.

## Will there be a PNP draw today?

**Short answer:** There is no guaranteed daily New Brunswick PNP draw, and the province does not announce rounds on a fixed public schedule. New Brunswick holds selection rounds periodically through the year, sometimes clustering several draws within a few days and sometimes leaving weeks between them, based on its allocation and labour market needs. That means today may or may not bring a draw, and no third-party tracker can promise one. The most dependable approach is to keep a valid Expression of Interest in the pool so you are eligible whenever the next round runs, and to watch the Government of New Brunswick invitation and selection rounds page, which is updated after each round. You can also follow our [news](/news) page, where we summarize new rounds as the province publishes them.

## What is the NB PNP 2026?

**Short answer:** The NB PNP in 2026 is the New Brunswick Provincial Nominee Program (NBPNP) as it operates this year: an economic immigration program that lets the province nominate skilled workers, graduates, and entrepreneurs for Canadian permanent residence based on its own labour market needs. In 2026 the program runs through the Skilled Worker, Express Entry, Strategic Initiative, and Business Immigration streams, plus the Critical Worker and Private Career College Graduate pilots. Candidates submit an Expression of Interest, and ImmigrationNB invites from the pool in periodic draws that have targeted sectors such as healthcare, construction, education, and information technology. Per the province's published 2026 archive, New Brunswick ran numerous rounds across the NBPNP and Atlantic Immigration Program through the year; check the official selection rounds page for the current invitation totals. Final permanent residence decisions still rest with IRCC, not the province.

## Who is eligible for NB PNP?

**Short answer:** Eligibility depends on the stream, but most New Brunswick pathways require a real connection to the province plus qualifying skilled work. Common routes include a full-time, non-seasonal job offer from an eligible New Brunswick employer, at least six months to twelve months of recent skilled work in the province, or graduation from a designated New Brunswick learning institution. The Express Entry stream additionally requires a valid federal Express Entry profile and skilled experience in a National Occupational Classification (NOC) Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities (TEER) 0, 1, 2, or 3 occupation. Business applicants need funds, relevant experience, and a viable business plan. Language ability, education, and settlement funds also factor in across streams. Because each stream sets its own bar, confirm your exact pathway against the official stream pages or with a licensed consultant before you submit an EOI.

## Is New Brunswick easy to get PR?

**Short answer:** New Brunswick is often one of the more accessible provinces for permanent residence if you already have a genuine tie there, such as a New Brunswick job offer, local work experience, or a credential from a New Brunswick school, but easy overstates it. The province invites selectively against its priorities, and a nomination is only the first step. You still need IRCC to approve the permanent residence application, which requires meeting federal admissibility, medical, and background rules. Candidates without any New Brunswick connection face far longer odds, because most streams are built around employment or study in the province. The realistic path is to build a legitimate connection, keep a strong Expression of Interest in the pool, and apply through the stream that fits your profile. A licensed RCIC can tell you honestly whether New Brunswick is a viable route for you.

# Ontario PNP Draw 2026: OINP Rounds, Streams, and How to Get Invited

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/ontario-pnp-draw-2026
Category: Provincial Nominee Program
Published: 2026-07-23
Author: Go Far Global Team

> A licensed RCIC firm explains how Ontario PNP draws work in 2026, what the OINP overhaul changed, the new Workforce Priority Stream, fees, and where to track official results.

*As of July 23, 2026.*

If you are watching for the next Ontario Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) draw, this guide explains how Ontario selects candidates, what the 2026 overhaul changed, and where the official numbers live. Go Far Global is a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm in Toronto, and we track every Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program (OINP) round as the province publishes it.

## What is an Ontario PNP draw?

**Short answer:** An Ontario PNP draw is a selection round in which the OINP invites the highest ranked candidates from its pool to apply for a provincial nomination. Ontario runs the OINP as its economic immigration program alongside Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC). The province nominates people whose skills the Ontario economy needs, and the Government of Canada makes the final decision on permanent residence. A draw does not grant status. It issues an invitation to apply (ITA), which is your chance to submit a full application that Ontario then assesses before deciding whether to nominate you.

## How does an Ontario PNP draw actually work?

**Short answer:** You register an Expression of Interest (EOI), the OINP scores and ranks every profile in a stream, and each draw invites the top ranked candidates above a cut off that Ontario sets for that round. Your EOI stays active for 12 months, then it is removed automatically. Draws are often targeted, meaning Ontario selects for a specific region, occupation group, or language. Receiving an invitation does not mean you are nominated. Once invited, the timelines are tight. Ontario sets a deadline in the invitation itself, and both the employer and the applicant generally need to complete their parts within the window Ontario specifies, so check the exact dates on your invitation rather than assuming a fixed number of days. You can review the mechanics on Ontario's official [invitations to apply page](https://www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-immigrant-nominee-program-oinp-invitations-apply).

## What changed in the OINP 2026 overhaul?

**Short answer:** Ontario closed its legacy streams and rebuilt the program. Regulatory changes came into force on June 25, 2026 as the first of a two phase redesign, and the province launched the new Ontario Workforce Priority Stream. Eight former streams closed, including Employer Job Offer: Foreign Worker, Employer Job Offer: International Student, Employer Job Offer: In-Demand Skills, Masters Graduate, PhD Graduate, and the three Express Entry aligned streams (Human Capital Priorities, French-Speaking Skilled Worker, and Skilled Trades). The province has said more changes are still coming. If you held an active EOI in a now closed stream, the old ranking no longer applies, so read the [2026 OINP updates](https://www.ontario.ca/page/2026-ontario-immigrant-nominee-program-updates) and reassess under the new framework.

## Which OINP streams issue invitations in 2026?

**Short answer:** As of July 2026, the Ontario Workforce Priority Stream is the active pathway, and it splits into three routes based on your occupation skill level and profession. Ontario classifies jobs by Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities (TEER) category, and each route sets its own job offer, language, and education requirements. Ontario invites candidates from these pools through targeted draws published on its official [OINP page](https://www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-immigrant-nominee-program-oinp). The table below summarizes the three pathways and their core requirements as the province describes them.

| Pathway | Who it targets | Core requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TEER 0 to 3 | Skilled workers in TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 occupations with a full-time, permanent Ontario job offer | Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB) 6 (CLB 5 for certain occupations), post-secondary education, qualifying work experience |
| TEER 4 to 5 | Workers in TEER 4 or 5 occupations with a full-time, permanent Ontario job offer | CLB 4, secondary school credentials |
| Self-Employed Physicians | Physicians practising or planning to practise in Ontario | Member in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario, eligible registration |

## How does an Ontario nomination boost your Express Entry score?

**Short answer:** A provincial nomination adds 600 points to your Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score in federal Express Entry, which effectively guarantees an invitation to apply for permanent residence in a later federal round. The PNP has two routes, an Express Entry linked route and a non Express Entry (paper based) route. If a province nominates you through the Express Entry route, you confirm the nomination in your profile and receive the 600 point boost, then you have 60 calendar days to apply for permanent residence once IRCC invites you. Ontario's current Workforce Priority Stream is a direct application to the province rather than an Express Entry stream, so confirm which route applies before you plan around CRS points. Estimate your baseline with our [CRS calculator](/tools/crs-calculator).

## How much does an OINP application cost?

**Short answer:** Ontario charges a tiered application fee for the Workforce Priority Stream based on where the job or practice sits. It costs $1,500 if the job offer is outside the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) and $2,000 if the job offer is within the GTA, which Ontario defines as the City of Toronto plus the Durham, Halton, Peel, and York regions. Self-employed physicians pay the same tiers based on their Ontario medical practice address. These provincial fees are separate from the federal permanent residence fees you pay IRCC later. You can confirm current amounts on Ontario's [application process page](https://www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-immigrant-nominee-program-oinp-application-process).

| Application type | Location of job or practice | OINP fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ontario Workforce Priority Stream | Outside the GTA | $1,500 |
| Ontario Workforce Priority Stream | Within the GTA | $2,000 |
| Self-Employed Physicians | Outside the GTA | $1,500 |
| Self-Employed Physicians | Within the GTA | $2,000 |

## Where can you track the latest Ontario PNP draw results?

**Short answer:** The authoritative record is the province's own invitations to apply page, which lists every OINP round with its date, stream, number of invitations, and score range. Treat any third party "latest draw" number as unofficial until you confirm it there. For context, the province ran a series of targeted rounds through spring 2026 before the redesign, and those rounds appear in the official invitations to apply archive under streams that have since closed. Because the program is mid redesign, dates and cut offs shift, so verify current figures on the official page rather than relying on a static blog. We also post plain language recaps on our [news feed](/news).

## When would the next OINP draw be?

**Short answer:** Ontario does not publish a fixed draw calendar, so no one can name the exact date of the next OINP round in advance. The province holds draws periodically and announces each one on its official invitations to apply page after it happens. During 2026, the OINP paused parts of its system to implement the two phase redesign, which changed the rhythm of draws compared with prior years. The practical move is to keep a valid Expression of Interest on file, make sure your profile reflects your strongest score, and monitor the official page plus our news feed. Anyone promising you a guaranteed date for the next draw is guessing. Register early so you are already in the pool whenever the next targeted round runs.

## Will there be an OINP draw in 2026?

**Short answer:** Yes. Ontario ran multiple targeted OINP draws through the first half of 2026 and kept the program operating while rolling out its redesign. The legacy streams issued invitations into spring 2026, and the new Ontario Workforce Priority Stream launched after regulatory changes came into force on June 25, 2026. So 2026 has already seen draws, and more rounds are expected under the redesigned framework as the province works through the second phase of changes. Exact timing is not scheduled in advance, and the province has cautioned that criteria and intake are still evolving. Check the official invitations to apply page for the current position, and confirm your eligibility under the new streams rather than the closed ones.

## What is the PNP score for Ontario?

**Short answer:** There is no single fixed pass score for the OINP. Each stream ranks its own pool, and Ontario sets a cut off for every individual draw, so the required score changes from round to round and from stream to stream. Under the redesigned Ontario Workforce Priority Stream, the province ranks Expression of Interest profiles using a points system that weighs factors such as job offer characteristics, language ability, education, and Ontario labour market needs. That is separate from the federal Comprehensive Ranking System used in Express Entry. Because cut offs are set per draw, the only reliable figure is the one Ontario publishes for each round on its invitations to apply page. Build the strongest profile you can rather than aiming at a moving number.

## Will there be a PNP draw today?

**Short answer:** Almost certainly not on any specific day you happen to check, because Ontario does not run daily draws. OINP rounds happen periodically, not on a set schedule, and the province posts results after each one. If you see a claim that a draw is happening today, verify it against the official invitations to apply page before you act on it, since unofficial trackers often repost old rounds. Across Canada, different provinces draw on their own timelines, so a PNP draw somewhere in the country on a given day does not mean Ontario drew. The reliable habit is to keep your Expression of Interest current and check the province's official page directly rather than relying on same day rumors or social media posts.

## What is the OINP PNP quota for 2026?

**Short answer:** Ontario's annual nomination quota is set by the federal government, not by the province alone. Each year, IRCC allocates a fixed number of provincial nominations to each province and territory, and Ontario draws within that ceiling. Ontario has historically received one of the largest allocations in the country because of its economy and population. IRCC and the province publish the current year's allocation, so treat any figure you see on social media as unofficial until you confirm it through those channels. The allocation matters because it caps how many nominations Ontario can issue in a year, which shapes how selective draws become. For the confirmed 2026 number, rely on the official IRCC and Ontario publications rather than third party posts.

## What is a good CRS score for OINP?

**Short answer:** The Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) is a federal Express Entry tool, not an OINP score, so a good CRS for OINP only mattered for Ontario's former Express Entry linked streams, which closed in the 2026 redesign. When those streams operated, Ontario searched the Express Entry pool for candidates with competitive scores, and its Human Capital Priorities stream historically looked at candidates at or above roughly 400 CRS, with actual targets varying by draw. Today the active Workforce Priority Stream is a direct provincial application that uses its own points system, not CRS. CRS still matters for the payoff, because a provincial nomination adds 600 CRS points in Express Entry. Estimate your CRS with our [calculator](/tools/crs-calculator), then talk to an RCIC about the best route for you.

## Is Ontario shutting down PNP?

**Short answer:** No. Ontario is not shutting down the OINP. It closed its legacy streams and rebuilt the program, which is different from ending it. Regulatory changes came into force on June 25, 2026 as the first of a two phase redesign, and the province immediately launched the new Ontario Workforce Priority Stream to replace the closed pathways. The program continues to nominate candidates for permanent residence in partnership with IRCC. What changed is the structure, the eligibility criteria, and the scoring, not the existence of provincial nomination in Ontario. If your plan relied on a stream that closed, you have not lost the OINP as an option. You need a fresh eligibility check against the new streams, which is exactly the kind of review an RCIC can run for you.

Ready to find out which OINP pathway fits you under the 2026 rules? [Book a consultation with a Go Far Global RCIC](/book), and we will map your options, check your eligibility, and build a plan around the current draws. You can also read our latest [provincial nominee guidance](/immigration/provincial-nominee).

# Alberta PNP Draw 2026: How AAIP Draws and Nominations Work

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/alberta-pnp-draw-2026
Category: Provincial Nominee Program
Published: 2026-07-23
Author: Go Far Global Team

> The Alberta PNP draw is a selection round run by the Alberta Advantage Immigration Program (AAIP). This 2026 guide explains how Alberta ranks candidates, which streams hold draws, the minimum CRS score of 300 for the Express Entry Stream, and how a nomination adds 600 CRS points toward permanent residence.

*As of August 18, 2026.*

> **August 2026 update:** Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) gave the Alberta Advantage Immigration Program (AAIP) an additional 200 nominations on August 10, 2026, raising Alberta's total 2026 allocation to 6,603. On August 12, 2026 the province expanded its guidance on the economic establishment requirement for the Rural Entrepreneur Stream, Graduate Entrepreneur Stream and Foreign Graduate Entrepreneur Stream. Eligibility criteria did not change. Alberta also launched an Eligibility Explorer tool on June 17, 2026 that lets you check which streams fit your situation before you create an Expression of Interest profile.

If you are tracking the "Alberta PNP draw," you are watching the selection rounds run by the Alberta Advantage Immigration Program (AAIP), the province's arm of Canada's Provincial Nominee Program (PNP). Go Far Global is a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm in Toronto, and this guide explains how those draws actually work, how the province ranks candidates, and how a nomination changes your odds of permanent residence. We focus on the evergreen mechanics so the page stays useful between rounds. For any specific draw figure, we point you to Alberta's own records.

## What is the Alberta PNP draw, and how does the AAIP choose candidates?

**Short answer:** An Alberta PNP draw is a selection round in which the Alberta Advantage Immigration Program (AAIP) invites candidates from its Expression of Interest (EOI) pools to apply for a provincial nomination. Alberta does not run draws on a fixed calendar. The province holds them as needed to meet labour shortages and provincial priorities, which is why timing varies from month to month. Your EOI score matters, but it is not the only factor. The AAIP also weighs occupation, sector, work location, and your connection to Alberta when it decides whom to invite in a given round. For the program overview, see the [Government of Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html) and the [Government of Alberta](https://www.alberta.ca/alberta-advantage-immigration-program).

## Which AAIP streams and pathways hold draws?

**Short answer:** Alberta draws from several worker streams, and each targets a different type of candidate. The largest is the Alberta Opportunity Stream, for people already working in Alberta on an eligible work permit. The Alberta Express Entry Stream selects candidates from the federal Express Entry pool and runs dedicated pathways for health care, technology, and law enforcement. Alberta also draws from the Rural Renewal Stream and the Tourism and Hospitality Stream. Because each stream has its own rules and its own pool, cut-off scores and invitation counts differ sharply between them, even in the same week. The table below shows the main worker streams and who they target.

| Stream or pathway | Who it targets | Express Entry profile needed? |
|---|---|---|
| Alberta Opportunity Stream | Workers already in Alberta on an eligible work permit | No |
| Alberta Express Entry Stream | Federal Express Entry candidates with Alberta ties or priority occupations | Yes |
| Accelerated Tech Pathway | Tech workers with an eligible Alberta job offer | Yes |
| Dedicated Health Care Pathway | Licensed health professionals with an Alberta job offer | Sometimes |
| Rural Renewal Stream | Candidates endorsed by a designated rural Alberta community | No |

For the full, current stream list and eligibility, see the province's application streams page at the [Government of Alberta](https://www.alberta.ca/aaip-application-streams).

## How does Alberta rank and score candidates in a draw?

**Short answer:** For the Alberta Express Entry Stream, you must have an active federal Express Entry profile, qualify under a federal program, and hold a minimum Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score of 300 to be eligible. Beyond that federal floor, Alberta assesses candidates through its Expression of Interest system and ranks them on factors tied to provincial priorities, then invites the profiles that best fit the target of a given draw. The province is explicit that the EOI score alone does not decide selection. Occupation, sector demand, an Alberta job offer, existing work in the province, and family ties all shape who gets invited, so two people with the same score can see different outcomes. Full criteria live with the [Government of Alberta](https://www.alberta.ca/aaip-alberta-express-entry-stream-eligibility).

## What were the most recent Alberta PNP draw results?

**Short answer:** Alberta publishes every draw on its official processing information page, which is the only authoritative record of dates, cut-off scores, and invitation counts. Across 2026, minimum scores have ranged roughly from 45 to 73, and invitations per draw have ranged from fewer than 10 to nearly 1,000, per that page. We do not restate a single "latest" number here, because it changes with every round and third-party trackers often lag or differ. The pool sizes below, reported on the same official page, show how competition varies by stream. Treat them as a snapshot, since the province updates them as EOIs are submitted and drawn.

| Stream or pathway | Candidates in the pool (approx.) |
|---|---|
| Alberta Opportunity Stream | 22,913 |
| Tourism and Hospitality Stream | 3,637 |
| Accelerated Tech Pathway | 2,116 |
| Rural Renewal Stream | 1,808 |
| Dedicated Health Care Pathway | 1,298 |

Figures reported on the AAIP processing information page and subject to change. Confirm the current record at the [Government of Alberta](https://www.alberta.ca/aaip-processing-information).

## How does an Alberta nomination affect your Express Entry CRS score?

**Short answer:** A provincial nomination adds 600 points to your Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score, which in practice guarantees a federal Invitation to Apply (ITA) for permanent residence. This is the core reason candidates chase an Alberta Express Entry Stream invitation. The Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) has two routes: an "enhanced" route tied to Express Entry, and a "base" route that runs on paper outside Express Entry. If Alberta nominates you through the Express Entry route, the federal government awards the 600 points once, and you claim them in your profile. Since federal PNP-specific rounds already draw from nominated candidates, that boost effectively moves you to the front of the line.

The mechanics of claiming the points are federal, not provincial. Once Alberta issues your nomination certificate, you confirm it in your Express Entry profile to receive the 600 additional points, per the [Government of Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees/express-entry/get-confirm-nomination.html). You can estimate your baseline federal score anytime with our [CRS calculator](/tools/crs-calculator).

## What changed in the Alberta AAIP in 2026?

Alberta made four changes worth tracking this year, and none of them altered the core eligibility rules for the worker streams. The largest is a capacity increase: IRCC granted the province an extra 200 nominations on August 10, 2026, lifting the 2026 allocation to 6,603. The other three are process changes. Alberta clarified how it assesses the economic establishment requirement for its three entrepreneur streams, launched a self-serve eligibility tool, and gave candidates the ability to edit a Worker Expression of Interest after submitting it. Allocation details by stream sit on the province's processing information page.

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| August 12, 2026 | Expanded guidance on the economic establishment requirement for the Rural, Graduate and Foreign Graduate Entrepreneur Streams |
| August 10, 2026 | IRCC added 200 nominations, raising Alberta's 2026 allocation to 6,603 |
| June 17, 2026 | Eligibility Explorer tool launched for checking stream eligibility before submitting an EOI |
| May 26, 2026 | Worker Expression of Interest became editable, with WEOIs valid for one year from submission |

A Worker Expression of Interest stays valid for one year after submission, and editing it does not extend or reset that validity. Candidates can also reject invitations to streams they do not want and return to the WEOI pool, as long as they do so before the 15-day invitation period closes.

## How can you position yourself for an Alberta PNP invitation?

**Short answer:** Build a complete federal Express Entry profile, target an in-demand Alberta occupation, and submit an accurate Expression of Interest so you are in the pool when the province draws. Because AAIP draws chase specific sectors like health care, technology, construction, and agriculture, your occupation and job offer often matter more than a marginal CRS gain. Strengthen your language scores, secure an eligible Alberta job offer where possible, and keep your EOI current. A licensed RCIC can map your profile to the stream you actually qualify for and flag risks before you apply. Start by reading our [Provincial Nominee Program guide](/immigration/provincial-nominee) and following the latest rounds in our [news](/news).

## When was the last Alberta PNP draw?

**Short answer:** There is no fixed answer, because the AAIP holds draws as needed rather than on a set schedule. The province can run several draws in a single week and then pause, so the "last" draw depends on the day you check. The only reliable source for the most recent round is Alberta's official processing information page, which lists each draw date, the stream drawn, the minimum score, and the number of invitations. Third-party trackers and news posts often report a date that is already out of date. ## What is the PNP score for Alberta?

**Short answer:** There is no single fixed "PNP score" for Alberta, because each draw sets its own minimum. Alberta ranks candidates using its Expression of Interest (EOI) system, and the cut-off in any round depends on the stream and the province's priorities that day. Across 2026, minimum EOI scores in AAIP draws ranged roughly from 45 to 73, per the province's official records, but that band shifts as demand changes. A high score helps, yet it does not guarantee an invitation, because Alberta also weighs your occupation, sector, and Alberta connection. Treat any single number you see online as a past result, not a target you can rely on for the next round. See the official archive at the [Government of Alberta](https://www.alberta.ca/aaip-processing-information).

## What CRS score is required for Alberta PNP?

**Short answer:** To be eligible for the Alberta Express Entry Stream, you need a minimum Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score of 300, plus an active federal Express Entry profile and eligibility under a federal program. That 300 is an eligibility floor for that stream, not a promise of selection. Alberta can and does invite candidates with CRS scores below the federal general-draw cut-offs, which is one reason a provincial nomination is so valuable. Other AAIP streams, such as the Alberta Opportunity Stream, do not use CRS at all, because they are not tied to Express Entry. So the CRS requirement applies specifically to the Express Entry route. Confirm the current threshold on the eligibility page at the [Government of Alberta](https://www.alberta.ca/aaip-alberta-express-entry-stream-eligibility).

## Is there any PNP draw today?

**Short answer:** Maybe, and the only way to know is to check Alberta's official processing information page, which the province updates when a draw runs. Alberta sometimes clusters several draws within days and then goes quiet for weeks. Rather than refreshing third-party trackers, bookmark the official page and check it directly, since it is the authoritative record of what was drawn and when. If you work with a licensed representative, they can monitor rounds against your specific stream and alert you when a relevant draw occurs. ## Is Alberta PNP still open?

**Short answer:** Yes. The Alberta Advantage Immigration Program remains an active pathway to permanent residence in 2026 and continues to run draws across its worker streams. Like every province, Alberta operates within a yearly nomination allocation set with the federal government, so intake in specific streams can pause once that stream fills or the province reaches its cap. A temporary pause in one stream does not mean the whole program has closed. The most accurate read on which streams are open and accepting Expressions of Interest is the province's own application streams page. If a stream you want is paused, a licensed RCIC can help you find an alternative route or prepare so you are ready when it reopens. See the [Government of Alberta](https://www.alberta.ca/aaip-application-streams).

## Is 67 points required for PNP?

**Short answer:** No. The 67-point requirement belongs to the federal Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP), a separate points grid out of 100, not to the Alberta PNP. People often confuse the two because both sit under Express Entry. For the Alberta Express Entry Stream, the relevant thresholds are a valid Express Entry profile, eligibility under a federal program, and a minimum Comprehensive Ranking System score of 300, not 67. The FSWP 67-point test only decides whether you can enter the Express Entry pool as a skilled worker in the first place. Once you are in the pool, your CRS score and Alberta's draw criteria take over. If the grids feel tangled, a licensed consultant can confirm exactly which ones apply to you.

# Manitoba PNP Draws 2026: Latest Results, Scores and How the EOI Draw Works

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/manitoba-pnp-draw-2026
Category: Provincial Nominee Program
Published: 2026-07-23
Author: Go Far Global Team

> The Manitoba Provincial Nominee Program runs Expression of Interest draws about twice a month. Here is how MPNP draws work, recent results, the scores you need, and how to get a Letter of Advice to Apply.

*As of July 23, 2026.*

The Manitoba Provincial Nominee Program (MPNP) runs its own draws throughout the year, separate from the federal Express Entry system. If you are watching for the next Manitoba PNP draw, this guide explains when the draws happen, how candidates are ranked, what scores recent rounds have needed, and how to get an invitation.

## When was the last Manitoba PNP draw?

**Short answer:** The MPNP holds Expression of Interest (EOI) draws roughly every two weeks. Its July 16, 2026 draw issued about 2,146 Letters of Advice to Apply (LAAs) across the Skilled Worker in Manitoba, Skilled Worker Overseas, and International Education streams, per figures reported for that round.

Because draw dates and totals change constantly, the only authoritative list is the province's own draw archive. Check it directly before you rely on any number you see repeated elsewhere.

## How does the Manitoba PNP Expression of Interest (EOI) draw work?

**Short answer:** You submit a free Expression of Interest (EOI) profile, the MPNP scores it out of 1,000 points, and in each draw it sends a Letter of Advice to Apply (LAA) to the highest-ranked candidates in the streams being invited. An LAA is an invitation to submit a full application, not a nomination.

The Expression of Interest system works like a ranked pool. Your score is built from factors such as your connection to Manitoba, language ability, age, education, and work experience. Candidates with a stronger Manitoba connection, for example a close relative in the province, past study or work there, or a job offer, tend to rank higher. The province draws the top-ranked candidates at regular intervals rather than on a fixed calendar, so the gap between draws and the number invited can vary.

## What score do you need for a Manitoba PNP draw?

**Short answer:** There is no single fixed cut-off. Each draw sets its own lowest score based on the stream and the pool that day, and the number can move by dozens of points between rounds. Recent Skilled Worker Overseas cut-offs have generally sat well above the program minimum, while direct invitations to Express Entry candidates in the pool have used different thresholds.

The table below shows the shape of recent 2026 rounds. Treat the totals as reported figures and confirm the exact numbers on the official draws page before acting on them.

| Draw date | Streams invited | LAAs issued (reported) |
|---|---|---|
| July 16, 2026 | Skilled Worker, International Education, Express Entry pathway | ~2,146 |
| June 18, 2026 | Skilled Worker in Manitoba, Skilled Worker Overseas | ~124 |
| June 4, 2026 | Skilled Worker streams (first June draw) | 100+ |

Your ranking score matters more than any past cut-off. A higher score in the pool is the single most reliable way to be invited, and you can estimate where you stand before you commit by checking your points with our [CRS and points tools](/tools/crs-calculator).

## Which Manitoba streams hold draws?

**Short answer:** Manitoba draws candidates through four main pathways: Skilled Worker in Manitoba (SWM), Skilled Worker Overseas (SWO), the International Education Stream (IES), and the Business Investor Stream. Most invitations go to the two Skilled Worker streams.

Skilled Worker in Manitoba is for people already working in the province, usually on a work permit, with a job offer from a Manitoba employer. Skilled Worker Overseas is for candidates outside Canada who have a genuine connection to Manitoba and score at least 60 of 100 points on the assessment factors. The International Education Stream serves graduates of Manitoba post-secondary institutions. The Business Investor Stream targets entrepreneurs planning to start or buy a business in the province. Each stream has its own criteria, so the pathway that fits you depends on your situation. You can read more about provincial options on our [provincial nominee overview](/immigration/provincial-nominee).

## How do you get invited in a Manitoba PNP draw?

**Short answer:** Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) profile, make sure your Manitoba connection and points are as strong as possible, and wait to be ranked in a draw. If your score is high enough when the MPNP draws your stream, you receive a Letter of Advice to Apply (LAA) and then submit a full nomination application.

The steps are straightforward on paper. First, confirm you meet a stream's eligibility. Second, build and submit your EOI, which is free and valid for the pool. Third, strengthen the factors you control, such as language test results and your documented connection to Manitoba. A provincial nomination, once approved, adds 600 points to a federal Express Entry profile, which effectively guarantees a federal invitation to apply for permanent residence. Because the ranking rules and connection requirements are detailed, many applicants have a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) review their profile first. If you want that review, you can [book a consultation](/book).

## When was the last PNP draw in Manitoba?

**Short answer:** Manitoba's most recent reported draw was on July 16, 2026, and the program runs new draws roughly every two weeks. Exact dates are never on a fixed schedule.

The MPNP does not publish an advance calendar, so there is no guaranteed date for the next round. It has, however, kept a steady rhythm of roughly two draws per month through 2026, inviting candidates across its Skilled Worker and education streams. The safest way to track it is the official draws archive, which the province updates within a day or two of each round. If you are in the pool, watch your MPNP account, since a Letter of Advice to Apply (LAA) appears there directly rather than by separate email alone.

## What is the PNP score for Manitoba?

**Short answer:** Manitoba scores Expression of Interest (EOI) candidates out of 1,000 points, and Skilled Worker Overseas applicants must reach at least 60 of 100 on the underlying assessment factors to be eligible. The draw cut-off then depends on how the rest of the pool ranks that day.

The 1,000-point EOI ranking weighs your connection to Manitoba most heavily, then language, age, education, and work experience. Meeting the 60-point eligibility floor for Skilled Worker Overseas gets you into the pool, but it does not guarantee an invitation, since draws invite the highest-ranked candidates first. A strong, well-documented Manitoba connection, competitive language scores, and skilled work experience are what push a profile above recent cut-offs. Confirm the current point grid on the province's official site before you submit.

## Is there an MPNP draw today?

**Short answer:** There may or may not be. Manitoba does not draw daily and does not announce draws in advance, so the only way to know is to check the official MPNP draws page, which is updated after each round.

Draws happen on the province's own schedule, usually a couple of times a month rather than daily. Third-party sites and social posts often repeat draw news a day or two late, so the [official draws archive](https://immigratemanitoba.com/draws/) is always the fastest reliable source. If today is not a draw day, the most useful thing you can do is make sure your Expression of Interest (EOI) profile is complete and your score is as high as possible, so you are ready when your stream is next invited.

## What was the last PNP draw?

**Short answer:** Across Canada, provinces run PNP draws on their own timelines, and Manitoba's most recent reported round was July 16, 2026. Other provinces, including Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, hold separate draws under their own programs.

"The last PNP draw" depends on which province you mean, because each Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) runs independently. Manitoba, Ontario, Saskatchewan, Alberta, British Columbia, and the Atlantic provinces each publish their own draw results. If Manitoba is your target, follow the MPNP draws page. If you are open to more than one province, it is worth comparing where your profile ranks best, which is something a consultant can map out with you.

## Is 67 points required for PNP?

**Short answer:** No. The 67-point pass mark belongs to the federal Federal Skilled Worker (FSW) eligibility grid, not to Manitoba's PNP. Manitoba uses its own separate scoring, and Skilled Worker Overseas requires at least 60 of 100 points to be eligible.

The 67-of-100 figure is a common mix-up because it comes from a different federal test. Provincial Nominee Programs set their own thresholds, and Manitoba's Skilled Worker Overseas floor is 60 points on its five assessment factors, with a separate 1,000-point EOI ranking used to decide who gets invited. Always check the criteria for the exact stream you are applying under, since the number that matters is the one your province publishes, not the federal FSW pass mark.

## What this means for you

Manitoba is one of the more accessible provinces for candidates with a real connection to it, and its steady draw rhythm gives applicants regular chances to be invited. The number that decides your outcome is your ranking score in the pool, not any past cut-off. # Canada Holds First-Ever Express Entry Draw for Skilled Military Recruits

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/express-entry-skilled-military-recruits-draw-2026
Category: Express Entry
Published: 2026-07-23
Author: Go Far Global Team

> On July 23, 2026, IRCC ran the first Express Entry draw ever held under the Skilled Military Recruits category: 4 invitations at a CRS score of 368, the smallest draw on record.

*As of July 23, 2026.*

On July 23, 2026, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) held the first Express Entry draw ever run under the new Skilled Military Recruits category. It was also the smallest Express Entry draw on record: 4 invitations to apply (ITAs) at a minimum Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score of 368.

## What happened in the July 23, 2026 Express Entry draw?

**Short answer:** IRCC ran Express Entry draw #430 on July 23, 2026, the first ever under the Skilled Military Recruits category, issuing 4 ITAs at a CRS cut-off of 368. That is the fewest invitations ever sent in a single Express Entry round.

A typical category-based round sends thousands of invitations, so a draw of 4 stands out immediately. The details are below.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Draw number | #430 |
| Date | July 23, 2026 |
| Category | Skilled Military Recruits (2026, Version 1) |
| Invitations (ITAs) | 4 |
| CRS cut-off | 368 |

## What is the Skilled Military Recruits category?

**Short answer:** Skilled Military Recruits is one of the Express Entry category-based selection categories IRCC added for 2026. It lets IRCC invite candidates in the Express Entry pool whose background is in a foreign military and who have a route into service with the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF).

Category-based selection lets IRCC invite candidates who fit a specific priority rather than only the highest-scoring profiles overall. The Skilled Military Recruits category centres on CAF roles, including operations members, specialized members, and commissioned officers. You can read more about how Express Entry works on our [Express Entry guide](/immigration/express-entry).

## Who qualifies for the Skilled Military Recruits category?

**Short answer:** According to IRCC's criteria for the category, candidates are generally expected to have at least 10 years of continuous service in a recognized foreign military, a guaranteed full-time Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) job offer of at least 3 years, and a post-secondary credential of 2 years or more.

A foreign credential is assessed through an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA). Because this is a brand-new and narrowly defined category, the requirements are strict and still settling into place. If you have a military background and think this could apply to you, confirm the current rules with a licensed consultant before you count on them, since the exact eligibility is easy to misread.

## Why did the draw invite only 4 candidates?

**Short answer:** A 4-invitation round most likely reflects how small the eligible pool is right now. Very few Express Entry candidates currently meet a category built around a decade of foreign military service and a three-year CAF job offer.

The low CRS cut-off of 368 points the same way. When a category targets a small, hard-to-fill group, the score needed to be invited drops well below the general Express Entry range, because IRCC is inviting nearly everyone who qualifies rather than ranking a large field. Expect these rounds to stay small unless the eligibility rules widen.

## How does this fit Express Entry category-based selection in 2026?

**Short answer:** Skilled Military Recruits sits alongside the other 2026 category-based draws, including Canadian Experience Class (CEC), French-language proficiency, healthcare, and the trades. Each category targets a specific labour-market or policy priority.

For most applicants, the categories that carry real volume are still the larger ones. A military-focused stream shows how precise IRCC's Express Entry targeting has become, but it does not change how you are ranked in the categories you actually qualify for. If you want to see where your profile stands, check your points with our [CRS calculator](/tools/crs-calculator).

## What should you do if you have a military background?

**Short answer:** If you have genuine foreign military experience and a real route into the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF), the new category could open a door that did not exist before, though the bar is high. The first step is confirming whether you meet the strict eligibility before you build your Express Entry profile around it.

If you are already in the Express Entry pool for other categories, this draw does not change your odds there. A licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) at Go Far Global can review your background and tell you honestly whether this pathway or another one fits you best. [Book a consultation](/book) and we will go through your options.

# Canada Immigration Fees 2026: PR Increase April 30, Citizenship $123

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/canada-immigration-fees-2026-complete-cost-guide
Category: News
Published: 2026-07-18
Author: Go Far Global Team

> A plain, current breakdown of every Canadian immigration government fee in 2026, in Canadian dollars, after the April 30 permanent residence increase and the March 31 citizenship change.

# Canada Immigration Fees 2026: PR Increase April 30, Citizenship $123

*As of August 31, 2026.*

Government fees are the part of an immigration budget you can pin to the dollar. Permanent residence fees rose on 30 April 2026. The right of citizenship fee rose on 31 March 2026. Temporary residence fees on the live Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) list did not move with those two changes. Figures below are in Canadian dollars and come from the IRCC fee list (date modified 2 July 2026) and the 30 April 2026 fee-changes page.

## TL;DR

Right of Permanent Residence Fee (RPRF) is $600 as of 30 April 2026 (was $575) | Most economic permanent residence processing is $990 for the principal applicant, $1,590 with RPRF | Adult citizenship is $653: $530 processing plus $123 right of citizenship from 31 March 2026 | A visitor visa or super visa is $100. A study permit is $150. A work permit is $155. Biometrics are $85, family maximum $170 | Applications received on or after 30 April 2026 pay the new permanent residence fees

## What changed in 2026?

**Short answer:** Two separate increases landed. Permanent residence fees increased on 30 April 2026 for economic programs, family class, business, protected persons, humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) or public policy, and permit holders. IRCC announced that in the [27 March 2026 notice](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/permanent-residence-fees-increasing.html). The right of citizenship fee increased on 31 March 2026 by $3.25, from $119.75 to $123. The adult citizenship processing fee stayed $530. IRCC announced that in the [right of citizenship fee notice](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/right-citizenship-fee-increasing.html). Applications received on or after each date pay the new amount.

The old-versus-new table is on IRCC's [fee changes](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/fee-changes.asp) page, date modified 30 April 2026. If you paid the old permanent residence fee with an application received on or after 30 April 2026, IRCC asks you to pay the difference through the additional-payment category in the online payment tool.

Temporary residence lines on the current [fee list](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/fees.asp) (date modified 2 July 2026) still show study permit $150, work permit $155, visitor visa $100, eTA $7, and biometrics $85. Restoration and inadmissibility fees last moved on 1 December 2025.

## How much is permanent residence in 2026?

**Short answer:** For most economic applicants, including Express Entry, the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), Quebec skilled workers, Atlantic immigration, and most economic pilots, the principal applicant pays $990 in processing plus $600 RPRF, which is $1,590 if you pay both together. A spouse or partner is the same $990 plus $600. Each dependent child is $270 and is not charged the RPRF. Business immigration is $1,895 processing for the principal applicant, $2,495 with RPRF. You can pay the RPRF with the application or later, but you must pay it before you become a permanent resident. IRCC refunds the RPRF if you withdraw or the application is refused. It is the only fee IRCC refunds after processing starts.

| Permanent residence stream (from 30 April 2026) | Processing (CAD) | With RPRF $600 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Economic principal applicant (Express Entry, PNP, Quebec skilled, Atlantic, most pilots) | $990 | $1,590 |
| Accompanying spouse or partner | $990 | $1,590 |
| Each dependent child | $270 | $270 (no RPRF) |
| Business principal applicant | $1,895 | $2,495 |
| H&C / public policy principal applicant | $660 | $1,260 |
| Protected person principal applicant | $660 | $660 (no RPRF) |
| Permit holders class without RPRF / with RPRF | $390 | $990 |

RPRF does not apply to dependent children of a principal applicant or sponsor, to sponsorship of adopted children, to sponsorship of an orphaned brother, sister, niece, nephew or grandchild, or to protected persons, including applicants eligible on H&C grounds and convention refugees.

The April 30 increase on the fee-changes table was $575 to $600 for RPRF, $950 to $990 for most economic principal applicants, $1,810 to $1,895 for business, $375 to $390 for permit holders, and $635 to $660 for protected persons and H&C principal applicants.

## How much is family sponsorship?

**Short answer:** Sponsoring a spouse or partner is $1,260 if you pay the sponsorship fee, the principal applicant processing fee, and the RPRF together. Independently sponsoring a dependent child is $180 per child. Sponsoring a parent or grandparent is also listed at $1,260 with RPRF, or $660 without. Those combined totals are on the live fee list. The 30 April 2026 component increases were sponsorship $85 to $90, sponsored principal applicant $545 to $570, sponsored dependent child principal applicant $85 to $90, accompanying spouse $635 to $660, and accompanying child $175 to $180.

New Parents and Grandparents Program intake was paused in 2026. Confirm the live [family immigration](/immigration/family-immigration) status before you pay anything toward a parent file. A super visa is a different application with a $100 visa fee. It is not a sponsorship.

## How much is Canadian citizenship?

**Short answer:** An adult grant is $653: $530 processing plus $123 right of citizenship. That $123 rate applies to applications received on or after 31 March 2026. A minor grant (under 18) is $100 processing and does not include the right of citizenship fee. A citizenship certificate (proof of citizenship) is $75. A search of citizenship records is $75. Resume citizenship is $530 for an adult and $100 for a minor. Renounce citizenship is $100.

| Citizenship certificate (proof) | $75 |
| Search of records | $75 |

## How much are study permits, work permits, and visitor visas?

**Short answer:** On the 2 July 2026 fee list a study permit, including an extension, is $150 per person. A work permit, including an extension, is $155 per person. The open work permit holder fee is $100. A visitor visa, including a super visa, is $100 per person, or $500 as a family maximum when 5 or more eligible family members apply at the same time and place. Extending stay as a visitor is $100. An electronic travel authorization (eTA) is $7. Biometrics are $85 per person, $170 as a family maximum for 2 or more eligible people applying together.

The visitor visa $100 / family $500 split is also printed on the [apply for a visitor visa](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/apply-visitor-visa.html) page. Super visa applicants see the same $100 plus $85 biometrics on the [super visa apply](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/parent-grandparent-super-visa/apply.html) page. ## What do these government fees not include?

**Short answer:** Language tests, an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA), the panel-physician medical exam, translations, courier, and any Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) or lawyer fees. A single Express Entry adult who pays processing and RPRF together is $1,590 in IRCC fees before test, ECA, and medical. A spouse sponsorship that pays the combined $1,260 still needs biometrics if required, and still needs the relationship evidence. Confirm every figure on the live [fee list](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/fees.asp) the week you pay. Fees can move again.
