# Study in Canada from Nigeria 2026: Schools, Permit, and PR

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/study-canada/study-canada-from-nigeria-2026
Category: Education
Published: 2026-06-27
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Nigeria is one of the fastest-growing source countries for Canadian study permits in West Africa.

*As of June 26, 2026.*

Nigeria is one of the fastest-growing source countries for Canadian study permits in West Africa. Students from Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, and beyond are choosing Canadian universities and colleges for the quality of education, the Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), and the realistic path to permanent residence afterward. This guide covers the full process for Nigerian students in 2026: picking the right school, getting a study permit, and planning for what happens after graduation.

> Who this is for: Nigerian secondary school leavers and current university students who want to study at a Canadian college or university, and parents supporting those applications.

## Who actually applies from Nigeria?

**Short answer:** Three main applicant profiles dominate Canadian study permit applications from Nigeria: recent WAEC/JAMB graduates entering a Canadian bachelor's or diploma program, current Nigerian university students transferring or pursuing a second degree, and working adults seeking Canadian graduate programs in business, IT, or public health to transition careers.

Nigerian applicants generally fall into one of these groups:

**Profile A: Secondary school completers.** Students who have finished their WAEC or NECO senior secondary certificate and are applying directly to Canadian colleges or universities. These applicants need to show strong grades, English proficiency, and proof of funds. Most target one or two-year college diplomas or four-year bachelor's programs.

**Profile B: Nigerian university students or graduates.** Students who have completed one or more years at a Nigerian university and want to transfer or pursue a full program in Canada. Visa officers look closely at the student's academic record, their reason for leaving Nigeria mid-study, and whether the proposed Canadian program represents genuine academic progression.

**Profile C: Young professionals.** Working Nigerians aged 25 to 35 applying to Canadian graduate programs, often in business administration, public health, computer science, or project management. The key challenge here is demonstrating both genuine study intent and ties to support eventual return or PR application through proper channels.

Each profile has different documentation strengths and weaknesses, which is why the supporting letter matters as much as the bank statement.

## Where do Nigerian students actually apply to study in Canada?

**Short answer:** The most popular destinations for Nigerian students are Ontario (Toronto, Ottawa, Hamilton, Waterloo), British Columbia (Vancouver, Burnaby), Alberta (Calgary, Edmonton), and Atlantic provinces (Halifax, Fredericton, Moncton) for more accessible admission and lower living costs. The school you choose must appear on the [Designated Learning Institution (DLI) list](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/prepare/designated-learning-institutions-list.html) to qualify for a study permit.

DLI stands for Designated Learning Institution. Only DLI-approved schools can support a study permit application. Every public college and university in Canada is a DLI. Some private colleges are also designated, but not all. Confirm your school's DLI status before applying.

Nigerian students tend to favour these program areas, based on filing patterns at Go Far Global:

- **Business and finance**: MBA, accounting, project management, supply chain
- **Information technology**: computer science, cybersecurity, data analytics, software engineering
- **Health sciences**: nursing bridging, public health, health informatics
- **Engineering**: civil, mechanical, electrical at both college and university level
- **Hospitality and tourism**: two-year college diplomas with fast PGWP eligibility

**Tier 1 (high competition, strong name recognition):** University of Toronto, University of British Columbia, McMaster, University of Waterloo, Queen's. These require very strong academic records and are selective for international applicants.

**Tier 2 (strong programs, more accessible):** York University, Ryerson (now Toronto Metropolitan University), Concordia, University of Calgary, University of Alberta, Dalhousie. Tuition typically $25,000 to $50,000 CAD per year.

**Tier 3 (diploma-focused, PR pathway strong):** Humber College, Seneca College, Algonquin College, NAIT, SAIT, Nova Scotia Community College. Tuition typically $14,000 to $22,000 CAD per year. Strong PGWP eligibility and faster entry to the labour market.

## What is the study permit process from Nigeria?

**Short answer:** Nigerian applicants apply online through the IRCC (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada) portal, submit biometrics at the Visa Application Centre (VAC) in Lagos or Abuja (both operated by VFS Global), and typically receive a decision within 8 to 16 weeks from the date biometrics are given. The 2024 Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) requirement applies and must be included before the application is submitted.

PAL stands for Provincial Attestation Letter. Since January 2024, most study permit applicants at the post-secondary level need a PAL from the province where their school is located. The school requests it from the provincial government on the student's behalf. You generally need to accept the offer of admission and pay at least a partial tuition deposit before the school will request your PAL.

The application process step by step:

| Stage | Typical Timeline |
|---|---|
| Receive conditional or unconditional offer from a Canadian DLI | Starting point |
| Accept offer and pay tuition deposit | 0 to 2 weeks |
| School requests Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) from province | 1 to 3 weeks |
| PAL issued to student | 2 to 8 weeks (varies by province) |
| Open IRCC Secure Account and submit study permit application online | Same day PAL received |
| Receive Biometric Instruction Letter (BIL) from IRCC | Within 1 to 2 weeks of submission |
| Book and attend biometrics appointment at VFS Global Lagos or Abuja | 1 to 3 weeks after BIL |
| Medical exam (if required, at a panel physician in Nigeria) | 1 to 2 weeks |
| IRCC reviews application and makes decision | 8 to 16 weeks after biometrics |
| Submit passport for visa stamp (if approved) | 1 to 2 weeks |
| Receive passport, book travel | 1 week |

**Total realistic timeline: 5 to 7 months from offer to landing in Canada.** Start the process early. Nigerian applicants from the Abuja visa office should allow more time than the global average because processing volumes for West Africa are high.

Biometrics (fingerprints and photo) are collected at [VFS Global centres in Lagos and Abuja](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/where-to-give-biometrics.asp). You cannot skip biometrics unless you have given them within the past 10 years for a previous Canadian application. Book your VFS appointment as soon as you receive your Biometric Instruction Letter, as slots fill quickly.

## What documents do Nigerian students need?

**Short answer:** Every application requires a valid Nigerian passport, the acceptance letter from a Canadian DLI, the Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL), proof of funds, proof of language proficiency, academic transcripts, a statement of purpose (study plan), and a completed IMM 1294 application form. Additional documents depend on the applicant's profile.

The [IRCC study permit documents checklist](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents.html) is the authoritative source. Do not rely on third-party checklists; they go out of date. The core documents are:

**Always required:**
- Valid Nigerian passport (valid for the full duration of study, ideally)
- Acceptance letter from a PGWP-eligible DLI
- Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) from the province
- Proof of funds (see next section)
- Statement of purpose explaining why you want to study in Canada, why this program, and your plans after graduation
- Academic transcripts and certificates (WAEC, NECO, JAMB, university transcripts)

**Usually required:**
- English language test results (IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, or Duolingo)
- Nigerian police clearance certificate
- Recent passport photos
- Proof of payment of application fee ($150 CAD for study permit) and biometrics fee ($85 CAD)

**Sometimes required:**
- Medical exam results from a designated panel physician in Nigeria
- Family ties documentation (marriage certificate, birth certificates for dependants)
- Evidence of prior travel to Canada, the UK, the US, or Schengen if applicable

IRCC's processing fees are set out on the [IRCC study permit application page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/apply.html).

## How much money do Nigerian students need to prove?

**Short answer:** IRCC requires proof of tuition for the first year plus at least $20,635 CAD for living expenses (outside Quebec), meaning a typical Nigerian applicant needs to show $35,000 to $65,000 CAD depending on the school and program. Documents must show funds are accessible, liquid, and genuinely available to the applicant.

The $20,635 CAD living expense figure is set by IRCC and does not include tuition or transportation. For the full picture:

| Expense category | Estimated amount (CAD) |
|---|---|
| College tuition (one year, typical range) | $14,000 to $22,000 |
| University tuition (one year, typical range) | $25,000 to $45,000 |
| Living expenses required by IRCC (outside Quebec) | $20,635 |
| Airfare (Lagos or Abuja to Canada, return) | $1,200 to $2,000 |
| **Total to show for college applicant** | **$36,000 to $45,000** |
| **Total to show for university applicant** | **$47,000 to $68,000** |

Read the full requirements on the [proof of funds page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html).

Acceptable proof of funds for Nigerian applicants:

- **Guaranteed Investment Certificate (GIC)** of at least $20,635 CAD at a Canadian bank (Scotiabank, CIBC, RBC, National Bank). This is the cleanest option and many visa officers view it favourably.
- **Nigerian bank statements** for the past 6 to 12 months, showing consistent balances sufficient to cover tuition and living costs. GTBank, First Bank, Access Bank, UBA, Zenith Bank statements are all accepted.
- **Sponsor letter from a parent or guardian**, accompanied by the sponsor's bank statements, employment letter, payslips, and evidence of their relationship to the applicant.
- **Government scholarship award letter** (Nigerian government, PTDF, or foreign scholarship bodies).
- **Education loan approval** from a Nigerian or international bank.

The most common reason Nigerian study permit applications are refused is weak or inconsistent proof of funds. Bank statements that show large unexplained deposits shortly before the application, or balances that are inconsistent with the sponsor's stated income, raise credibility concerns. Prepare 12 months of clean statements where possible.

## What English language test do you need?

**Short answer:** Most Canadian colleges require IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band below 5.5); most universities require IELTS Academic 6.5 (no band below 6.0). TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, and Duolingo English Test are also accepted at many institutions. For the Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), you will need to show an IELTS General Training score at CLB 7 for university graduates and CLB 5 for college/trades graduates.

CLB stands for Canadian Language Benchmark. The language test for PGWP eligibility must be valid (taken within 2 years) at the time you apply for the PGWP, not at the time you apply for your study permit.

The Duolingo English Test ($59 USD online) is now accepted at many Canadian institutions and is significantly cheaper than IELTS ($265 to $310 USD in Nigeria). However, Duolingo is not valid for the PGWP language requirement. If you plan to work in Canada after graduation, take the IELTS General Training test close to the end of your studies.

Nigerians educated in English-medium secondary schools often score well on IELTS because English is the official language of instruction in Nigeria. Many applicants can write the test and meet university-level requirements without a preparatory course. Check your specific school's minimum requirements before registering for a test.

## What happens after graduation: can Nigerian students stay and work in Canada?

**Short answer:** After completing a full-time program of at least 8 months at a PGWP-eligible DLI, you can apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) valid for up to 3 years. You must apply within 180 days of receiving your final transcript or official letter confirming graduation. After working in a TEER (Training, Education, Experience, and Responsibilities) 0, 1, 2, or 3 occupation for one year, you may be eligible for permanent residence through Express Entry or a Provincial Nominee Program.

To qualify for a PGWP:

1. Complete a full-time program of at least 8 months at a DLI
2. Graduate from a PGWP-eligible program (confirmed on the DLI list)
3. Maintain valid immigration status throughout your studies
4. Apply within 180 days of official confirmation of graduation
5. Meet the IELTS General Training language requirement (CLB 7 for university graduates, CLB 5 for college and trades graduates)

PGWP length matches your program length, up to a maximum of 3 years.

Once you have a PGWP and Canadian work experience, PR options include:

**Path A: Canadian Experience Class (Express Entry).** Work full-time in a skilled occupation (TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3) for at least one year, then apply through [Express Entry](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry.html). The Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS, the points-based score used to rank Express Entry candidates) score required varies by draw. Canadian work experience, a Canadian credential, and strong language scores improve your CRS score significantly.

**Path B: Provincial Nominee Program (PNP).** Most provinces operate graduate nominee streams. These add 600 points to your CRS score and effectively guarantee an Invitation to Apply if you have been working in the province and meet the program requirements. Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, and Atlantic provinces all have active PNP streams.

**Path C: Atlantic Immigration Program.** If you study and work in any of the four Atlantic provinces (Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland and Labrador), you may qualify for the Atlantic Immigration Program, which is employer-driven and leads to PR faster than Express Entry in some cases.

Nigerian graduates who complete Canadian programs, gain PGWP work experience, and maintain strong language scores are well positioned for PR. The credential, the Canadian work history, and English fluency are the three factors that matter most in Express Entry scoring.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Studying in Canada from Nigeria

**How long does a study permit from Nigeria take in 2026?**
Processing times from the Abuja visa office vary but typically run 8 to 16 weeks from the date biometrics are submitted. The total timeline from receiving an offer of admission to landing in Canada is usually 5 to 7 months. Apply as early as possible after receiving your offer. IRCC posts current processing times on their website, and these change regularly.

**Does my Nigerian bank account have to hold the full funds before I apply?**
The funds do not have to be sitting in your personal account. You can show a sponsor's bank statements, a scholarship letter, a GIC certificate, or an education loan approval. What matters is that the officer can see a clear, credible connection between the available money and the person responsible for funding your studies. Funds that appear suddenly in the account in the weeks before the application, without explanation, often trigger credibility concerns.

**Can I work while studying in Canada?**
Yes. Study permit holders enrolled in a full-time program at a DLI are permitted to work up to 24 hours per week off campus during regular academic sessions, and full-time during scheduled breaks. This means most Nigerian students can hold part-time jobs during the school year and full-time jobs in the summer. On-campus work is also permitted without a separate work permit.

**What is the study permit refusal rate for Nigerians, and how do I avoid refusal?**
Nigeria has historically had higher study permit refusal rates than some other source countries. The most common refusal reasons are: insufficient or inconsistent proof of funds, a weak study plan that does not explain why Canada was chosen over Nigeria or another country, and concern that the applicant is unlikely to leave Canada after the program ends. A clear, specific study plan and solid financial documentation reduce refusal risk significantly. If you have received a prior refusal, the second application needs to directly address the reasons given in the refusal letter.

**Can I bring my spouse or child to Canada while I study?**
A spouse or common-law partner can apply for an open work permit if you are enrolled in a graduate-level program (master's or PhD) at a DLI. For most undergraduate and college programs, spouses are not automatically eligible for open work permits, but they can apply for visitor status. Children under school age can accompany you; school-age children attending Canadian public school may need their own study permit or can be listed as accompanying minors depending on the province and school board.

## Ready to plan your Canadian study path?

**Short answer:** Go Far Global is a CICC (College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants)-regulated RCIC (Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant) firm based in Toronto. We work with Nigerian students at every stage: choosing the right DLI and program for your goals, preparing a strong study permit application, and planning the PGWP and PR pathway. [Book a consultation](/book) to get started.

School selection affects not just admission but your PGWP eligibility, your PR pathway, and your cost of living in Canada. These decisions compound over the 5 to 7 year journey from study permit to PR. Getting the school-program-province combination right at the start saves time and money later.

If you have received a study permit refusal, have a complex funds situation, or are planning a family application alongside yours, working with a regulated representative reduces the risk of a second refusal.

# OINP 2026 Redesign: Ontario Replaces 8 Streams With the Workforce Priority Stream

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/oinp-workforce-priority-stream-2026
Category: News
Published: 2026-06-27
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Ontario rewrote its main economic immigration program today.

*As of August 5, 2026. Updated for the August 4 opening of the Expression of Interest portal, and with Ontario’s published Workforce Priority Stream scoring framework.*

Ontario rewrote its main economic immigration program this summer, and as of August 4, 2026 the replacement is live. On June 26, 2026, the Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program (OINP) closed all eight of its remaining streams and replaced them with one new stream, the Ontario Workforce Priority Stream. The change took effect immediately under amendments to Ontario Regulation 422/17, and it is the first of a two-phase redesign. This guide breaks down what closed, what the new stream requires, what happens to applications already in the system, and what to do next. The details come straight from the Government of Ontario.

> Who this is for: skilled and intermediate workers with an Ontario job offer, self-employed physicians, Ontario employers, and anyone with an OINP application or Expression of Interest already in progress.

## What changed in the OINP on June 26, 2026?

Short answer: Ontario closed eight streams and launched one new stream, the Ontario Workforce Priority Stream. The Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development amended Ontario Regulation 422/17 under the Ontario Immigration Act, 2015, effective June 26, 2026. The amendments remove the eight streams the OINP had been running and introduce a single consolidated stream built around arranged employment in Ontario. The province calls this Phase 1 of a two-phase redesign meant to make permanent-residence pathways faster for people with a job offer, raise language and education standards, strengthen program integrity, and give rural and northern employers easier revenue thresholds. The Expression of Interest (EOI) system that feeds the program is closed for now and is expected to reopen later in the summer. Ontario sets out the change on its [2026 OINP updates](https://www.ontario.ca/page/2026-ontario-immigrant-nominee-program-updates) page.

## Which OINP streams were closed?

Short answer: All eight remaining streams are gone, across the employer, graduate, and Express Entry categories. The closures cover the three Employer Job Offer streams, both graduate streams, and all three Express Entry-aligned streams, and no further invitations will be issued under any of them. The table lists every closed stream.

| Category | Closed OINP stream |
|---|---|
| Employer Job Offer | Foreign Worker |
| Employer Job Offer | In-Demand Skills |
| Employer Job Offer | International Student |
| Graduate | Master's Graduate |
| Graduate | PhD Graduate |
| Express Entry | Human Capital Priorities |
| Express Entry | French-speaking Skilled Worker |
| Express Entry | Skilled Trades |

If you were building a profile for one of these streams, that route no longer exists. The replacement is the Workforce Priority Stream below. For the earlier May 30 regulatory step that set up this redesign, see our [OINP May 30 rule changes](/news/oinp-2026-redesign-may-30) explainer.

## What is the new Ontario Workforce Priority Stream?

Short answer: It is one stream with three pathways, all built around a permanent Ontario job offer, except for physicians. The Ontario Workforce Priority Stream folds the old structure into a single program with pathways for workers across every National Occupational Classification (NOC) Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities (TEER) category, plus a separate route for self-employed physicians. The province says the stream is meant to help employers keep proven talent in hard-to-fill roles and move workers with arranged employment toward permanent residence. Two of the three pathways require a full-time, permanent job offer in Ontario, while the physician pathway does not. Canada explains how a provincial nomination fits the wider system on the [Provincial Nominee Program](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html) page, and how nominations interact with [Express Entry](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry.html).

## Who qualifies under the TEER 0-3 pathway?

Short answer: Skilled workers in TEER 0 to 3 jobs with a permanent Ontario job offer who meet one experience option. This pathway targets internationally trained workers in NOC TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 occupations with a full-time, permanent job offer in Ontario. On work experience, you must show one of three things: six months consecutive in the last 12 months in the job-offer position with the job-offer employer; for recent Ontario graduates, three months consecutive in the last 12 months in that position with that employer; or two years cumulative in the last five years in the same NOC occupation. Applicants in licensed occupations are exempt from the experience requirement. The language requirement is Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB) 6, dropping to CLB 5 for certain occupations, and you need a post-secondary degree or diploma. Some occupations carry alternate criteria, so check the regulation for your role.

## What are the TEER 4-5 and self-employed physician pathways?

Short answer: One covers intermediate roles with a job offer, the other covers physicians with no job offer. The TEER 4-5 pathway is open to workers in NOC TEER 4 and 5 occupations with a full-time, permanent Ontario job offer. It asks for nine months of cumulative experience in the last two years in the job-offer position with the job-offer employer, CLB 4 language, and a Canadian secondary school diploma or equivalent. Additional criteria, including wage requirements for some roles, are set out in the regulation. The self-employed physician pathway is the one route with no job offer. To qualify, you must be a member in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO), hold a valid certificate of registration in an eligible class (independent, academic, or provisional), and be eligible to bill the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP). Across all three pathways, employers in rural communities, defined as a census division with a population under 150,000, get lower gross annual revenue thresholds.

The table sums up the three pathways.

| Pathway | Job offer | Experience | Language | Education |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TEER 0-3 | Permanent, full-time | 6 months, or 3 months for recent Ontario grads, or 2 years cumulative in 5 years | CLB 6 (CLB 5 some roles) | Post-secondary degree or diploma |
| TEER 4-5 | Permanent, full-time | 9 months cumulative in 2 years | CLB 4 | Secondary school diploma |
| Self-employed physician | Not required | CPSO good standing, OHIP billing eligibility | Set by regulation | Eligible registration class |

## How are candidates scored under the new Ontario Workforce Priority Stream?

**Short answer:** Ontario ranks Expression of Interest (EOI) profiles on a points grid it published in late July 2026. Job-offer candidates can score up to 130 points and self-employed physicians up to 115. The grid rewards Ontario work experience, Canadian income history, higher wages, official-language ability, and settling outside Toronto.

Ontario released the full scoring factors for the Workforce Priority Stream in late July 2026, so candidates can now see how the province will rank them once the EOI system reopens. Points come from employment, education, language, and regional factors. The main factors and their maximum values are below.

| Scoring factor | Maximum points |
|---|---|
| Ontario work experience (24+ months in the offered job) | 18 |
| Official language ability (Canadian Language Benchmark 9 or higher) | 15 |
| Hourly wage ($40 per hour or more) | 15 |
| Work location (Northern Ontario) | 15 |
| Knowledge of both official languages | 10 |
| Occupational category (health occupations score highest) | 10 |
| Highest level of education | 10 |
| Canadian credentials (more than one) | 10 |
| Legal status (valid work permit) | 10 |
| National Occupational Classification (NOC) TEER 0-1 | 9 |
| Canadian earnings history | 8 |

Two things stand out. First, regionalization is now a real lever: a job in Northern Ontario earns the full 15 location points while a job in Toronto earns zero, so where the job sits can change your rank. Second, self-employed physicians are scored on a modified grid that removes the wage factor and instead awards points for cumulative medical practice in Ontario. Point values for each sub-level can still change, so confirm every figure on the province's [official Workforce Priority Stream page](https://www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-workforce-priority-stream) before you rely on it. To estimate your federal ranking alongside this, use our [CRS calculator](/tools/crs-calculator), and to follow Ontario's invitation rounds once they resume, see our [Ontario PNP draw guide](/news/ontario-pnp-draw-2026).


## Is the Ontario Workforce Priority Stream open now?

**Short answer:** Yes. Ontario opened the Expression of Interest portal for the Ontario Workforce Priority Stream on August 4, 2026, and it is now the only OINP stream accepting registrations. No invitations have been issued under the new stream yet. Ontario's invitations page still lists only pre-redesign Employer Job Offer draws, the most recent on April 30, 2026, so everyone registering today is entering a pool that has not been drawn from.

The order of operations is not the one most applicants expect, and you cannot start it yourself. Your employer goes first: they register their business in the Employer Portal and submit a job offer for your position. That generates a job offer ID, and only then can you register an EOI. Employers who were registered before the redesign do not need to register again, but they must submit a new job offer, because offers made under the closed streams do not carry over.

Three deadlines then run, and the third one contains a trap:

| Step | Who | Deadline |
|---|---|---|
| Register the EOI | You | 30 calendar days from your employer submitting the job offer |
| Application for approval of the employment position | Your employer | 14 calendar days from the invitation to apply |
| Submit your application and pay | You | 17 calendar days from the invitation to apply |

The trap is in the last row. Your 17 days run from the invitation, but Ontario will not let you submit until after your employer has filed their application for approval of the employment position. You can build your application during those 17 days; you cannot press submit. An employer who uses their full 14 days leaves you three. Agree a filing date with your employer before you register the EOI, not after the invitation arrives.

## What happens to your existing OINP EOI or application?

Short answer: Pending EOIs under the old streams will be withdrawn, but submitted applications keep the old rules. The EOI system is now closed to new EOIs, and no further invitations will be issued under the former streams. Any EOI or job offer registered under an old stream that has not already led to an invitation to apply will be automatically withdrawn over the coming weeks while Ontario updates its platforms, and affected candidates, employers, and representatives will be notified directly. If you already submitted a full application after receiving an invitation under a former stream, that application will still be assessed against the rules in effect when you submitted it. Once the new EOI system reopens, eligible candidates will need to register a fresh EOI under the Workforce Priority Stream. Employers who already have a portal account do not need to re-register it, but they will have to submit a new job offer and a new application for approval of the employment position.

## What should workers and employers do now?

Short answer: Register, if your employer will move. The EOI portal opened on August 4, 2026, so the preparation window is over and the pool is live but undrawn. Workers should confirm their occupation's TEER category, check which experience option they can meet, and book a language test that reaches the benchmark for their pathway, since CLB 6 is higher than several old streams required. Employers should confirm their roles are permanent and full-time and, if they are rural, check whether they fall under the lower revenue thresholds. The province also tightened compliance: the response time for a Notice of Intent to Issue an Administrative Monetary Penalty (AMP) or Ban order dropped from 60 to 30 days, and notices can now be sent by email, mail, or in person and are treated as delivered. You can follow draw activity through our [OINP news and draws](/news/ontario-oinp-overhaul-2026) tracker, and review the program on Ontario's [OINP](https://www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-immigrant-nominee-program-oinp) page.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the OINP Redesign

These are the questions Ontario candidates are asking after the June 26 changes. In short: the OINP was redesigned, not cancelled, the eight old streams are closed, and the new Workforce Priority Stream opens for EOIs later this summer.

**Is the OINP suspended in 2026?** Not suspended, redesigned. The program is open, but the Expression of Interest system is temporarily closed while Ontario switches platforms, and it is expected to reopen later in the summer for the new Workforce Priority Stream.

**Will the OINP be removed?** No. Ontario removed eight individual streams and replaced them with one consolidated stream. The program itself continues, and the province has said a second phase of the redesign is still to come.

**Are there still OINP draws in 2026?** No new invitations will be issued under the former streams. New draws will run under the Ontario Workforce Priority Stream once the EOI system reopens later in the summer.

**Who is eligible for the Ontario Workforce Priority Stream?** Skilled workers in TEER 0 to 3 jobs and intermediate workers in TEER 4 to 5 jobs, in both cases with a permanent full-time Ontario job offer plus the required experience, language, and education, and self-employed physicians who meet the CPSO and OHIP conditions without a job offer.

**What happens to my existing OINP application?** If you only have an EOI or job offer under an old stream with no invitation yet, it will be withdrawn over the coming weeks. If you already submitted an application after an invitation, it stays under the old rules.

Short answer: By matching you to the right pathway and timing the new EOI. Go Far Global is a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm in Toronto, regulated by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC). We help workers confirm their TEER category and experience option, plan the language score the new benchmarks require, and prepare a clean EOI and application for the Workforce Priority Stream the moment it opens. We also help Ontario employers structure qualifying job offers, including the rural revenue thresholds. [Book a consultation](/book) to get ready before the EOI reopens.

# TEF Canada: Score Chart, CLB Levels, and Express Entry Value (2026)

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/tef-canada-score-chart-clb-2026
Category: News
Published: 2026-06-25
Author: Go Far Global Team

> TEF Canada is one of two French tests Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) accepts for economic immigration and citizenship, and a strong score can lift your Express Entry profile...

*As of June 25, 2026.*

TEF Canada is one of two French tests Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) accepts for economic immigration and citizenship, and a strong score can lift your Express Entry profile more than almost anything else you do. This guide gives you the official score-to-benchmark chart, the level Express Entry actually requires, how TEF Canada compares to the Test de connaissance du francais pour le Canada (TCF Canada), what it costs, and what changed in 2026 when IRCC tightened how it verifies language results. The conversion figures come straight from IRCC's official table.

> Who this is for: Express Entry candidates and students who plan to prove French with TEF Canada, especially anyone targeting the [French-language category draws](/news/express-entry-category-based-selection-2026).

## What is the TEF Canada exam?

Short answer: It is a French proficiency test built for Canadian immigration. The Test d'evaluation de francais pour le Canada (TEF Canada) measures four abilities: reading, listening, writing, and speaking. Each ability is scored on its own scale, reading out of 300, listening out of 360, and writing and speaking out of 450, with no combined total. IRCC recognizes TEF Canada for Express Entry, several [Provincial Nominee Program](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html) streams, and citizenship. You take it at an approved test centre, such as an Alliance Francaise location, not on your own at home. A TEF Canada result is valid for two years from the test date, the same window IRCC applies to all approved tests.

## What is the TEF Canada score chart, and how does it convert to CLB?

Short answer: IRCC converts your raw scores to benchmark levels, one skill at a time. TEF Canada scores convert to the Niveaux de competence linguistique canadiens (NCLC), the French equivalent of the Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB). IRCC scores each of the four skills independently and does not average them, so your weakest skill sets your usable level. The table below is the official conversion for tests taken on or after December 10, 2023.

| NCLC / CLB level | Reading (out of 300) | Listening (out of 360) | Writing (out of 450) | Speaking (out of 450) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 263-300 | 316-360 | 393-450 | 393-450 |
| 9 | 248-262 | 298-315 | 371-392 | 371-392 |
| 8 | 233-247 | 280-297 | 349-370 | 349-370 |
| 7 | 207-232 | 249-279 | 310-348 | 310-348 |
| 6 | 181-206 | 217-248 | 271-309 | 271-309 |
| 5 | 151-180 | 181-216 | 226-270 | 226-270 |
| 4 | 121-150 | 145-180 | 181-225 | 181-225 |

Check your own result against IRCC's [Express Entry language test results](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/language-test.html) page, because IRCC keeps a separate table for tests taken before December 10, 2023.

## What TEF Canada score do you need for Express Entry?

Short answer: NCLC 7 in every skill is the number that matters most. The Federal Skilled Worker Program sets a floor of CLB 7 in your first official language, and the French-language category draws require NCLC 7 across all four abilities. Reaching NCLC 7 means at least 207 in reading, 249 in listening, 310 in writing, and 310 in speaking. Because IRCC does not average, one skill at NCLC 6 keeps you out of a French-category round until you retake the test. The payoff is large: strong French adds substantial [Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) points](/news/how-to-improve-crs-score) and opens the French-language category, which has invited candidates at scores well below the general cut-offs. IRCC sets out the rounds and categories on its [Express Entry](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry.html) page.

## TEF Canada vs TCF Canada: which should you take?

Short answer: Both count equally for IRCC, so choose on format and fit. TEF Canada and TCF Canada are the two French tests IRCC accepts, and a given NCLC level carries the same weight no matter which test produced it. They differ in structure and timing. TEF Canada mixes multiple-choice and open-ended sections and runs shorter overall, while TCF Canada uses a different question style and schedule. Test-centre availability, exam dates, and your own comfort with each format usually decide it. If your goal is the French-language category, the test you pick matters far less than hitting NCLC 7 in all four skills. If your stronger language is English instead, compare the English tests in our [CELPIP vs IELTS guide](/news/celpip-vs-ielts-canada-2026). IRCC explains the category routes on its [category-based selection](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/rounds-invitations/category-based-selection.html) page.

## How much does TEF Canada cost, and how do you register?

Short answer: You register through an approved test centre, and fees vary by centre. TEF Canada is delivered by approved organizations such as Alliance Francaise centres across Canada and abroad, and each sets its own fee and schedule, so confirm the current price when you book. Register only through an official, approved centre. This matters for more than logistics: IRCC verifies results directly with test providers, and a result that did not come from a legitimate sitting can sink your whole application. Book early, because seats for popular dates fill well in advance, especially when a French-category draw is expected.

## What did Canada change about language-test checks in 2026?

Short answer: IRCC tightened verification across all approved tests. In June 2026, IRCC updated the instructions its officers follow, requiring them to cross-reference an applicant's photo against the test result, check testing-provider fraud alerts, and refer any concern to the Tips and Reports Management Unit before reaching a decision. The change covers all five approved tests, the French TEF Canada and TCF Canada included, and IRCC has separately said it is reviewing irregularities in a French-category Express Entry round. For an honest applicant, the takeaways are simple: sit the test yourself at an approved centre, keep your registration and result records, and avoid anyone promising a "guaranteed" score. A misrepresentation finding does not just refuse the application, it can bar you from Canada for five years.

## Frequently Asked Questions About TEF Canada

These are the questions candidates ask most often before booking TEF Canada. The short version: it tests four French skills, each scored on its own scale, and NCLC 7 in all four is the level most Express Entry candidates aim for.

**Is the TEF Canada exam hard?** It is challenging for most non-native speakers, especially the listening and speaking sections under time pressure. Difficulty is relative to your French level, and steady practice across all four skills is what moves the result.

**Can I prepare for TEF Canada in three months?** Many candidates reach NCLC 7 in about three months of focused study if they already have an intermediate base. If you are starting closer to beginner, plan for longer and build all four skills, since your weakest one caps your level.

**How much score is CLB 7 in TEF Canada?** NCLC 7, the French CLB 7, needs at least 207 in reading, 249 in listening, 310 in writing, and 310 in speaking on the current conversion table.

**Is TEF Canada valid for citizenship?** Yes. IRCC accepts TEF Canada as proof of French for citizenship, alongside its use for Express Entry and several provincial programs.

## How can a licensed immigration consultant help you use a TEF Canada score?

Short answer: By turning the score into the right strategy. Go Far Global is a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm in Toronto, regulated by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC). We help candidates read their TEF Canada result against the NCLC chart, work out the Comprehensive Ranking System points and French-category eligibility it unlocks, and plan an Express Entry or provincial strategy around it. [Book a consultation](/book) to see what your French score is worth.

*This article is general information, not legal advice. Score conversions, draw categories, and test rules change. Confirm the current rules for your situation with a licensed RCIC and on the official IRCC website before you act.*

# CUAET by the Numbers: 962,612 Approved, Extensions Now Run to 2027

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/cuaet-by-the-numbers-2026
Category: News
Published: 2026-06-25
Author: Go Far Global Team

> The Canada-Ukraine Authorization for Emergency Travel (CUAET) was the largest emergency immigration measure in Canadian history, and it is widely misunderstood today.

*As of June 25, 2026.*

The Canada-Ukraine Authorization for Emergency Travel (CUAET) was the largest emergency immigration measure in Canadian history, and it is widely misunderstood today. The program closed to new applicants in 2023, yet the work-permit extensions tied to it were renewed again in 2026 and now run into 2027. This guide sets out what CUAET was, the official numbers behind it, who can still extend their status, and where the permanent-residence routes stand. The headline figures come from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) data released under the Access to Information Act, request A-2025-73938.

> Who this is for: Ukrainians in Canada on a CUAET-linked permit, their families, and anyone tracking how the program actually played out.

## What is CUAET, and is it still open?

Short answer: It is closed to new applicants. CUAET launched on March 17, 2022, after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, as a fast, fee-free route for Ukrainians and their family members to come to Canada as temporary residents for up to three years. It granted [open work permits](/news/open-work-permit-canada-2026), study permits, and visitor status outside the normal rules. IRCC stopped accepting new CUAET applications on July 15, 2023, and the program has not reopened. What continues are the in-Canada measures for people who already arrived, including the work-permit extensions covered below. IRCC explains the current measures on its [immigration measures and support for Ukrainians](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/ukraine-measures.html) page.

## How many people came to Canada under CUAET?

Short answer: Close to a million applications, and hundreds of thousands of arrivals. According to IRCC data released under the Access to Information Act (request A-2025-73938), the program received 1,189,326 applications and approved 962,612, an approval rate of 82.2 percent, as of early April 2024. By May 31, 2024, 298,301 people had been confirmed in Canada under the measures: 239,912 on work permits, 45,597 on visitor records, and 10,626 on study permits. The scale dwarfs any other recent special measure. The table sets out the figures with the dates they reflect.

| CUAET measure | Figure | As of |
|---|---|---|
| Applications received | 1,189,326 | April 2, 2024 |
| Applications approved | 962,612 (82.2%) | April 2, 2024 |
| People confirmed in Canada | 298,301 | May 31, 2024 |
| On work permits | 239,912 | May 31, 2024 |
| On visitor records | 45,597 | May 31, 2024 |
| On study permits | 10,626 | May 31, 2024 |
| Permanent-residence applications received | 25,465 | May 31, 2025 |

These are operational figures that IRCC rounds and updates over time, so treat them as the official snapshot rather than a live count.

## Were CUAET extensions ended in 2026?

Short answer: No, they were renewed. A common belief is that the CUAET extensions stopped on March 31, 2026. They did not. On March 31, 2026, IRCC announced a new temporary public policy, effective April 1, 2026, that extended the work-permit measure rather than closing it. Eligible Ukrainians can now apply to extend or renew their open work permit until March 31, 2027, for a permit valid up to three years. The deadline that many expected to be the end became a one-year renewal instead. IRCC set out the change in its [March 2026 work-permit announcement](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/2026/03/canada-extends-certain-work-permit-measures-for-ukrainians.html).

## Who can still extend a CUAET work permit, and until when?

Short answer: Those already in Canada under the measures, until March 31, 2027. To extend or renew your open work permit, you generally need to have arrived in Canada on or before March 31, 2024, hold valid temporary resident status, and hold a valid open work permit when you apply. People who were approved but allowed to arrive by December 31, 2024 are also included. Applications are made online, standard fees now apply, and a permit can be issued for up to three years depending on your passport validity. If your current permit expires while IRCC processes the extension, maintained status lets you keep working under the same conditions until a decision is made. The steps are on the IRCC [extend your open work permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/ukraine-measures/open-work-permit-extension.html) page.

## Is there a CUAET permanent residence pathway?

Short answer: There are family-reunification permanent-residence streams, plus the general programs. CUAET was always a temporary measure, not a direct route to permanent residence. Canada created family-reunification permanent-residence pathways for Ukrainian nationals, and IRCC data shows 25,465 such permanent-residence applications received as of May 31, 2025. Beyond those streams, Ukrainians in Canada use the same permanent-residence programs as other skilled workers, mainly Express Entry and the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP). Canadian work experience built on a CUAET permit can strengthen an [Express Entry profile](/news/how-to-improve-crs-score). Because the work-permit extensions are temporary, plan the permanent-residence step early. IRCC describes the main economic route on its [Express Entry](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry.html) page.

## What happened to the free fees and settlement services?

Short answer: They ended in 2024 and 2025. The fee exemptions that made CUAET work and study permits free ended on December 31, 2024, so standard application fees now apply to extensions and new permits. The free settlement services that CUAET arrivals could access ended on March 31, 2025. The core support that remains is the ability to extend an open work permit until March 31, 2027. Budget for the standard fees when you plan an extension, because the fee-free phase is over.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CUAET

These are the questions Ukrainians in Canada ask most often. In short: CUAET closed to new applicants in 2023, the work-permit extensions run to March 31, 2027, and permanent residence runs through family-reunification streams or the general economic programs.

**Will CUAET be extended?** The work-permit measure was extended on March 31, 2026 and now runs to March 31, 2027. IRCC has not announced anything beyond that date, so confirm the current deadline on the official pages before you rely on it.

**Will Canada extend a work permit in 2026?** Yes for eligible Ukrainians. If you arrived under the measures and meet the conditions, you can apply to extend your open work permit until March 31, 2027, for up to three years.

**Is there a CUAET to permanent residence pathway?** There is no automatic CUAET-to-permanent-residence conversion. Canada runs family-reunification permanent-residence streams for Ukrainians, and the general Express Entry and provincial programs are open to those who qualify.

**Is Canada still accepting new Ukrainian refugees under CUAET?** No. CUAET stopped accepting new applications on July 15, 2023. People outside Canada now use the regular immigration and refugee programs.

## How can a licensed immigration consultant help with a CUAET extension or permanent residence?

Short answer: By timing the extension correctly and finding the permanent route that fits. Go Far Global is a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm in Toronto, regulated by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC). We help Ukrainians extend their open work permit before the March 31, 2027 deadline, keep status while the application is processed, and assess whether a family-reunification stream, Express Entry, or a provincial program is the realistic permanent-residence path. [Book a consultation](/book) to plan the next step.

*This article is general information, not legal advice. Immigration rules and deadlines change. Confirm the current rules for your situation with a licensed RCIC and on the official IRCC website before you act.*

# Canada H-1B Visa: Work Permit Options for H-1B Holders (2026)

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/canada-h1b-visa-work-permit-options-2026
Category: News
Published: 2026-06-25
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Canada does not have an H-1B visa.

*As of June 25, 2026.*

Canada does not have an H-1B visa. The H-1B is a United States work visa, and the phrase "Canada H-1B visa" usually points to the open work permit Canada offered H-1B holders in 2023, which closed within a day of opening. That program is no longer accepting applications, and interest has surged again because the United States added a US$100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions in September 2025. This guide explains what happened to Canada's H-1B work permit, whether it will return, and the routes that are open to H-1B holders right now.

> Who this is for: H-1B visa holders in the United States who are weighing a move to Canada, and Canadian employers who want to hire them.

## Is there a Canada H-1B visa?

Short answer: No. Canada has no visa called the H-1B. The H-1B is a United States specialty-occupation work visa issued by United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). When people search for a "Canada H-1B visa," they usually mean one of two things: the special open work permit Canada ran for H-1B holders in 2023, or the general Canadian work permits and permanent-residence programs a skilled worker can use to move north. Both are covered below. The short version is that Canada admits skilled workers through work permits and the Express Entry permanent-residence system, not through an H-1B equivalent.

## Is Canada's H-1B work permit still open?

Short answer: No, it closed in 2023. On July 16, 2023, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) launched a special open work permit for H-1B visa holders, valid for up to three years, with study or work permits available to accompanying family members. IRCC set a cap of 10,000 principal-applicant applications, and that cap was reached on July 17, 2023, one day after launch. The program has not reopened. According to IRCC data released under the Access to Information Act (request A-2025-73938), this measure and its related family public policy ran at roughly a 96 percent approval rate, with processing times of about 159 to 173 days. People who already hold the permit can still apply to extend it. IRCC sets out the closed program on its [H-1B visa holder work permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/special-instructions/h1b.html) page.

## What sparked the renewed interest in 2026?

Short answer: A large new United States fee on H-1B petitions. On September 19, 2025, the United States issued a presidential proclamation, "Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers," that added a US$100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions for workers outside the United States, effective September 21, 2025. USCIS later clarified that the fee applies to new petitions only, not to extensions, renewals, or petitions filed before September 21, and that it is set to last 12 months unless extended. The cost and uncertainty pushed many H-1B holders and their employers to look north, which is why searches for a "Canada H-1B visa" climbed sharply through late 2025. The United States position is set out on the [USCIS H-1B FAQ](https://www.uscis.gov/newsroom/alerts/h-1b-faq).

## Will Canada reopen the H-1B pathway in 2026?

Short answer: An accelerated pathway is planned, but it is not open yet. Canada committed in its 2025 federal budget to launch an accelerated work permit pathway for H-1B holders, as part of a broader strategy to attract global technology talent. As of June 2026, IRCC has not opened that pathway or published its eligibility rules, an application date, or a cap. Treat any "apply now" claim about it with caution, and confirm the status on official IRCC pages before you act. Until it opens, the routes in the next section are the real options for moving to Canada.

## What are the current options for H-1B holders to move to Canada?

Short answer: Several work-permit and permanent-residence routes are open right now. The right one depends on your employer, your occupation, and whether you want a temporary work permit or permanent residence. A Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) is a labour-market test that some work permits require, and the table notes where it applies. The Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities (TEER) categories rank occupations by skill level, with TEER 0 and 1 covering management and degree-level roles.

| Route | Who it fits | LMIA needed? | Speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intra-Company Transfer (ICT) | Your US employer has a Canadian parent, branch, affiliate, or subsidiary | No, LMIA-exempt | Work permit, often weeks |
| Global Talent Stream | High-skill workers in TEER 0 or 1 with a Canadian job offer in an eligible occupation | Yes, but expedited | Two-week target for the work permit |
| Express Entry | Skilled workers seeking permanent residence, with or without a job offer | No | Months, points-based |
| Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) | Workers a province selects, often in technology | Varies | Months |
| [Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) professional](/news/tn-visa-canada-cusma-professional-work-permit-2026) | Mexican citizens who hold an H-1B and work in a covered profession | No | Work permit, often weeks |

Each route has its own eligibility rules, and many H-1B holders qualify for more than one. The fastest temporary options are usually the [Intra-Company Transfer](/news/intra-company-transfer-work-permit-canada-2026) for a move within the same company, and the Global Talent Stream for a new Canadian employer.

## How does the Global Talent Stream work for H-1B holders?

Short answer: It is Canada's fast lane for skilled technology hires. The Global Talent Stream, part of the Global Skills Strategy, lets eligible employers hire high-skill foreign workers with a two-week processing target for the work permit. It is built for occupations on the Global Talent Occupations List, which is dominated by technology and engineering roles, and for unique, specialized talent referred by a designated partner. For an H-1B holder who has a Canadian job offer in a qualifying role, this is often the quickest way to start working in Canada. IRCC explains the employer and worker requirements on its [Global Skills Strategy](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/special-instructions/global-skills-strategy.html) page.

## Can H-1B holders get Canadian permanent residence?

Short answer: Yes, mainly through Express Entry and the provinces. Express Entry manages applications for the Federal Skilled Worker Program, the Canadian Experience Class, and the Federal Skilled Trades Program. It scores candidates on age, education, language, and work experience, and many H-1B holders score well because they are educated and experienced in skilled occupations. Canadian work experience and a valid job offer can raise that score. Provincial Nominee Programs add another route, with several provinces running technology-focused streams. Canada has also signalled a streamlined permanent-residence transition for a large group of work permit holders across 2026 and 2027, though the rules for H-1B holders specifically are not yet confirmed. Plan the permanent-residence step early, because a work permit is usually the bridge, not the destination.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Canada H-1B Visa

These are the questions H-1B holders raise most often when they look at Canada. The core point holds: Canada has no H-1B visa, the 2023 work permit is closed, and an accelerated pathway is planned but not yet open.

**Will Canada open its H-1B work permit again?** Canada has committed to an accelerated work permit pathway for H-1B holders, but as of June 2026 it is not open and IRCC has not released eligibility rules or a start date. Watch the official IRCC pages for the launch rather than third-party "apply now" pages.

**What is the $100,000 H-1B rule?** It is a United States fee, not a Canadian one. A September 2025 US proclamation added a US$100,000 charge on new H-1B petitions for workers abroad, which is part of why interest in Canada rose.

**Is Canada inviting H-1B visa holders?** Canada has said it wants to attract global technology talent, including H-1B holders. For now that interest runs through the existing work-permit and Express Entry routes, not a dedicated open intake.

**Does the Canada H-1B visa have a cost?** There is no Canadian H-1B visa, so there is no H-1B fee in Canada. You pay the standard Canadian work-permit or permanent-residence fees for whichever route you use.

## How can a licensed immigration consultant help an H-1B holder move to Canada?

Short answer: By matching you to the route you actually qualify for. Go Far Global is a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm in Toronto, regulated by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC). We assess whether an Intra-Company Transfer, the Global Talent Stream, Express Entry, or a provincial program is the fastest fit for your job and your goals, and we help you steer clear of the "apply now" traps around a pathway that has not opened. [Book a consultation](/book) to map your options.

*This article is general information, not legal advice. Immigration rules change, and both the United States fee and Canada's planned pathway are still developing. Confirm the current rules for your situation with a licensed RCIC and on the official IRCC website before you act.*

# Changing Schools on a Study Permit in Canada: 2026 Rules for International Students

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/changing-schools-study-permit-canada-2026
Category: News
Published: 2026-06-24
Author: Go Far Global Team

> International students in Canada must get a new study permit before changing to a new school, and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) tightened how it enforces that rule in June 2026.

International students in Canada must get a new study permit before changing to a new school, and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) tightened how it enforces that rule in June 2026. Since November 8, 2024, you can no longer switch designated learning institutions (DLIs) on the same study permit. On June 18, 2026, IRCC updated its instructions on assessing study permit conditions, clarifying the consequences of an unauthorized transfer and narrowing how it treats program changes made within the same school.

*As of June 23, 2026.*

If you are planning to move to a different college or university, the order of steps now matters: you apply first, get approved, and only then start at the new school. Doing it the other way around can put your status and your future applications at risk.

## What are the rules for changing schools on a study permit in 2026?

Since November 8, 2024, an international student inside Canada cannot change designated learning institutions (DLIs) on the same study permit. To move to a new school, you must apply for a new study permit, submitted as a study permit extension if you are already in Canada, and receive approval before you begin studying at the new DLI. The school you are moving to must be on IRCC's DLI list. IRCC sets out this process on its [changing your school or program](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/change-schools.html) page, which it last updated in June 2026.

## What changed for school transfers on June 18, 2026?

On June 18, 2026, IRCC updated the program delivery instructions its officers use to assess study permit conditions. The update clarified how the department handles unauthorized transfers between DLIs, and it narrowed how officers assess program changes made within the same school. In plain terms, officers are now looking more closely at whether a student actually held the correct study permit for the institution they are attending. The change does not alter the core rule from November 2024; it sharpens enforcement of it, so students who moved or are planning to move should make sure their permit matches their current DLI.

## Can an international student change schools in Canada?

Yes, but you must get a new study permit first. The process is to apply to extend your study permit with the new school's details before you start studying there. Your application includes a Letter of Acceptance (LOA) from the new DLI and, where the province requires one, a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL). You should confirm the new school is on the [DLI list](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada.html) before committing, because only a designated learning institution can support a study permit. Until your new permit is approved, you are authorized to study only at the DLI named on your current permit.

## Do I need a new study permit to change my program at the same school?

Changing your program at the same DLI generally does not require a new study permit. In that case you update your information in your IRCC secure account rather than filing a new application. The June 18, 2026 update narrowed how IRCC assesses these within-school changes, so the safest approach is to keep records showing you stayed at the same designated learning institution and to review IRCC's current guidance before assuming a program switch needs no action. The distinction that matters most is institution versus program: a new institution needs a new permit, while a new program at the same institution usually does not.

## What documents do I need to transfer to a new DLI?

The documents you need depend on whether you are switching institutions, switching programs at the same school, or studying in Quebec, because each situation triggers a different requirement. A move to a new designated learning institution is the one that always requires a fresh study permit before you start. The table below summarizes the three common situations.

| Situation | What you need |
|---|---|
| Changing to a new DLI (inside Canada) | New study permit (filed as an extension) + Letter of Acceptance from the new DLI + Provincial Attestation Letter where required |
| Changing program at the same DLI | Update your IRCC account; generally no new permit |
| Studying in Quebec | A Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) in addition to the study permit |

Apply with the complete set of documents for your situation so an officer can confirm your new school and program before approving the permit.

## What happens if I switch schools without a new study permit?

Studying at a new designated learning institution before your new study permit is approved counts as unauthorized study. Breaching the conditions on your study permit can put you out of status, and it can affect future immigration applications and your eligibility for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP). IRCC lists the [conditions on your study permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/while-you-study.html) on canada.ca, including the requirement to study at the institution named on your permit. If your application is still pending, do not start at the new school until you receive the approval.

## How long does a study permit transfer take?

A study permit extension to change schools is processed like other in-Canada study permit applications, and processing times change throughout the year, so check IRCC's current estimate before you plan a start date. Apply as early as you can once you have your new Letter of Acceptance. If you submit a complete application before your current permit expires, you generally keep studying under maintained status, but only at your existing DLI, until IRCC makes a decision. You can apply through IRCC's [extend or change the conditions of your study permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/extend-study-permit.html) process. For a step-by-step walkthrough of the extension itself, see our guide to [extending a study permit in Canada](/news/extend-study-permit-canada-2026).

## Common Questions: Do You Need a New Study Permit to Change Schools?

These are the questions students raise most often about transfers under the current rules. The core rule has not changed since November 2024, but the June 2026 enforcement update makes following the steps in order more important than ever.

**What are the new rules for international students changing schools?** You need a new study permit before you can study at a new DLI; you can no longer transfer on your existing permit.

**Can I transfer schools as an international student?** Yes, by applying to extend your study permit with the new school's Letter of Acceptance and waiting for approval before you start.

**I am a student in Canada changing my DLI, what do I file?** Inside Canada, you submit a study permit extension that names the new designated learning institution.

## Sources

- [Changing your school or program, Canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/change-schools.html)
- [Study in Canada as an international student, Canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada.html)
- [Conditions on your study permit, Canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/while-you-study.html)
- [Extend or change the conditions of your study permit, Canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/extend-study-permit.html)

# BOWP Without an AOR: PNP vs Manitoba Bridge 2026

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/pnp-work-permit-without-aor-2026
Category: News
Published: 2026-06-24
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Provincial nominees in Canada can now apply for a work permit without an Acknowledgement of Receipt (AOR), under a temporary measure that Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC)...

# Work Permit Without an AOR for Provincial Nominees, 2026

*As of September 3, 2026.* A provincial nomination does not let you work in Canada. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) still wants a work permit while a permanent residence file is in process. A bridging open work permit (BOWP) for Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) applicants requires your acknowledgement of receipt (AOR) letter. The live exception is a Manitoba-only open work permit tied to a provincial support letter, not a nationwide "no AOR" switch.

## TL;DR

PNP nomination is not a work permit | BOWP for PNP: live in Canada outside Quebec, principal applicant, complete PR file, AOR letter, no employment restriction on the nomination | Manitoba Workforce Transition Bridge: support letter on or before December 31, 2025, employed in Manitoba, apply before December 31, 2027 | Spouse open work permit without AOR is family class only, and only if status expires in 2 weeks or less | Work permit fee $155. Open work permit holder fee $100

## Can I apply for a work permit without an AOR?

**Short answer:** For a PNP [bridging open work permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/pr-work-permits/bridging.html), no. IRCC requires the AOR letter it sends after it gets your permanent residence application. That is true if you applied for the PNP through Express Entry (after the completeness check) and if you applied not through Express Entry (after the eligibility assessment). You also need to be the principal applicant, live in Canada and intend to live outside Quebec, hold valid worker status or be eligible to restore, and have no employment restrictions as a condition of the nomination. Upload the AOR and, for PNP, the nomination letter. Submitting an Express Entry profile is not a permanent residence application and does not create a BOWP.

The [non-Express Entry after you apply](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees/non-express-entry/after-apply.html) page is blunt: "A provincial nomination doesn't mean you can work in Canada. You still need to apply for a work permit if you want to work while we process your permanent residence application."

One official path does not use a PR AOR. The [Manitoba Workforce Transition Bridge](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/foreign-workers/open-work-permits-province-territory.html) temporary public policy, in effect July 6, 2026, lets IRCC issue an open work permit to a person who has a Manitoba open work permit support letter issued on or before December 31, 2025 showing they were screened and placed in Manitoba's Expression of Interest pool on or before that date, plus an employment letter from a current Manitoba employer. Apply before the policy expires on December 31, 2027. A 2026 "continued support" letter does not replace the 2025 support letter. Alberta and Yukon files under the old expired policies are not eligible. The older public policy that covered Alberta, Manitoba, and Yukon closed: Alberta letters had to be issued on or before December 31, 2024, and Yukon and Manitoba letters on or before December 31, 2025. The new bridge is Manitoba only, because Manitoba signed a Letter of Intent with IRCC. You must have valid temporary resident status, maintained status, or a restoration application. You can leave Canada while the open work permit is pending, but you must be in Canada with status, or have applied to restore, when IRCC decides.

| Path | AOR required? | What IRCC actually asks for |
|---|---|---|
| PNP BOWP (Express Entry) | Yes | Complete PR application, completeness check, AOR, nomination letter, live in Canada outside Quebec |
| PNP BOWP (not Express Entry) | Yes | Complete PR application, eligibility assessment, AOR, nomination letter, live in Canada outside Quebec |
| Manitoba Workforce Transition Bridge | No PR AOR | Manitoba support letter on or before December 31, 2025, employed in Manitoba, apply by December 31, 2027 |
| Spouse / common-law partner open work permit | Usually yes | AOR for the family-class PR file. Narrow exception if your status expires in 2 weeks or less |

Do not mix this with the [spouse open work permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html) page. That without-AOR rule is for a spouse, common-law, or conjugal partner in the family class or the spouse or common-law partner in Canada class, not for PNP.

## How to extend a work permit without an aor?

**Short answer:** If you do not have an AOR yet, you are not in the BOWP lane. IRCC's Express Entry BOWP instructions say: if you are not eligible for a BOWP yet, do not let the work permit expire while you wait for an invitation to apply. Maintain status by [extending your work permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/guide-5553-applying-change-conditions-extend-your-stay-canada-worker.html). Your employer may need a new Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) or a new offer of employment. Pay the work permit fee on the [IRCC fee list](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/fees.asp): $155 per person. An open work permit also needs the $100 open work permit holder fee. Restoration as a worker, if you already lost status, is listed as $401.25 (restore $246.25 plus a new $155 permit).

The Manitoba bridge is the other official extend-without-PR-AOR route, and only if you already hold that 2025 Manitoba support letter and you are employed in Manitoba. Cohort 1 is a valid permit at application. Cohort 2 is an expired permit. Cohort 3 is authorization to work without a permit under paragraph 186(u) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations. IRCC employees' instructions say applications after December 31, 2027, including renewals, will be refused.

If your PNP nomination restricts you to one employer, a BOWP is not available. Stay on an employer-specific permit until that condition is gone. Read the nomination letter before you file.

## How long does it take to receive aor from IRCC for PNP?

**Short answer:** IRCC does not publish a separate "AOR weeks" clock. On the [after you apply](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees/non-express-entry/after-apply.html) page (date modified August 4, 2026), IRCC says it checks that the application is complete, the fee is paid, and the documents are included. If the file is incomplete, IRCC rejects it and refunds the processing fees. If it is complete, IRCC sends an AOR that includes your application number. After the AOR, you can [check status](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-status.html) with that number. Biometrics, if you are 14 to 79, are a later letter: 30 days from the date of that letter to give fingerprints and a photo. Use [check processing times](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html) for the permanent residence line that matches your stream. That tool is not an AOR timer.

Incomplete forms, unpaid biometrics, a withdrawn nomination, or a plan to live outside the nominating province delay the file. Tell IRCC about address, family, and representative changes through the web form. Guessing "two weeks for AOR" from a forum is not a source.

## Can I apply for a work permit after receiving an aor?

**Short answer:** Yes, if you also meet the rest of the BOWP tests. The AOR is the document IRCC tells you to upload in the "Client information" field. For PNP you also upload the nomination letter. Choose "Open work permit" as the type. Pay $155 plus the $100 open work permit holder fee. Apply online in most cases. You must live in Canada when you apply and intend to live outside Quebec. You can leave Canada while the BOWP is processing, but if the old permit expires while you are outside, you cannot work until the new one is approved.

The AOR is necessary. It is not sufficient. No employment restriction on the nomination. Principal applicant only. Complete PR application, not just a profile in a pool. If the nomination is employer-specific, use an extension that matches that job, not a BOWP.

## Can I get a work permit while waiting for PR?

**Short answer:** Yes, through a work permit that fits your facts. A PNP nomination is not that permit. After AOR, many in-Canada PNP principal applicants use a BOWP. Before AOR, extend the permit you have, restore if you lost status, or, if you are a Manitoba candidate with a 2025 support letter and a Manitoba job, use the Workforce Transition Bridge. Some physicians with a provincial support letter can ask for faster work-permit processing. That faster lane is on the same after-you-apply page. It is not a BOWP waiver.

We are Go Far Global, a licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) firm. If your permit is about to expire and the AOR is still missing, [book a consultation](/book) before you guess a public policy. See [provincial nominee](/immigration/provincial-nominee), [work permit](/immigration/work-permit), [Express Entry](/immigration/express-entry), [family immigration](/immigration/family-immigration) for the spouse lane, and [processing times](/immigration/processing-times). More explainers sit under [news](/news).
