# In-Demand Jobs Canada 2026: NOC Codes, Express Entry Categories, and Provincial Lists

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/in-demand-jobs-canada-2026
Category: Immigration
Published: 2026-05-24
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Acronyms used in this guide: NOC (National Occupational Classification), TEER (Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities), IRCC (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship...

# In-Demand Jobs Canada 2026: NOC Codes, Express Entry Categories, and Provincial Lists

*As of May 24, 2026.*

*Acronyms used in this guide: NOC (National Occupational Classification), TEER (Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities), IRCC (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada), ESDC (Employment and Social Development Canada), CRS (Comprehensive Ranking System), PNP (Provincial Nominee Program), CEC (Canadian Experience Class), FSW (Federal Skilled Worker), FSTP (Federal Skilled Trades Program), LMIA (Labour Market Impact Assessment), STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics), NCLC (Niveaux de Compétence Linguistique Canadiens), CICC (College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants).*

If you are planning to immigrate to Canada and want to maximize your odds, the single most useful question is not "what's a good job?" but "what are the in-demand jobs in Canada that the government actively prioritizes for immigration in 2026?" The answer comes from three official sources: IRCC's [Express Entry category-based draws](/immigration/express-entry/category-based-draws), Provincial Nominee Program in-demand lists, and Job Bank's National Occupational Outlook ratings. This guide walks through what's actually on those lists, the NOC codes that get drawn most often, and how to align your immigration application with where Canada has genuine labour shortages.

Written by Rami Mamar, RCIC-IRB (License #R515110), regulated by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants.

## What Does "In-Demand" Mean in Canadian Immigration?

> **Short answer:** An "in-demand" occupation in 2026 is one that meets at least one of three criteria: it appears on IRCC's category-based Express Entry draw lists (healthcare, STEM, skilled trades, transport, French speakers, foreign medical doctors, researchers/senior managers, agriculture/agri-food, military personnel), it appears on a province's published nominee program priority list, or it is rated "Shortage" or "Outlook 3" on the Job Bank Occupational Outlook for your province. These three sources do not always agree, which is why immigration strategy depends on understanding all three.

The three lists serve different purposes:

| Source | Maintained by | Updates | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Express Entry category-based draws** | IRCC | Annual category list with periodic draws | CRS-eligible Express Entry profiles in specific NOCs |
| **Provincial Nominee Program priority lists** | Each province | Quarterly to annually | PNP nomination eligibility (provinces choose their own priorities) |
| **Job Bank National Occupational Outlook** | ESDC | Twice yearly | LMIA priority processing, labour market trend data, provincial planning |

An occupation that appears on all three lists (registered nurses, for example) is unambiguously in demand and offers the strongest immigration pathway. An occupation that appears on only one (long-haul truck drivers, in the new 2026 Transport Express Entry category but not most provincial PNP lists) still offers a strong path but only through that specific stream.

## What Are the 2026 Express Entry Category-Based Draws?

> **Short answer:** For 2026, IRCC runs Express Entry category-based draws across nine targeted categories: Healthcare, STEM (including a dedicated cybersecurity sub-category), Skilled Trades, Transport, French speakers, Foreign Medical Doctors with Canadian work experience, Researchers and Senior Managers, Agriculture and Agri-Food, and Military Personnel. The first four (Healthcare, STEM, Trades, French) carried over from 2025; the rest were added or expanded for 2026. The minimum work experience requirement increased from 6 to 12 months for most categories.

IRCC announced the 2026 category-based draw expansion in early 2026 ([category-based selection at canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/rounds-invitations/category-based-selection.html)) ([IRCC category-based selection on canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/rounds-invitations/category-based-selection.html)), building on the 2023 launch of the program. The full list of categories and their key eligibility criteria:

| Category | Minimum Canadian/foreign work experience required | First 2026 draw |
|---|---|---|
| Healthcare and Social Services | 12 months in TEER 0/1/2/3 healthcare NOC | Q1 2026 |
| STEM Occupations | 12 months in TEER 0/1/2/3 STEM NOC | Q1 2026 |
| Skilled Trades | 12 months in trades NOC | Q1 2026 |
| French Language Proficiency (NCLC 7+) | None occupation-specific | Continuous (most frequent) |
| Transport Occupations | 12 months in transport NOC | Q1 2026 (new) |
| Foreign Medical Doctors with Canadian Work Experience | 12 months as a physician in Canada | February 20, 2026 (first draw) |
| Researchers and Senior Managers with Canadian Work Experience | 12 months in eligible role | Q1 2026 (new) |
| Agriculture and Agri-Food | 12 months in eligible NOC | Q2 2026 (new) |
| Highly Skilled Foreign Military Personnel | 12 months military service in eligible role | Q2 2026 (new) |

Category-based draws typically clear at lower CRS scores than general Express Entry draws (the French category routinely cleared at 365 to 400 in 2025 and 2026, while general draws cleared at 485 to 520). The lower CRS thresholds are the main reason category-based draws are highly valuable for applicants who otherwise would not be invited.

For our complete coverage of these categories, see [Express Entry Category-Based Draw 2026: New Categories and Increased Work Requirements](/news/express-entry-category-based-draw-2026-new-categories).

Canada has documented healthcare staffing shortages and the category-based draws clear at CRS scores of approximately 430 to 460 for most healthcare professionals.

The healthcare NOC codes eligible for 2026 Express Entry category draws (per [IRCC Express Entry rounds on canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/ministerial-instructions/express-entry-rounds.html)):

## Which STEM Occupations Qualify for Express Entry in 2026?

> **Short answer:** The 2026 STEM category includes engineers, software developers, data scientists, mathematicians, statisticians, actuaries, cybersecurity specialists (added as a sub-category in late 2024), database analysts, web developers, and several physical and life sciences occupations. CRS cut-offs for STEM draws typically run 450 to 480, with the cybersecurity sub-category sometimes drawing slightly lower.

The STEM NOC codes eligible for 2026 Express Entry category draws (per [IRCC category eligibility lists](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply.html)):

| NOC | Occupation | TEER |
|---|---|---|
| 21100 | Physicists and astronomers | 1 |
| 21101 | Chemists | 1 |
| 21102 | Geoscientists and oceanographers | 1 |
| 21110 | Biologists and related scientists | 1 |
| 21200 | Architects | 1 |
| 21210 | Mathematicians, statisticians and actuaries | 1 |
| 21211 | Data scientists | 1 |
| 21220 | Cybersecurity specialists | 1 |
| 21221 | Business systems specialists | 1 |
| 21222 | Information systems specialists | 1 |
| 21223 | Database analysts and data administrators | 1 |
| 21230 | Computer systems developers and programmers | 1 |
| 21231 | Software engineers and designers (alternate listing) | 1 |
| 21232 | Software engineers and designers | 1 |
| 21233 | Web designers | 1 |
| 21234 | Web developers and programmers | 1 |
| 21300 | Civil engineers | 1 |
| 21301 | Mechanical engineers | 1 |
| 21310 | Electrical and electronics engineers | 1 |
| 21311 | Computer engineers (except software engineers and designers) | 1 |
| 21321 | Industrial and manufacturing engineers | 1 |
| 21330 | Mining engineers | 1 |
| 21399 | Other professional engineers | 1 |

The dedicated cybersecurity sub-category (NOC 21220) was a 2024-2025 addition reflecting Canada's documented cybersecurity workforce gap. Cybersecurity workers with relevant certifications (CISSP, CISM, CEH, SANS GIAC) routinely receive faster invitations than general STEM applicants because of the targeted draw frequency.

## Which Skilled Trades Qualify for Express Entry in 2026?

> **Short answer:** The 2026 Skilled Trades category targets construction trades (electricians, plumbers, carpenters, bricklayers, welders), industrial trades (millwrights, industrial mechanics, machinists), and select transport-related trades. Cooks were removed from the trades category effective 2026 (they were eligible in 2025). CRS cut-offs typically run 440 to 470.

Trades NOC codes eligible for 2026 category-based draws (per [IRCC Federal Skilled Trades Program eligibility](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-trades.html)):

| NOC | Occupation | TEER |
|---|---|---|

Trades workers must have at least 12 months of full-time work experience to qualify for the 2026 category. The Federal Skilled Trades Program (FSTP) requires 2 years of full-time experience for federal economic immigration.

## What Transport Occupations Qualify for the New 2026 Express Entry Category?

> **Short answer:** IRCC added the Transport category for 2026 in response to documented driver shortages, particularly long-haul truck drivers and aircraft maintenance engineers. The category covers commercial pilots, aircraft maintenance engineers, transportation safety inspectors, air traffic controllers, and certain truck driving roles. CRS cut-offs are expected to clear in the 440 to 480 range based on initial 2026 draws.

Transport NOC codes eligible for the 2026 category-based draws:

| NOC | Occupation | TEER |
|---|---|---|
| 72404 | Heavy-duty equipment mechanics (transport-relevant subset) | 2 |
| 72405 | Railway carmen/women | 2 |
| 72406 | Aircraft mechanics and aircraft inspectors | 2 |
| 73300 | Transport truck drivers | 3 |
| 73310 | Heavy equipment operators | 3 |
| 73311 | Railway and motor transport labourers | 3 |
| 75100 | Aircraft pilots, flight engineers and flying instructors | 1 |
| 75101 | Air traffic controllers and related occupations | 1 |
| 75102 | Deck officers, water transport | 1 |
| 75103 | Engineer officers, water transport | 1 |
| 75104 | Railway traffic controllers and marine traffic regulators | 1 |
| 75200 | Air pilots, flight engineers and flying instructors (alternate listing) | 1 |

The truck driving sub-category (NOC 73300) is the highest-volume occupation in the Transport category. Canada has documented a shortage of more than 25,000 long-haul truck drivers based on Trucking HR Canada reports ([ESDC labour market data at canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development.html)), which is the underlying labour-market data IRCC used to justify the new category.

## Who Qualifies for the 2026 Foreign Medical Doctors Express Entry Category?

> **Short answer:** IRCC created a new dedicated Express Entry category for 2026 targeting foreign-trained physicians who have already worked in Canada. To qualify, you must hold a medical degree recognized by a provincial medical regulatory body, have at least 12 months of work experience as a physician in Canada, and meet standard Express Entry requirements. The first draw is scheduled for February 20, 2026.

The eligible NOCs for the Foreign Medical Doctors category (per [IRCC Express Entry rounds on canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/ministerial-instructions/express-entry-rounds.html)):

| NOC | Occupation | TEER |
|---|---|---|
| 30010 | Specialists in surgery | 1 |
| 30011 | Specialists in medicine | 1 |
| 31100 | Specialists in clinical and laboratory medicine | 1 |
| 31101 | Specialists in psychiatry and addiction medicine | 1 |
| 31102 | General practitioners and family physicians | 1 |

The category addresses a long-running problem: foreign-trained doctors come to Canada through other immigration streams, struggle to navigate provincial licensing, and end up working in non-medical roles while Canada has documented physician shortages. The new category-based draw targets doctors who have already cleared provincial licensing and are working as physicians in Canada; IRCC wants to convert their temporary status to permanent residence quickly.

## Who Qualifies for the 2026 Researchers and Senior Managers Category?

> **Short answer:** This new 2026 category targets foreign nationals who have already worked in research roles or senior management positions in Canada. The category includes research scientists and managers in STEM fields, senior managers across financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, and engineering, plus academic researchers with industry experience. Candidates must demonstrate 12 months of relevant Canadian work experience.

Eligible NOCs include:

| NOC | Occupation | TEER |
|---|---|---|
| 00010 | Senior managers; financial, communications and other business services | 0 |
| 00011 | Senior managers; health, education, social and community services | 0 |
| 00012 | Senior managers; trade, broadcasting and other services | 0 |
| 00013 | Senior managers; public administration | 0 |
| 00014 | Senior managers; production goods, utilities, transportation and construction | 0 |
| 00015 | Senior managers; agriculture, natural resources, fisheries and engineering | 0 |
| 10010 | Financial managers | 0 |
| 10011 | Human resources managers | 0 |
| 10019 | Other administrative services managers | 0 |
| 10020 | Insurance, real estate and financial brokerage managers | 0 |
| 10021 | Banking, credit and other investment managers | 0 |
| 10022 | Advertising, marketing and public relations managers | 0 |
| 41200 | University professors and lecturers | 1 |
| 41201 | Post-secondary teaching and research assistants | 1 |

This category reflects IRCC's intent to retain high-earning, established professionals who have already demonstrated economic contribution in Canada.

## How Does the Express Entry French-Language Category Work?

> **Short answer:** The Express Entry French Language category targets candidates who demonstrate NCLC 7 or higher in all four French abilities (listening, speaking, reading, writing). It is the most frequent category-based draw, with CRS thresholds historically as low as 336 in 2025 and consistently 50-100+ points below general draws. The category supports federal Francophone immigration targets that escalate to 10.5% of total PR admissions by 2028.

The French category does not have occupation requirements. Any Express Entry candidate meeting:
- NCLC 7 minimum in all four abilities (TEF Canada or TCF Canada)
- Otherwise standard Express Entry eligibility (TEER 0/1/2/3 work experience, education, ECA)

...qualifies for the French-language draw.

The category accommodates immigration from West Africa (Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon), Maghreb (Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria), parts of Europe (France, Belgium, Switzerland), and bilingual immigrants from other countries. For Canadian context, see our [French Test for Canada Immigration guide](/news/learning-french-immigration) and the dedicated [Francophone Mobility Program article](/news/francophone-mobility-program).

## Who Qualifies for the 2026 Agriculture and Agri-Food Express Entry Category?

> **Short answer:** The agriculture and agri-food category addresses labour shortages in food production, meat processing, harvesting, and related occupations. Eligible NOCs span specialist agricultural workers, agri-food industrial occupations, and certain technical roles in food processing. The category complements the Agri-Food Pilot which targets specific employer-driven applications.

Agriculture and agri-food NOC codes eligible for 2026 category draws:

| NOC | Occupation | TEER |
|---|---|---|
| 63100 | Butchers; retail and wholesale | 3 |
| 63201 | Bakers | 3 |
| 65200 | Food and beverage servers | 4 |
| 82030 | Agricultural service contractors and supervisors | 2 |
| 84120 | Specialized livestock workers and farm machinery operators | 3 |
| 85100 | Livestock labourers | 5 |
| 85101 | Harvesting labourers | 5 |
| 85103 | Aquaculture and marine harvest labourers | 5 |
| 94140 | Industrial butchers and meat cutters, poultry preparers and related workers | 3 |
| 94141 | Fish and seafood plant workers | 4 |

The TEER 4 and 5 inclusions are notable because most Express Entry categories exclude these levels. The Agriculture category accepts them because labour shortages in seasonal and processing work are documented in StatCan and Job Bank data and the federal Levels Plan specifically allocates 10,000+ admissions to caregiver and agriculture pilots.

## Who Qualifies for the 2026 Foreign Military Personnel Express Entry Category?

> **Short answer:** This unique 2026 category targets foreign military personnel recruited by the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF). Eligible roles include military medical doctors, military nurses with specialized training, and military pilots with relevant certifications. The category supports CAF's recruitment objectives and recognizes that military training transfers strong skills to civilian roles.

Eligible occupations include selected NOCs across healthcare and aviation tied to military experience, with specific licensing/certification requirements aligned to CAF roles. The category is smaller in volume than healthcare or STEM but offers a clean pathway for foreign military applicants who otherwise might not qualify for standard streams.

## Which Jobs Are In-Demand for Provincial Nominee Programs?

> **Short answer:** Each PNP publishes its own priority occupation list (see [IRCC provincial nominee program overview](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html)), refreshed quarterly or annually. The lists overlap heavily with Express Entry categories (healthcare, trades, tech) but include province-specific gaps: Ontario emphasizes manufacturing and construction, British Columbia focuses on healthcare and tech, Alberta covers energy and rural occupations, Saskatchewan added technology to its priority list in 2026, and Manitoba removed hospitality from its Temporary Resident Retention Pilot.

Below are summarized 2026 PNP priorities by province. Always verify against the current provincial website before applying; these lists change throughout the year.

### Ontario (OINP)

Active streams: Master's Graduate, PhD Graduate, Employer Job Offer (Foreign Worker, In-Demand Skills, International Student), Skilled Trades. The Human Capital Priorities, French-Speaking Skilled Worker, and Express Entry Skilled Trades streams remained suspended through most of 2026.

Tech NOCs targeted by Ontario:
- 21232 Software engineers and designers
- 21230 Computer systems developers and programmers
- 21220 Cybersecurity specialists
- 21223 Database analysts and data administrators
- 21211 Data scientists

In-Demand Skills (NOC TEER 4 streams) include agriculture, construction, food processing labourers.

### British Columbia (BC PNP)

Active streams: Skilled Worker, International Graduate, Entry Level and Semi-Skilled (closed April 23, 2026), International Post-Graduate (closed January 7, 2026), Healthcare Professional, Tech (closed December 2024).

Priorities through 2026: Healthcare (31 eligible occupations including all RN/LPN sub-categories), Construction trades (9 eligible occupations including electricians, plumbers, carpenters), Childcare workers.

### Alberta (AAIP)

Active streams: Opportunity Stream, Dedicated Health Care Pathway (500 reserved spaces), Express Entry Stream for Priority Sectors (construction, manufacturing, aviation, agriculture; 600 reserved spaces), Rural Renewal Stream, Tourism and Hospitality Stream.

Alberta added a $135 CAD Worker Expression of Interest (WEOI) fee effective April 7, 2026.

### Saskatchewan (SINP)

Active streams: International Skilled Worker (Express Entry, Occupations In-Demand), Saskatchewan Experience, Entrepreneur, Farm Owner-Operator, International Worker.

Saskatchewan added **technology** to its priority sectors for 2026 (it was not on the 2025 list). Priority sectors: healthcare, technology, agriculture, skilled trades, mining, manufacturing, energy.

A new eligibility restriction effective 2026: PGWP holders who studied outside Saskatchewan and worked in their field for fewer than 6 months are barred from Saskatchewan Experience pathways.

### Manitoba (MPNP)

Active streams: Skilled Worker in Manitoba, Skilled Worker Overseas, International Education Stream, Business Investor Stream.

Manitoba's largest 2026 change (February 4): Hospitality and Food Services sectors removed from the Temporary Resident Retention Pilot. In their place, 16 new skilled trades occupations were added. See our [Manitoba MPNP 2026 coverage](/immigration/provincial-nominee) for the full breakdown.

### Atlantic Provinces

Nova Scotia consolidated 10 separate streams into 4 effective February 18, 2026: Nova Scotia Graduate, Skilled Worker, Entrepreneur, Nova Scotia Express Entry.

The Atlantic Immigration Program (AIP) remains the employer-driven pathway across all four Atlantic provinces with no points test.

### Quebec

Quebec operates separately from PNP. Quebec Skilled Worker (PSTQ) and Quebec Experience Program (PEQ) select candidates based on Quebec-specific criteria with French language proficiency weighted heavily. Quebec announces its priority occupations through its annual Plan Régulateur.

## What Are Job Bank's Occupational Outlook Ratings?

> **Short answer:** [Job Bank publishes an "Outlook" rating for every NOC in every province on canada.ca](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis) on a 3-star scale: 1 star (Limited; Surplus), 2 stars (Fair; Balanced), 3 stars (Good; Shortage). The 3-star ratings indicate where Canada has documented labour shortages and are the underlying data IRCC uses to justify category-based draws and provinces use for PNP priority lists.

Look up the outlook for any NOC at ESDC's [Job Bank trend analysis on canada.ca](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis), which feeds IRCC's category-based draw decisions(https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis). The tool returns:

- **Star rating** (1-3 stars) for the NOC in your province
- **Job openings forecast** (3-year projection)
- **Job seekers forecast** (3-year projection)
- **Shortage/surplus assessment** based on the gap
- **Prevailing wage** (low, median, high)

Occupations consistently rated 3-star (shortage) across most provinces in 2025-2026:

- Registered nurses (NOC 31301)
- Nurse practitioners (NOC 31302)
- Family physicians (NOC 31102)
- Long-haul truck drivers (NOC 73300)
- Construction electricians (NOC 72200)
- Construction managers (NOC 70010)
- Welders (NOC 72500)
- Heavy-duty equipment mechanics (NOC 72401)
- Early childhood educators (NOC 42202)
- Cybersecurity specialists (NOC 21220)
- Software engineers (NOC 21232)
- Bus drivers (NOC 73301)
- Personal support workers (NOC 33102, classified as Nurse aides)

Occupations consistently rated 1-star (surplus) in many provinces:

- General office support clerks (TEER 4)
- Retail salespersons in saturated markets
- Tour and travel guides (TEER 5)
- Certain media/communications roles in declining sectors

The Job Bank rating is not legally binding for immigration eligibility, but it does drive ESDC's LMIA processing priorities. Files in 3-star occupations receive faster handling than 1-star occupations.

## What Salaries Do In-Demand Canadian Jobs Pay?

> **Short answer:** In-demand status does not always equate to high pay. Long-haul truck drivers (NOC 73300, 3-star shortage in most provinces) earn $55,000-75,000; early childhood educators (NOC 42202, 3-star shortage in many provinces) earn $35,000-48,000; software engineers (NOC 21232) earn $85,000-115,000+. The salary you can expect depends on the specific occupation, not just whether it's in demand.

Approximate 2026 salary ranges for in-demand occupations (full annual breakdowns are in our [Average Salary in Canada 2026 article](/news/average-salary-canada-2026)):

| In-demand occupation | TEER | Approximate 2026 median annual wage |
|---|---|---|
| Family physicians | 1 | $250,000+ |
| Software engineers | 1 | $85,000-115,000 |
| Cybersecurity specialists | 1 | $90,000-120,000 |
| Data scientists | 1 | $85,000-110,000 |
| Registered nurses | 1 | $75,000-95,000 |
| Pharmacists | 1 | $95,000-115,000 |
| Construction electricians | 2 | $60,000-85,000 |
| Plumbers | 2 | $58,000-82,000 |
| Welders | 2 | $55,000-75,000 |
| Heavy-duty equipment mechanics | 2 | $65,000-90,000 |
| Long-haul truck drivers | 3 | $55,000-75,000 |
| Personal support workers / nurse aides | 3 | $40,000-50,000 |
| Early childhood educators | 3 | $35,000-48,000 |
| Harvesting labourers | 5 | $32,000-40,000 |

A common mistake we see is applicants choosing the "easiest" in-demand pathway (truck driving or PSW) without realizing the salary trade-offs. If your goal is high earning potential, the in-demand healthcare and STEM categories are stronger. If your goal is fastest immigration regardless of starting wage, the TEER 3 in-demand categories (truck driving, PSW, ECE) offer clean paths but lower starting income.

## How Should I Pick an Immigration Pathway Based on In-Demand Lists?

> **Short answer:** Match your existing occupation against the three lists in order of immigration value: first check Express Entry category eligibility, then check Provincial Nominee Program priorities for your target province, then check Job Bank shortage ratings as a third confirmation. If your occupation appears on all three, you have the strongest pathway; if it appears on only one, focus on that single stream.

The decision workflow we use with clients:

1. **Find your NOC code** using the lookup process in our [NOC Code Canada 2026 guide](/news/noc-code-canada-2026).
2. **Check Express Entry category eligibility.** Does your NOC appear on a 2026 category list? If yes, optimize your Express Entry profile for that category-based draw.
3. **Check provincial priority lists** for your target province at the relevant provincial nominee program website.
4. **Look up the Job Bank Occupational Outlook** for your NOC and province. A 3-star shortage rating supports both Express Entry category eligibility and PNP nomination.
5. **Verify your prevailing wage** in your target province at [jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis/search-wages](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis/search-wages).
6. **Calculate your CRS score** using a CRS calculator to see if you're within range of recent draws.
7. **Pick your strongest pathway** based on the combination: highest-volume in-demand list, lowest CRS cutoff in the relevant category, fastest provincial processing.

For most applicants, the best 2026 paths are (in rough order):

1. Express Entry French-language category (if you can hit NCLC 7); clears at very low CRS scores
2. Healthcare category-based draw (if you're an RN, LPN, doctor, or pharmacist); clears around 430-460
3. STEM category-based draw with cybersecurity sub-category; clears around 450-480
4. Skilled Trades category-based draw; clears around 440-470
5. Provincial Nominee Program in your occupation/province; 600 CRS bonus virtually guarantees ITA
6. Transport occupations category (new 2026); early draws clearing at favorable CRS
7. Canadian Experience Class with Canadian work experience already accumulated; clears around 507-515

## What Are the Most Common Mistakes Picking an In-Demand Job?

> **Short answer:** The four most common in-demand-job mistakes are picking a TEER 4/5 occupation without realizing Express Entry excludes those levels, assuming "in-demand" automatically means high CRS scores, confusing federal Express Entry categories with provincial in-demand lists, and ignoring the 12-month work experience requirement that increased from 6 months for 2026 categories.

In rough order of frequency:

1. **Choosing a TEER 4 or 5 occupation expecting it to count for Express Entry.** Truck drivers (NOC 73300) is TEER 3 and works for Express Entry; bus drivers (NOC 73301) is TEER 4 and does not work for federal economic streams. Always check TEER level before committing.
2. **Assuming "in-demand" means automatic invitation.** In-demand status reduces competition (lower CRS thresholds for category-based draws) but you still need to meet the CRS minimum and have a complete profile. A 380-CRS profile in a high-demand category may still not be invited.
3. **Confusing federal and provincial in-demand lists.** Software engineers are on the federal STEM category and Ontario's OINP tech list; you can pursue both pathways in parallel. Truck drivers are on the federal Transport category but on Saskatchewan's targeted SINP stream specifically; picking the wrong path costs months.
4. **Missing the 12-month work experience increase.** For 2026, most category-based draws require 12 months (up from 6 months). Applicants with 6-11 months are not eligible; they must wait or pursue alternative streams.

For more on common application mistakes, see [How to Improve Your CRS Score 2026](/news/how-to-improve-crs-score-2026) and [GCMS Notes: How to Read Them and Use Them](/news/gcms-notes-canada-immigration-guide).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What jobs are most in demand in Canada in 2026?

The most consistently in-demand jobs are: registered nurses, family physicians, software engineers, cybersecurity specialists, construction electricians, long-haul truck drivers, welders, early childhood educators, heavy-duty equipment mechanics, and personal support workers. All appear on either the federal Express Entry category list, provincial PNP priorities, or both, with 3-star Job Bank shortage ratings across most provinces.

### Which jobs qualify for Express Entry category-based draws in 2026?

Nine categories: Healthcare and Social Services, STEM (with cybersecurity sub-category), Skilled Trades, French-language proficiency, Transport Occupations, Foreign Medical Doctors with Canadian work experience, Researchers and Senior Managers, Agriculture and Agri-Food, and Highly Skilled Foreign Military Personnel.

### Are truck drivers in demand in Canada?

Yes. Long-haul truck drivers (NOC 73300) have a documented shortage of 25,000+ workers per Trucking HR Canada. NOC 73300 is TEER 3 and qualifies for Express Entry (FSW, CEC) and the new 2026 Transport category-based draws. Saskatchewan offers a dedicated International Truck Driver stream.

### What is the minimum CRS score for the healthcare category in 2026?

Healthcare category-based Express Entry draws have historically cut off at 430-460 CRS in 2025-2026. The exact cutoff varies per draw based on volume and IRCC targets. Check our [latest Express Entry draws coverage](/news/ircc-draws) for current cutoffs.

### Do I need a job offer to qualify for in-demand category draws?

No, not for category-based Express Entry draws specifically. The category eligibility is based on your NOC, work experience years, and language scores. However, a valid job offer can boost your CRS score under the Federal High-Skilled Class proposal (taking effect late 2027 or 2028) where job offer points return for high-wage tier occupations.

### How do I find provincial in-demand lists?

Each provincial nominee program publishes its current priority list (see [IRCC PNP overview on canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/provincial-nominees.html)) on its official website. Provincial sites are listed at canada.ca's PNP page (search "provincial nominee program" + your target province name).

### What is Job Bank's Occupational Outlook?

A 3-star rating system that ESDC publishes for every NOC in every province. 3-star = shortage (high in-demand), 2-star = balanced, 1-star = surplus. Look up your NOC at [jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis).

### Can I qualify for multiple in-demand categories?

Yes. If your NOC appears on multiple lists (e.g., NOC 31301 RNs appears on Healthcare Express Entry category, Ontario OINP, BC PNP, AAIP, Manitoba MPNP, Saskatchewan SINP), you can submit Express Entry profile and multiple PNP applications in parallel. The first one that yields an ITA or nomination becomes your active pathway.

### What was added to the in-demand list for 2026?

New 2026 categories: Foreign Medical Doctors with Canadian Work Experience (first draw February 20, 2026), Researchers and Senior Managers, Transport Occupations, Agriculture and Agri-Food (expanded), Highly Skilled Foreign Military Personnel. The cybersecurity sub-category within STEM was clarified. The minimum work experience requirement increased from 6 months to 12 months for most categories.

### What was removed from the in-demand list for 2026?

Cooks (NOC 62200) were removed from the Express Entry Skilled Trades category for 2026 (they were eligible in 2025). Manitoba removed Hospitality and Food Services from its Temporary Resident Retention Pilot effective February 4, 2026. Some provincial PNP streams have closed or paused in 2026 (notably Ontario's Express Entry-aligned streams remained suspended, BC Entry Level and Semi-Skilled closed April 23, 2026).

## What Are the Next Steps to Apply Using In-Demand Job Data?

If you're planning a Canadian immigration application in 2026, the highest-leverage action is matching your occupation to the in-demand lists that actually drive eligibility and processing speed.

The verification workflow we recommend:

1. **Find your exact NOC code** using the process in our [NOC Code Canada 2026 guide](/news/noc-code-canada-2026).
2. **Check Express Entry category-based draws** at the IRCC category-based draw page on canada.ca to see if your NOC appears.
3. **Cross-reference provincial nominee program lists** for the province you want to live in.
4. **Look up Job Bank's Outlook rating** for your NOC in that province.
5. **Look up the prevailing wage** so you understand realistic year-1 earnings.
6. **Run your CRS score** with the CRS calculator to confirm you can clear current draw cutoffs.

If your occupation is missing from the lists you want, the most common pivots are: (1) gain Canadian work experience under a TR pathway then transition to CEC; (2) target a French-language credential to access the French category; (3) shift to a province whose PNP includes your NOC.

For a written assessment of your specific profile against 2026 in-demand pathways, [book a consultation with our RCIC team](/appointment). We typically map out the strongest stream within a 30-minute review.

For broader 2026 immigration strategy, see our [Express Entry Category-Based Draw 2026 article](/news/express-entry-category-based-draw-2026-new-categories), [Canada Immigration Levels Plan 2026 to 2028](/news/canada-immigration-levels-plan-2026), [How to Improve Your CRS Score 2026](/news/how-to-improve-crs-score-2026), and the [Federal High-Skilled Class proposal](/news/canadian-experience-class-ending-federal-high-skilled-class).

# Average Salary in Canada 2026: $1,344 a Week in June (StatCan)

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/average-salary-canada-2026
Category: Settlement
Published: 2026-05-24
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Acronyms used in this guide: NOC (National Occupational Classification), TEER (Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities), CRS (Comprehensive Ranking System), IRCC...

# Average Salary in Canada 2026: $1,344 a Week in June (StatCan)

*As of August 31, 2026.*

Statistics Canada released June 2026 payroll earnings on 27 August 2026. Average weekly earnings for all employees in Canada, including overtime, were CAD $1,343.86, up 3.4% from a year earlier. That is the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours (SEPH) figure, seasonally adjusted, from table 14-10-0223-01. It is not a promise of what you will earn, and it is not the same as a median. This guide uses that release, then explains how salary numbers show up in immigration files.

## TL;DR

Canada's average weekly earnings in June 2026 were CAD $1,343.86, up 3.4% year over year | Alberta ($1,387.44) and Ontario ($1,383.94) led the provinces | Nunavut was highest among territories at $1,883.29 | Average weekly hours were 33.4 | Multiply $1,343.86 by 52 and you get about $69,881, but that is a rough annualization of a weekly all-employee average, not a full-time contract salary | Job Bank prevailing wages, not this average, are what officers use for many work permit and Express Entry job-offer questions

## What is the average salary in Canada in 2026?

**Short answer:** The latest Statistics Canada payroll number is CAD $1,343.86 a week in June 2026, including overtime, for all employees, seasonally adjusted. The agency rounded the year-over-year story to $1,344, up 3.4%. Month over month, weekly earnings were up 0.6% in June. Average weekly hours worked were 33.4 hours, little changed from a year earlier. The source is The Daily, [Payroll employment, earnings and hours, and job vacancies, June 2026](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/260827/dq260827b-eng.htm), released 27 August 2026, citing table [14-10-0223-01](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1410022301).

SEPH counts employees who received pay and benefits from an employer. It excludes the self-employed, owners of unincorporated businesses, and agricultural employees. Earnings are gross taxable payroll before deductions. A change in the average can come from wage changes, overtime, hours, or a shift in who is employed, not only from raises.

## What is the difference between average and median salary?

**Short answer:** The SEPH number above is an average (mean) of weekly earnings. High earners pull it up. A median (the middle worker) is usually lower. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) does not grade your Express Entry profile on the national average. Job offers are compared with occupation-specific wages, often using Job Bank prevailing wage for the National Occupational Classification (NOC) code and region.

If you are using salary to decide where to settle, compare the weekly figure with [cost of living](/tools/cost-of-living) in that city. A higher average in Alberta does not automatically mean more leftover money than in Quebec after rent.

## What is the average weekly pay by province and territory?

**Short answer:** In June 2026, Alberta led the provinces at CAD $1,387.44 a week, then Ontario at $1,383.94, then British Columbia at $1,351.02. Prince Edward Island was the lowest province at $1,193.19. Among territories, Nunavut was highest at $1,883.29. All figures are SEPH average weekly earnings including overtime, from the same Daily release.

| Geography | Average weekly earnings, June 2026 | 12-month change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Canada | $1,343.86 | +3.4% |
| Nunavut | $1,883.29 | +6.1% |
| Northwest Territories | $1,705.04 | -1.3% |
| Yukon | $1,502.89 | +0.3% |
| Alberta | $1,387.44 | +1.9% |
| Ontario | $1,383.94 | +3.9% |
| British Columbia | $1,351.02 | +3.7% |
| Saskatchewan | $1,306.71 | +3.5% |
| Newfoundland and Labrador | $1,302.07 | +2.0% |
| Quebec | $1,291.91 | +2.7% |
| New Brunswick | $1,246.25 | +4.4% |
| Nova Scotia | $1,229.95 | +6.8% |
| Manitoba | $1,210.66 | +3.3% |
| Prince Edward Island | $1,193.19 | +3.1% |

Nova Scotia had the largest provincial year-over-year increase (+6.8%). The Northwest Territories was the only geography in this table with a year-over-year decline (-1.3%).

## How should you turn weekly earnings into an annual number?

**Short answer:** A common shortcut is weekly earnings times 52. For the Canada figure that is about CAD $69,881. Treat that as an illustration, not your offer letter. SEPH averages include part-time employees and overtime. Average hours were 33.4 a week, which is not a 40-hour full-time contract. A full-time job in your NOC can sit well above or below that annualized average.

If an employer quotes an hourly wage, multiply by the hours in the contract, not by 33.4. If you need the number for a settlement budget, use the provincial row, then subtract rent and tax using a local [cost of living](/tools/cost-of-living) check.

## How does salary show up in a Canadian immigration application?

**Short answer:** IRCC does not ask "is your wage equal to the national average." It asks whether the job and the wage match the program rules. For many work permits and for Express Entry job-offer points, that means the prevailing wage for the NOC and region, plus a genuine job. High-wage streams and some provincial nominee program (PNP) grids also use wage cut-offs that are not the SEPH Canada average.

Use this article to understand the labour market you are walking into. Use Job Bank and the offer letter for the number that goes on the form. For Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) points, run the [CRS calculator](/tools/crs-calculator). For the permit itself, start at [work permits](/immigration/work-permit). A Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) file, when one is required, lives or dies on the offered wage versus the prevailing wage, not versus $1,344 a week.

## What else did StatCan say about jobs in June 2026?

**Short answer:** Payroll employment was little changed in June (+4,800). Job vacancies edged up to 509,100. The job vacancy rate was 2.8%. There were 2.9 unemployed people per vacancy. Construction and public administration added payroll jobs. Manufacturing, accommodation and food services, and retail declined that month. Those details are in the same [Daily release](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/260827/dq260827b-eng.htm).

Vacancies were up year over year in manufacturing, retail, professional, scientific and technical services, and mining and oil and gas. They were down in educational services and information and cultural industries. British Columbia had the highest provincial vacancy rate in that release (3.2%). None of that replaces an occupation-specific wage lookup.

## How do you look up the prevailing wage for your NOC?

**Short answer:** Go to Job Bank, look up the NOC, pick the region, and read the prevailing wage band. That is the figure employers and officers use. The SEPH Canada average is a background statistic. It will not save an offer that sits under the Job Bank prevailing wage for that occupation.

If you are comparing cities, pair the provincial weekly earnings row with rent. Ontario's $1,383.94 a week is not take-home pay in Toronto. Run the numbers through [cost of living](/tools/cost-of-living) before you treat a provincial average as a raise.

## What questions do people ask about average salary in Canada?

**Short answer:** They want one number. StatCan's latest payroll average is $1,343.86 a week in June 2026. Your job will not pay that number unless it happens to.

### What is the average salary in Canada right now?

CAD $1,343.86 a week in June 2026, SEPH, including overtime, all employees, seasonally adjusted, released 27 August 2026.

### What is the average salary in Ontario in 2026?

CAD $1,383.94 a week in June 2026, same survey and release.

### Is that a yearly salary of $70,000?

$1,343.86 times 52 is about $69,881. That annualization is a shortcut. It includes part-time workers and overtime and uses 33.4 average hours.

A Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) can tell you whether an offer wage meets the program, not whether it matches the national average. [Book a consultation](/book) if the offer is the immigration document.

# NOC Code Canada 2026: Complete TEER Lookup, Immigration Eligibility, and How to Find Your Occupation Code

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/noc-code-canada-2026
Category: Immigration
Published: 2026-05-24
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Acronyms used in this guide: NOC (National Occupational Classification), TEER (Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities), IRCC (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship...

# NOC Code Canada 2026: Complete TEER Lookup, Immigration Eligibility, and How to Find Your Occupation Code

*As of June 24, 2026.*

*Acronyms used in this guide: NOC (National Occupational Classification), TEER (Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities), IRCC (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada), ESDC (Employment and Social Development Canada), CRS (Comprehensive Ranking System), PNP (Provincial Nominee Program), CEC (Canadian Experience Class), FSW (Federal Skilled Worker), FST (Federal Skilled Trades), LMIA (Labour Market Impact Assessment), PGWP (Post-Graduation Work Permit), CLB (Canadian Language Benchmark), ECA (Educational Credential Assessment), CICC (College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants).*

Every Canadian work permit, Express Entry profile, Provincial Nominee Program application, and Post-Graduation Work Permit decision rides on one identifier: the **National Occupational Classification (NOC) code** that you assign to your job. Choose the wrong code and your file gets refused or returned. Choose the right code and you unlock category-based draws, faster processing, and PNP streams you might otherwise miss.

Statistics Canada and Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) maintain the official National Occupational Classification (NOC) system. The current version is **NOC 2021 (National Occupational Classification 2021) Version 2.0**, effective November 21, 2024 (see the [ESDC NOC site](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca)). This guide walks through what NOC codes are, how the TEER system works, how to look up your code, the most-searched immigration NOCs with their TEER levels, and the eligibility rules that flow from them.

Written by Rami Mamar, RCIC-IRB (License #R515110), regulated by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants.

## What Is a NOC Code and Why Does It Matter for Canadian Immigration?

> **Short answer:** A NOC code is a 5-digit identifier that classifies your job into one of about 500 occupational categories. The taxonomy uses a TEER (Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities) classification ranging from 0 (management) to 5 (no formal training required) under Canada's National Occupational Classification system. Every Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) and ESDC immigration program; Express Entry, PNPs, PGWP language requirements, LMIA wage floors, category-based draws; uses your NOC code to determine eligibility, skill level, and required documentation.

The NOC is jointly maintained by **Statistics Canada** and **Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC)**. It is the official taxonomy for every job in the Canadian labour market. The federal government uses it to publish labour-market statistics ([Statistics Canada labour data](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/subjects/labour)), to set [minimum wage rates for foreign workers via ESDC](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/foreign-workers/median-wage.html), and to determine immigration eligibility.

For immigration applicants, the NOC code does three things:

1. **It determines your skill level** (the TEER category, explained below).
2. **It controls which immigration programs you qualify for.** Express Entry, for example, requires work experience in TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3. TEER 4 and 5 work generally does not qualify for federal economic streams (limited exceptions exist in some PNPs).
3. **It triggers category-based draws.** Express Entry category draws (healthcare, STEM, skilled trades, transport, French speakers, foreign medical doctors, agriculture, and military personnel for 2026) are defined by specific NOC code lists.

Choosing the wrong NOC is one of the most common causes of refusal (see [IRCC NOC guidance on canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/eligibility/find-national-occupation-code.html)) we see in our Toronto office. A "Project Coordinator" can sit under TEER 1 (NOC 10010 Senior managers, financial, communications) or TEER 3 (NOC 13100 Administrative officers) depending on actual duties. Same job title; very different immigration outcomes.

## How Are NOC Codes Structured?

> **Short answer:** Each NOC code is exactly 5 digits ([NOC 2021 v2.0 structure on noc.esdc.gc.ca](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Structure/Matrix)). The first digit identifies the broad occupational category (0 through 9), the second digit identifies the TEER level (0 through 5), and the last three digits identify the specific occupation within that group. For example, **NOC 21232 Software engineers and designers**: broad category 2 (natural and applied sciences), TEER 1 (university degree), specific occupation 232.

The full structure under NOC 2021:

| Position | What it represents | Range |
|----|---|---|
| 1st digit | Broad occupational category | 0 to 9 |
| 2nd digit | TEER level | 0 to 5 |
| 3rd digit | Major group | 0 to 9 |
| 4th digit | Sub-major group | 0 to 9 |
| 5th digit | Unit group (specific occupation) | 0 to 9 |

The 10 broad categories (first digit) under NOC 2021:

| First digit | Broad occupational category |
|---|---|
| 0 | Legislative and senior management occupations |
| 1 | Business, finance and administration occupations |
| 2 | Natural and applied sciences and related occupations |
| 3 | Health occupations |
| 4 | Occupations in education, law and social, community and government services |
| 5 | Occupations in art, culture, recreation and sport |
| 6 | Sales and service occupations |
| 7 | Trades, transport and equipment operators and related occupations |
| 8 | Natural resources, agriculture and related production occupations |
| 9 | Occupations in manufacturing and utilities |

**Important change from NOC 2016 to NOC 2021:** The old system used 4-digit codes with skill levels (0, A, B, C, D). NOC 2021 introduced 5-digit codes and replaced skill levels with TEER. If you have any application or document referencing a 4-digit NOC (e.g., 2173 instead of 21232), it is using the old NOC 2016 system. IRCC accepted NOC 2016 references through November 16, 2022, then transitioned to NOC 2021 thereafter.

The Government of Canada maintains the authoritative NOC structure at [noc.esdc.gc.ca/Structure/Matrix](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Structure/Matrix). Always cross-reference your assumed code against the official matrix before submitting any immigration application.

## What Is the TEER System and How Does It Work?

> **Short answer:** TEER stands for **Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities** ([NOC structure documentation](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Structure/Hierarchy)). It replaced the old A/B/C/D skill levels in NOC 2021. Six TEER categories run from 0 (managerial) to 5 (no formal qualification needed). Immigration programs use TEER level to determine eligibility, language requirements, and processing pathways.

| TEER | Typical education / training required | Example occupations |
|----|---|---|
| **TEER 0** | Management occupations, broad knowledge and authority | Senior managers, restaurant managers (NOC 60030), construction managers (NOC 70010) |
| **TEER 1** | Completion of a university degree (bachelor's, master's, or doctorate) | Software engineers (NOC 21232), physicians (NOC 31100), accountants (NOC 11100), registered nurses (NOC 31301) |
| **TEER 2** | College diploma or apprenticeship training of 2+ years, OR supervisory roles | Computer network technicians (NOC 22220), electricians (NOC 72200), executive assistants (NOC 13110), licensed practical nurses (NOC 32101) |
| **TEER 3** | College diploma or apprenticeship training of less than 2 years, OR more than 6 months of on-the-job training | Long-haul truck drivers (NOC 73300), early childhood educators (NOC 42202), chefs (NOC 62200) |
| **TEER 4** | Completion of secondary school AND/OR several weeks of job-specific training | Retail salespersons (NOC 64100), home child care providers (NOC 44100), bus drivers (NOC 73301) |
| **TEER 5** | Short work demonstration with no formal educational requirement | Cleaners (NOC 65310), agricultural and harvest labourers (NOC 85101), food service counter attendants (NOC 65201) |

The TEER level is the second digit of your 5-digit NOC code. **NOC 21232** is TEER 1 (the "1" is the second digit). **NOC 64100** is TEER 4. This is the fastest way to read TEER from any NOC code at a glance. The phrase TEER code commonly refers to this second digit; strictly speaking it is the TEER level inside your NOC code, not a separate code.

The previous skill-level system mapped to TEER as follows:

| NOC 2016 skill level | NOC 2021 TEER |
|---|---|
| 0 (management) | TEER 0 |
| A (university) | TEER 1 |
| B (college / apprenticeship 2+ years OR supervisory) | TEER 2 or TEER 3 (split) |
| C (secondary plus on-the-job training) | TEER 4 |
| D (no formal training) | TEER 5 |

The biggest practical change is that the old "Skill Level B" was **split** into TEER 2 (longer training) and TEER 3 (shorter training). Some occupations that were skill-level B under NOC 2016 are now TEER 3 under NOC 2021, which changes their immigration eligibility under specific programs.

## How Do I Find My NOC Code?

> **Short answer:** Use the official [NOC Search tool](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Search/AdvancedSearch) maintained by ESDC or browse the NOC matrix at [noc.esdc.gc.ca](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca). Search by job title, browse by category, or look up by old NOC 2016 code via the concordance table. Then verify your assumed code against the official lead statement and main duties for that NOC unit group.

### Step 1: Start with Job Bank's NOC Search

The Government of Canada provides a free occupation search at [noc.esdc.gc.ca](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Search/AdvancedSearch). Enter your job title (in English or French) and the tool returns matching NOC codes ranked by relevance.

For example, searching "data analyst" returns NOC 21223 (Database analysts and data administrators, TEER 1) as the top match.

### Step 2: Read the Lead Statement and Main Duties

For every NOC unit group, the ESDC site publishes:

- **Lead statement**; one paragraph describing what people in this occupation do
- **Example titles**; the job titles commonly used for this occupation in industry
- **Main duties**; bulleted list of the typical responsibilities
- **Employment requirements**; typical education, certification, or experience required
- **Additional information**; career mobility notes, related occupations

Your actual job duties must match the **main duties** of the NOC you claim. Not just your title; the actual day-to-day work. This is the single most important verification step. If the main duties for NOC 21232 (Software engineers and designers) say things like "design and develop software solutions" and "evaluate, recommend, and implement software systems," and your real job is configuring SharePoint sites, you are not a software engineer. You might be NOC 22220 (Computer network technicians) or NOC 22221 (User support technicians) instead.

### Step 3: Cross-Reference Against the Official Matrix

The full NOC 2021 v2.0 structure is at [noc.esdc.gc.ca/Structure/Matrix](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Structure/Matrix). The matrix shows every unit group organized by broad category and TEER level. Use it to see related occupations and pick the best fit.

### Step 4: If You're Migrating from NOC 2016, Use the Concordance Table

If your old immigration application, ECA report, or employment record references a 4-digit NOC 2016 code, ESDC publishes a [concordance table](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Versions/VersionsOfTheNOC) that maps old codes to new ones. For example:

- NOC 2016 **2173** (Software engineers and designers) → NOC 2021 **21232** (same)
- NOC 2016 **3012** (Registered nurses) → NOC 2021 **31301** (same)
- NOC 2016 **0631** (Restaurant managers) → NOC 2021 **60030** (Restaurant and food service managers)

### Step 5: Confirm via the Job Bank's Occupational Outlook

Job Bank also publishes labour-market outlooks per NOC, with employment trends, prevailing wages by province, and skill shortage indicators. See [jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis). This is also where you'll find the "balanced," "shortage," or "surplus" rating that drives provincial in-demand lists.

## Which TEER Levels Qualify for Express Entry?

> **Short answer:** Express Entry requires work experience in TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3. TEER 4 and 5 work generally does not qualify for any federal economic stream. Within Express Entry, the three programs (FSW, CEC, FSTP) each have specific TEER and experience rules. Note that IRCC plans to retire FSW, CEC, and FSTP and replace them with a unified Federal High-Skilled Class in late 2027 or 2028, but current rules apply until then.

The three current Express Entry programs and their TEER eligibility:

### Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSW; eligibility at [canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/eligibility/federal-skilled-workers.html))

- **Eligible TEER:** 0, 1, 2, or 3
- **Work experience:** At least 1 year of continuous full-time (or equivalent part-time) skilled work within the past 10 years, in the same NOC
- **Where it can be earned:** Inside Canada or outside Canada
- **Language:** Minimum CLB 7 in all four abilities (listening, reading, writing, speaking)
- **Education:** Canadian secondary diploma OR foreign education with ECA showing Canadian-equivalent secondary or higher

### Canadian Experience Class (CEC; eligibility at [canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/eligibility/canadian-experience-class.html))

- **Eligible TEER:** 0, 1, 2, or 3
- **Work experience:** At least 1 year of skilled Canadian work experience in the past 3 years
- **Where it can be earned:** Canada only
- **Language:** CLB 7 for TEER 0 or 1 occupations; CLB 5 for TEER 2 or 3 occupations
- **Education:** No mandatory minimum (though education adds CRS points)

### Federal Skilled Trades Program (FSTP; eligibility at [canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/eligibility/federal-skilled-trades.html))

- **Eligible NOC:** Specific trades occupations under major groups 72, 73, 82, 83, 92, and 93 (all TEER 2 or 3 trades)
- **Work experience:** At least 2 years of full-time skilled trades work in the past 5 years
- **Job offer:** Required (or a certificate of qualification from a Canadian province or territory)
- **Language:** CLB 5 for speaking and listening; CLB 4 for reading and writing

For all three programs, claiming the wrong TEER on your work history is the fastest way to get refused. If you spent 3 years working as a TEER 4 retail supervisor but claim it as TEER 1 management experience, IRCC checks your duties against the NOC main duties and refuses for misrepresentation.

## How Does Each Provincial Nominee Program Use NOC Codes?

> **Short answer:** Each provincial nominee program has its own NOC eligibility list. Some PNPs accept TEER 4 occupations that Express Entry rejects (especially for healthcare and trades labour gaps). Always check the specific province's stream-by-stream eligibility before applying; these lists change throughout the year as provinces refine priorities.

A few illustrative examples of how PNPs treat NOC code eligibility differently from Express Entry:

| Province | Stream | TEER accepted | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **British Columbia** | BC PNP Skills Immigration | TEER 0, 1, 2, 3 + select TEER 4/5 | Healthcare and entry-level/semi-skilled categories accept some TEER 4/5 |
| **Ontario** | OINP Employer Job Offer | TEER 0, 1, 2, 3 + In-Demand Skills (TEER 4) | In-Demand Skills stream accepts specific TEER 4 NOCs in agriculture, construction, food processing |
| **Saskatchewan** | SINP Long-Haul Truck Driver | TEER 3 specifically | Targeted to NOC 73300 |
| **Manitoba** | MPNP Skilled Worker Overseas | TEER 0, 1, 2, 3 + Manitoba in-demand list | Manitoba publishes a NOC-specific in-demand list per draw |
| **New Brunswick** | NBPNP Skilled Worker | TEER 0, 1, 2, 3 | Aligned to provincial labour market needs |
| **Alberta** | AAIP Rural Renewal Stream | TEER 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (most permissive) | Specifically opens up TEER 4/5 work for rural communities |

The single biggest practical mistake we see: applicants assume that if they qualify for one PNP stream they qualify for all. A TEER 4 retail supervisor might qualify for Alberta's Rural Renewal Stream but be ineligible for BC's Skills Immigration Skilled Worker stream. Read each program's eligibility rules carefully.

For full coverage of 2026 PNP allocation changes, see our [Canada PNP 2026: 91,500 Nominations and Provincial Powers guide](/news/canada-pnp-2026-changes-91500-nominations-provincial-powers).

## How Do PGWP Language Requirements Depend on TEER Level?

> **Short answer:** Since November 1, 2024, Post-Graduation Work Permit applicants must show language proficiency at CLB 7 (for TEER 0 or 1 target occupations) or CLB 5 (for TEER 2 or 3 target occupations). The TEER of the occupation you intend to work in determines your language threshold.

This is one of the highest-impact ways your NOC code affects immigration outcomes. The November 2024 PGWP language rules:

| Target occupation TEER | Required CLB | Equivalent IELTS General (each band) |
|---|---|---|
| TEER 0 or 1 | CLB 7 | 6.0 |
| TEER 2 or 3 | CLB 5 | 5.0 |
| TEER 4 or 5 | N/A; PGWP can still issue but no specific TEER-tied language floor for these target jobs | N/A |

Test must be one of IELTS General Training, CELPIP General, or PTE Core, with results valid for 2 years at PGWP submission.

For complete PGWP rules including the field-of-study restrictions for college graduates (per [IRCC PGWP guidance on canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation.html)), see our [PGWP Canada 2026 guide](/news/pgwp-post-graduation-work-permit-canada-2026) and the [detailed PGWP language requirements article](/news/pgwp-language-requirements-2026).

## How Do LMIA Wage Floors Connect to Your NOC Code?

> **Short answer:** ESDC publishes a prevailing-wage table for every NOC code in every province. Your LMIA-based work permit application requires the employer to pay at least the prevailing wage for your NOC in the work location. The wage tied to your NOC code determines whether your job falls in the high-wage or low-wage LMIA stream, which carries different recruitment rules, processing timelines, and employer caps.

The high-wage versus low-wage split is set at the **provincial median hourly wage**. If the wage offered for your NOC in your work location is at or above the median, your file goes through the high-wage stream. Below the median, it goes through the low-wage stream, which carries:

- Stricter advertising requirements (8 weeks of advertising as of April 1, 2026, doubled from 4 weeks)
- Mandatory Canadian youth recruitment outreach documentation
- A workforce cap of 10% for low-wage TFWs in most provinces (15% in rural areas through March 2027)
- Mandatory transportation, housing assistance, and health insurance until provincial coverage starts

Look up your NOC's prevailing wage per province at [Job Bank's wage report tool](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis/search-wages).

For full coverage of the new April 2026 LMIA rules, see our [LMIA Changes April 2026 guide](/news/new-lmia-rules-april-2026).

## What Are the Most Common NOC Code Mistakes?

> **Short answer:** The five most common NOC mistakes are claiming a higher TEER than your actual duties support, picking by job title without reading the main duties, mixing up NOC 2016 (4-digit) and NOC 2021 (5-digit) codes, ignoring the lead statement, and assuming the same NOC code carries the same eligibility across all immigration programs. Each mistake is a documented refusal driver in our refusal-recovery practice.

In rough order of frequency at our Toronto office:

1. **Claiming a higher TEER than actual duties support.** A retail supervisor who manages 3 cashiers is typically TEER 4 (NOC 64100 or 62010), not TEER 0 (NOC 60010). IRCC checks duties against the NOC main duties. Misalignment triggers refusal and a 5-year misrepresentation ban under IRPA Section 40 is possible if IRCC concludes the misclaim was intentional.

2. **Picking the NOC by job title without reading the duties.** Two "Project Coordinator" jobs can fall under different NOCs (10010, 11202, or 13100) depending on whether the role involves managerial authority, business consulting, or general administration. Always read the main duties.

3. **Mixing NOC 2016 and NOC 2021 codes.** A four-digit code (e.g., 2173) is the old NOC 2016 system. IRCC requires NOC 2021 (five-digit) for all post-November 2022 applications. If an ECA report or employment letter cites a 4-digit code, find the NOC 2021 equivalent through the [ESDC concordance table](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Versions/VersionsOfTheNOC).

4. **Ignoring the lead statement.** Each NOC unit group has a one-paragraph lead statement describing the typical work. If your job description does not match the lead statement, the NOC is almost certainly wrong even if the title matches.

5. **Assuming one NOC carries the same eligibility everywhere.** TEER 4 NOC 64100 (Retail salespersons) does not qualify for Express Entry but may qualify for Alberta's Rural Renewal Stream. NOC 62200 (Chefs) was eligible for the 2025 Express Entry Trades category but was removed for 2026. Programs change; verify before applying.

## What Changed in NOC 2021 Version 2.0?

> **Short answer:** NOC 2021 Version 2.0 took effect November 21, 2024. It added 7 new unit groups (including dedicated codes for cybersecurity specialists and data scientists), refined definitions for several existing groups, and updated employment requirements based on labour-market input. The structural framework (5-digit codes, TEER system, 10 broad categories) is unchanged from Version 1.0.

Key v2.0 changes that matter for immigration:

- **NOC 21220 Cybersecurity specialists** was elevated to its own unit group (previously bundled with other IT roles), opening cybersecurity workers to a dedicated category in the 2026 STEM Express Entry draws.
- **NOC 21211 Data scientists** received its own unit group, providing a clear NOC for data-science roles that had been ambiguously coded under data analyst or statistician categories.
- **NOC 22220 Computer network and web technicians** consolidated two prior groups into a single unit group, simplifying the code path for IT technicians.
- Several construction trades unit groups were renamed or clarified, including a new dedicated unit group for **NOC 72601 Painters and decorators (industrial)**.
- Updated lead statements and main duties across about 30 unit groups in healthcare, technology, and skilled trades to reflect 2024 occupational realities.

IRCC accepts NOC 2021 v2.0 codes for all applications ([IRCC NOC guidance on canada.ca](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/eligibility/find-national-occupation-code.html)). Concordance between v1.0 and v2.0 is published at [noc.esdc.gc.ca](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca). If you're updating an in-flight application that used v1.0 codes, IRCC accepts either as long as the underlying occupation matches your claimed duties.

## Frequently Asked Questions About NOC Codes

### How do I find my NOC code?

Use the official [NOC Search tool](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Search/AdvancedSearch). Enter your job title in English or French, then verify the result by reading the lead statement and main duties for the suggested NOC. Your actual day-to-day work must match the main duties for the code to be correct.

### What is the difference between NOC 2016 and NOC 2021?

NOC 2016 used 4-digit codes and skill levels 0/A/B/C/D. NOC 2021 uses 5-digit codes and the TEER system (0 through 5). IRCC required all post-November 16, 2022 applications to use NOC 2021. NOC 2021 v2.0 took effect November 21, 2024 with minor refinements to specific unit groups.

### How do I know my TEER level?

The TEER level is the second digit of your 5-digit NOC code. NOC 21232 is TEER 1 (the "1" is the second digit). NOC 64100 is TEER 4.

### Is TEER 4 eligible for Express Entry?

No. Express Entry requires work experience in TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3. TEER 4 and 5 do not qualify. Some Provincial Nominee Programs (notably Alberta Rural Renewal, BC Entry Level/Semi-Skilled, Ontario In-Demand Skills) accept specific TEER 4 NOCs for targeted labour shortages.

### Does my NOC determine my CRS score?

Indirectly. Your NOC determines your eligibility for Express Entry (TEER must be 0/1/2/3) and which category-based draws you qualify for (healthcare, STEM, trades, transport, French speakers, agriculture, foreign medical doctors, researchers and senior managers, military personnel in 2026). Your specific CRS score depends on age, education, language, work experience years, and adaptability factors; but eligibility is gated by NOC and TEER.

### Can I claim multiple NOCs in my Express Entry profile?

You list each job separately with its own NOC. If you held different positions, claim them under their respective NOCs. You can also claim the highest NOC you held continuously for the required period (typically 1 year for CEC).

### How do I prove my NOC matches my job?

You submit an employment letter from each employer stating your title, dates of employment, duties, hours per week, salary, and signatory contact. The duties listed on the letter should match (but not necessarily copy verbatim) the main duties of the NOC you claim. IRCC verifies by reading the letter and calling the employer if needed.

### Are any TEER 5 occupations eligible for Canadian PR?

Generally no. Express Entry excludes TEER 5. The Caregiver Pilot programs (Home Child Care Provider Pilot, Home Support Worker Pilot) provide PR pathways for specific TEER 4 caregiver NOCs, with PR on arrival under qualifying conditions. Some agricultural and seasonal worker streams allow TEER 5 occupations to access work permits, but not direct PR through Express Entry.

### What happens if I claim the wrong NOC?

If your duties don't match the NOC main duties, IRCC refuses for either eligibility failure or misrepresentation. Misrepresentation under IRPA Section 40 carries a 5-year ban from any Canadian immigration application. Honest NOC misclassification (you genuinely believed your code was correct but officers disagreed) typically results in a procedural fairness letter and a chance to clarify before refusal.

### Where do I look up NOC prevailing wages?

[Job Bank's wage report tool](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis/search-wages) publishes low, median, and high hourly wages for every NOC in every province and territory. This is the same database ESDC uses to set LMIA wage floors and high-wage versus low-wage stream classifications.

### Do I need a separate NOC for self-employment?

Yes. For Express Entry self-employed applicants under the FSW class, your self-employment in your declared NOC must meet the same skilled-work definition (TEER 0/1/2/3, minimum 1 year). Self-employment is harder to document; you provide tax returns, business registrations, client contracts, and bank statements showing business income.

### What is the TEER code in Canada?

A TEER code is the second digit of your 5-digit National Occupational Classification (NOC) code. TEER stands for Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities, and the NOC has six TEER categories numbered 0 through 5. For federal economic permanent residence programs like Express Entry, your work experience must fall in TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 to count as skilled.

### Is TEER 3 eligible for PR?

Yes. TEER 3 work experience qualifies for Canada's federal economic permanent residence programs through Express Entry, alongside TEER 0, 1, and 2. TEER 4 and 5 work generally does not qualify for these federal streams, though some Provincial Nominee Programs accept selected TEER 4 occupations for targeted labour shortages.

### Is a PSW TEER 3 or 4?

A personal support worker, also listed as a home support worker under NOC 44101, is TEER 4 in the National Occupational Classification, not TEER 3. Because it is TEER 4, PSW experience does not qualify for Express Entry, though caregiver pilots and some Provincial Nominee Program streams provide other pathways. Confirm your exact code on the official [Government of Canada NOC search tool](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Search/AdvancedSearch).

## What Are the Next Steps to Use Your NOC Code in Immigration?

If you're preparing an Express Entry profile, a Provincial Nominee Program application, a PGWP, or an LMIA-supported work permit, your NOC code is the single most consequential identifier on your file. Get it wrong and the rest of your application falls apart.

The verification workflow that catches most errors:

1. **Search the official NOC tool** at [noc.esdc.gc.ca](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Search/AdvancedSearch) for your title.
2. **Read the lead statement and main duties** for the top suggested NOC.
3. **Compare your actual day-to-day work** against the main duties. They should match at least 70% to 80%.
4. **Check the TEER level** (second digit of the code) against your immigration program's eligibility.
5. **Verify category eligibility** if you're targeting Express Entry category-based draws.
6. **Look up the prevailing wage** at [jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis/search-wages](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/trend-analysis/search-wages) if your application involves an LMIA.

If you're uncertain after working through those steps, an RCIC review of your NOC choice typically takes 30 to 60 minutes and prevents refusals that cost months of processing and the non-refundable application fee. [Book a consultation with our team](/appointment) if you want a written assessment of your NOC selection before you submit.

For broader Express Entry strategy under 2026 rules, see our [How to Improve Your CRS Score guide](/news/how-to-improve-crs-score-2026), the [Express Entry Category-Based Draws 2026 article](/news/express-entry-category-based-draw-2026-new-categories), and the [Federal High-Skilled Class proposal](/news/canadian-experience-class-ending-federal-high-skilled-class) that will reshape the system in 2027-2028.
