# GCKey Login 2026: What It Means, How to Sign In, and What If It is Revoked

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/gckey-login-guide-2026
Category: Guides
Published: 2026-05-16
Author: Rami Mamar

> Every year, millions of people use GCKey to access Canadian immigration services online.

# GCKey Login 2026: What It Means, How to Sign In, and What If It's Revoked

*As of August 31, 2026.*

GCKey is the usual way people sign in to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) online. It is also one of the fastest ways to miss a deadline. The login loops, revoked credentials, and two-factor codes that stop a file are almost always a credential problem, not a lost application. This guide follows the official [GCKey help](https://www.canada.ca/en/government/sign-in-online-account/gckey.html) page, last updated 28 August 2026, and the [IRCC account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/account.html) pages.

## TL;DR

GCKey is a username and password, not an account, and it does not hold your immigration file | Anyone in any country can create one | You must use it at least once every two years or IRCC-style services will treat it as revoked, and a revoked GCKey cannot be recovered | Two-factor authentication uses an authenticator app or email, plus recovery codes you must save | Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) My Account is a different login (Sign-In Partner or CRA user ID), not GCKey

## What does GCKey mean, and what is it not?

**Short answer:** GCKey (Government of Canada Key) is a credential: a username and password used to sign in to federal online services that show a GCKey button. It is not an account and it does not store your study permit, work permit, or Express Entry file. The Government of Canada says so on the [GCKey help](https://www.canada.ca/en/government/sign-in-online-account/gckey.html) page. After you create GCKey, you still register separately for each service, including your IRCC secure account, so the credential is matched to that profile.

Anyone in any country can sign up. You do not need to be in Canada. You usually need only one GCKey for every federal service that accepts it, such as IRCC and My Service Canada Account. Keep track of which GCKey is linked to which service. Once a GCKey is linked to a government account, you must use that same username and password every time you sign in to that account.

## Does GCKey work for CRA My Account?

**Short answer:** No. The CRA sign-in page lists a Sign-In Partner (your bank), a CRA user ID and password, and a provincial partner for British Columbia and Alberta. It does not offer GCKey. Confirm that on [Sign in to your CRA account](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) before you try. Mixing the two logins is one of the more common support tickets we see from people who just created GCKey for IRCC and then try it on taxes.

## Should you use GCKey or a Sign-In Partner for IRCC?

**Short answer:** IRCC gives two doors into the same secure account: GCKey, or a Sign-In Partner that uses online banking from a participating Canadian bank. GCKey works worldwide. A Sign-In Partner is faster if you already bank in Canada. You cannot switch methods on an existing IRCC account. The choice is listed on [Sign in to your IRCC account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/ircc-accounts.html).

| Feature | GCKey | Sign-In Partner |
|---|---|---|
| Who can use it | Anyone worldwide | People with a participating Canadian bank login |
| Where it is set up | Government of Canada GCKey pages | Your bank's website |
| Two-factor authentication | GCKey authenticator app or email | Handled by the bank |
| If you lose access | Recover via email or recovery questions, or create a new GCKey if revoked | Contact the bank |
| Ties to your IRCC file | Linked at registration | Linked at registration |

If you are applying from Iran, the UAE, India, or anywhere without a Canadian bank login, GCKey is the path. If you already have a Canadian bank account, a Sign-In Partner skips a separate GCKey password. The government does not receive your bank balance or account number through a Sign-In Partner.

## How do you create a GCKey and an IRCC secure account?

**Short answer:** Start at the service you need, not at a random GCKey bookmark. Open the [IRCC account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/account.html) page, choose GCKey, then Sign Up. You create a unique username, a password that meets the on-screen checklist, recovery questions, a recovery email, and two-factor authentication. Save the recovery codes. Then register the IRCC secure account that actually holds your applications.

Use a current browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge). Turn JavaScript and cookies on. Do not bookmark pages you see after you sign in. Those steps are on the [GCKey help](https://www.canada.ca/en/government/sign-in-online-account/gckey.html) page under browser errors. Create the credential on a laptop if you can. Mobile browsers fail more often during signup.

You can hold more than one GCKey (work versus personal). Use a different recovery email for each one, and remember which GCKey is tied to IRCC.

## How do you sign in to IRCC with GCKey?

**Short answer:** Sign in the same way every time. On the IRCC sign-in page, choose the GCKey button, enter the username and password you used when you registered that IRCC account, continue through two-factor authentication, and you land in the secure account. If you use a different GCKey than the one you registered with, IRCC will not show your file.

The [list of Government of Canada accounts](https://www.canada.ca/en/government/sign-in-online-account.html) is the directory of services that accept GCKey. For immigration, stay on the IRCC account pages rather than a third-party "login" clone.

To check an application after you are in, use IRCC's [check application status](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-status.html) instructions. Status lives in the secure account, not in GCKey.

## What two-factor method does GCKey use?

**Short answer:** After username and password, GCKey asks you to confirm it is you. The official options are an authenticator app on a phone or desktop, or an email address. When you set that up, GCKey gives you recovery codes. Save those codes offline. If you lose the phone and the codes, the help page says you have to create a new GCKey.

If you still have the original method, sign in, complete two-factor, then use Change your two-factor authentication and save the new codes. Old codes stop working. If you lost the method, use a saved recovery code on the Recover account path, then change the method. Those steps are under [Change your GCKey two-factor authentication](https://www.canada.ca/en/government/sign-in-online-account/gckey.html).

Any modern authenticator app that generates time-based codes works. The government does not require a branded IRCC app.

## Why was my GCKey revoked, and can I get it back?

**Short answer:** No. If GCKey says your username and password have been revoked, you cannot recover that credential. You register again and, during that process, you may be able to recover the user profile or link existing applications. The two usual reasons are inactivity and a compromised password. The system requires you to use GCKey at least once every two years. That rule is on the official [revoked GCKey](https://www.canada.ca/en/government/sign-in-online-account/gckey.html) section.

If you still want GCKey after a revocation, go to the IRCC sign-in page, choose GCKey, Sign Up, and create a new username and password. Do not reuse the old password. Then re-enrol in each service. You can also revoke GCKey yourself. That cannot be undone, and you lose access to every federal service that used that credential until you re-register.

## What if you forgot the username or password?

**Short answer:** Recover from the Welcome to GCKey page of the service you are trying to use, not from a random search result. Forgot username emails the username to the recovery address you registered. Forgot password uses that email plus a recovery question, or the recovery questions and memorable person and date if you never added email. If you added no recovery email and you forgot both username and password, the help page says you create a new GCKey and register again.

Keep the recovery email unique to that GCKey. If the address is already on another GCKey, the system warns you and you either recover the old one, use a different email, or move the address (which removes it from the other GCKey).

## How should a representative handle your GCKey?

**Short answer:** Do not give your GCKey password to a consultant. A licensed representative uses IRCC's representative process, not your personal credential. Sharing the password is how accounts get revoked and how files get moved without your knowledge. Go Far Global is a licensed firm. A Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) can be appointed on the file without taking over GCKey.

If someone already has your password, change it, review the applications linked to the account, and consider whether you need a new GCKey. Then [book a consultation](/book) if the file itself needs a review.

## What questions do people ask about GCKey?

**Short answer:** The queries below are the ones that show up around this page: meaning, revoked messages, authenticator apps, and whether one GCKey covers every IRCC application.

### What does "your GCKey username and password have been previously revoked" mean?

It means that credential is dead. Create a new GCKey and re-link the IRCC account. You cannot recover the old one.

### Can I use the same GCKey for Express Entry and a work permit?

Yes, if both applications sit in the same IRCC secure account that you registered with that GCKey. Use the same sign-in path every time.

### Does GCKey expire?

Yes, through inactivity. Use it at least once every two years. A revoked GCKey is not the same as a forgotten password.

## Sources

- Government of Canada, [GCKey help](https://www.canada.ca/en/government/sign-in-online-account/gckey.html) (updated 28 August 2026)
- Government of Canada, [Sign in to an online account](https://www.canada.ca/en/government/sign-in-online-account.html)
- Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, [IRCC account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/account.html)
- Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, [Sign in to your IRCC account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/ircc-accounts.html)
- Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, [Check your application status](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-status.html)
- Canada Revenue Agency, [Sign in to your CRA account](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html)

# SIN Number Canada 2026: 9-Series Expiry, Documents, How to Apply

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/sin-number-canada-newcomer-guide-2026
Category: Guides
Published: 2026-05-16
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Applying for a SIN number in Canada takes two documents, not one: a primary document proving your status and a secondary document confirming your identity. Applying is free through every channel.

# SIN Number Canada 2026: 9-Series Expiry, Documents, How to Apply

*As of August 31, 2026.*

A Social Insurance Number (SIN) is the 9-digit identifier you need to work in Canada, get paid, file tax, and access federal programs. Service Canada issues it for free. Temporary residents get a number that starts with 9 and expires with the permit. Citizens and permanent residents get a number that does not expire. Plastic cards are gone. You get a Confirmation of SIN letter instead.

## TL;DR

A SIN is a 9-digit number. Temporary-resident numbers start with 9 and expire with the work permit, study permit, or visitor record | You need one primary document that proves status and one secondary document that confirms identity | Online applications take about 5 business days. Mail takes about 20 | You can start work as soon as you apply. You do not wait for the number to arrive | Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) emails are not accepted as permit proof

## What is a Social Insurance Number in Canada?

**Short answer:** A Social Insurance Number is a 9-digit number that Service Canada issues so you can work legally, get paid, pay tax, file a return, and use federal programs such as Employment Insurance and the Canada Pension Plan. The number is confidential. It is illegal for anyone else to use it. You are responsible for protecting it. It is not photo identification. There is no fee to apply, to confirm an existing number, or to update a record. Service Canada no longer issues plastic cards. Older plastic cards can still be used. If yours is lost or damaged, you request a Confirmation of SIN and you receive a letter in paper or digital format.

Full program rules sit on the Government of Canada [Social Insurance Number](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin.html) page, last updated 3 July 2026. View or print a number you already have through [My Service Canada Account](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/my-account.html).

## Who needs a SIN, and when should you apply?

**Short answer:** You need a SIN if you are legally authorized to work in Canada and you will be working, if you need proof or confirmation of an existing number, if you receive a new permit with a new expiry date, if your immigration status changes, if your legal name changes, or if you are correcting an error on the record. Canadian citizens and permanent residents also apply for a first-time number, for a child's confirmation, or to register a newborn in a territory. Anyone 12 or older can apply for their own SIN. A parent or legal guardian applies for a child under the age of majority in that province or territory.

Apply as soon as you have the documents. Temporary residents use the [SIN for temporary residents](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/temporary-residents.html) path, last updated 2 June 2026. Citizens and permanent residents start from the same [Apply for a SIN](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/apply.html) page. You must apply even if you already have a number when you need to extend a 9-series expiry, confirm a number, or update the record.

If you are visiting with no work authorization and you are not claiming federal benefits, you do not need one.

## What does a SIN that starts with 9 mean?

**Short answer:** SINs issued to temporary residents always start with 9. That number expires on the same date as the work permit, study permit, or visitor record that supported it. Keep the SIN record in step with the current permit. A citizen or permanent resident SIN is permanent and does not expire. When your status changes from temporary resident to permanent resident, you apply again so Service Canada can issue a permanent number. Destroy the old SIN document after the record is updated. It is no longer valid.

| First digit | Issued to | Expires? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 to 7 | Canadian citizens and permanent residents | No |
| 8 | Reserved by Service Canada | Not issued to applicants |
| 9 | Temporary residents authorized to work | Yes, with the immigration document |

That 9-series expiry is the payroll trap. Many systems flag the date and stop pay even when you are still allowed to work. The [temporary residents](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/temporary-residents.html) page is the source for the expiry rule.

## What documents do you need to apply?

**Short answer:** You need one primary identity document that proves your legal status in Canada and one secondary identity document that confirms who you are. If your current name does not match the name on those documents, you also need a supporting document for each name change. Documents that are not in English or French need the original plus a translation. Family members cannot translate. IRCC email messages are not accepted as permit proof. The permit itself has to be in the file.

Primary documents, from the [required documents for SIN](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/required-documents.html) page, last updated 20 May 2026:

- Canadian citizens: a provincial or territorial birth certificate, a certificate of Canadian citizenship, or a Registration of Birth Abroad issued before 1977. Quebec birth documents issued before 1994 are not accepted.
- Permanent residents: a permanent resident card, a Confirmation of Permanent Residence within 1 year of landing, or a Record of Landing issued before 2002. Verification of Landing or Status Verification can only amend a record or confirm an existing SIN.
- Temporary residents: a work permit, a study permit that says you "may work" or "may accept employment" in Canada, a visitor record that authorizes work, or a diplomatic identity card plus a work authorization from Global Affairs Canada.

If the study permit or visitor record is silent on work, contact IRCC about an amended permit before you apply. A standard study permit with no work line does not get you a SIN.

The secondary document must be valid and must show your full legal name and date of birth. A Canadian or foreign passport works. So does a Canadian driver's licence, a provincial or territorial identity card, or other Canadian government-issued ID.

Name-change supporting documents include a marriage certificate (not valid for Quebec residents married after 1 April 1981, wherever the marriage took place), a divorce document, a legal change of name certificate or court order, or an adoption order. If you changed your name more than once, you need a document for each change.

## How do you apply online, by mail, or in person?

**Short answer:** Online is the fastest route. You upload clear digital copies of both sides of each document, including the borders. Processing is about 5 business days to view the SIN confirmation letter in My Service Canada Account, or before the confirmation is mailed. Mail takes about 20 business days. You send original documents to Service Canada Social Insurance Registration Office, PO Box 7000, Bathurst NB E2A 4T1, Canada. Service Canada returns the documents by mail and is not responsible for items lost in transit. In person, you bring originals to a Service Canada office.

Start at [Apply for a SIN](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/apply.html) and pick your status and channel. The online form is at [sin-nas.canada.ca](https://sin-nas.canada.ca/en/Sin/). Photograph documents flat, in even light, with all four edges visible. Glare and cropped borders are the usual reason an upload is rejected.

You can start working as soon as you apply. You do not wait for the number. Your employer still has to record the SIN, so follow up when the confirmation letter is ready.

## What happens if your 9-series SIN expires while you wait on a new permit?

**Short answer:** If the SIN expires but you applied to extend the permit and you are on maintained status, you can continue working with the expired SIN until IRCC makes a decision. That is Service Canada's published rule on the [temporary residents](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/temporary-residents.html) page. Once the new permit arrives, apply to extend the SIN expiry so the record matches. After the update, destroy the old SIN document.

Payroll software often ignores maintained status and flags the expired number. Bring the extension receipt and the Service Canada wording. Then update the SIN the day the new permit is in hand. IRCC emails are still not enough. You need the permit document itself.

Maintained status is an IRCC rule, not a Service Canada invention. If you did not apply to extend before the permit expired, you are not on maintained status. Do not assume the expired SIN still covers work in that case.

## How do you find a SIN you already have?

**Short answer:** Sign in to [My Service Canada Account](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/my-account.html) and view or print it. If you cannot get into the account, look on an income tax return, a tax slip such as a T4, a Record of Employment, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan contribution receipt. If you still cannot find it, apply for a Confirmation of SIN. That process uses the same documents as a first-time application. It confirms the existing number. It does not issue a new one.

A 9-series SIN must be valid to use My Service Canada Account. If it has expired, extend it first using the [temporary residents](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/temporary-residents.html) steps. The [damaged, forgotten or lost SIN](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/lost.html) page, last updated 2 June 2026, is the source for recovery. If you find someone else's card or letter, return it to a Service Canada Centre or mail it to the Bathurst registration office.

Service Canada issues a new number only when there is clear evidence the current SIN has been used fraudulently. That path is [SIN fraud or data breach](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/fraud-data-breaches.html), not a routine confirmation.

## What mistakes cost newcomers time or pay?

**Short answer:** Arriving with only the permit and no secondary ID. Uploading cropped or glare-filled scans. Treating an IRCC email as the permit. Letting a 9-series expiry sit after a new permit arrives. Putting the number on a resume. Paying a third party to "get" a SIN. Assuming a study permit authorizes work when the document does not say so. After you land, the number belongs on payroll and tax forms, almost nowhere else.

Give the number to an employer after you have accepted a job, not on the application form. Nobody from Service Canada or the Canada Revenue Agency will email or text asking you to send the number. Use a canada.ca contact path if a message looks official.

We are Go Far Global, a licensed Canadian immigration firm. A SIN is a Service Canada file, not an IRCC visa, but the two lock together on every work permit and study-permit-with-work file we see. If the permit wording, maintained status, or a 9-series expiry is blocking payroll, [book a consultation](/book) and we will read the documents with you.

## Sources

- [Social Insurance Number (Service Canada, updated 2026-07-03)](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin.html)
- [SIN for temporary residents (updated 2026-06-02)](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/temporary-residents.html)
- [Apply for a SIN](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/apply.html)
- [Required documents for SIN (updated 2026-05-20)](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/required-documents.html)
- [Damaged, forgotten or lost SIN (updated 2026-06-02)](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/lost.html)
- [My Service Canada Account](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/my-account.html)

# Bill C-12 Is Now Law. The Federal Court Just Grouped the Constitutional Challenges.

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/bill-c12-passed-constitutional-challenges-2026
Category: News
Published: 2026-05-15
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Bill C-12 received Royal Assent on March 26, 2026.

# Bill C-12 Is Now Law. The Federal Court Just Grouped the Constitutional Challenges.

[Bill C-12 received Royal Assent](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/2026/03/new-immigration-and-asylum-measures-from-bill-c-12-the-strengthening-canadas-immigration-system-and-borders-act-have-become-law.html) on March 26, 2026. Today a Federal Court associate judge granted a request to case-manage the constitutional challenges against the new asylum rules as a single group. Roughly three dozen files are already in the docket. The Canadian Association of Refugee Lawyers (CARL) and the Canadian Immigration Lawyers Association (CILA) are coordinating the litigation. The arguments turn on [Charter section 7](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/const/page-12.html) (life, liberty, and security of the person) and section 15 (equality and non-discrimination).

*As of May 15, 2026.*

The bill is in force now. The litigation does not freeze it. Anyone with a refugee claim filed, planned, or potentially needed should understand what the rule actually does, who it catches, and what the court timeline looks like.

```youtube
Whvv_fECsqk
```

## What did Bill C-12 change after passing its constitutional challenges?

**Short answer:** Three core changes, a one-year cap on filing refugee claims measured from first entry to Canada (not most recent entry), retroactive to June 24, 2020 (central reason CARL/CILA argue Charter section 7 violation), and a separate bar for irregular Canada-US border crossers on or after June 3, 2025; Pre-Removal Risk Assessment remains but with much lower acceptance rates than a full Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB) hearing.

The core of Bill C-12 is a hard cap on when a person can make a refugee claim in Canada. Three changes matter most.

**A one-year time limit from first entry.** A person is now barred from filing a refugee claim if more than 12 months have passed since their first entry into Canada. The clock runs from the first entry, not the most recent one. A person who came to Canada three years ago on a study permit, returned home for a vacation in year two, came back, and then watched conditions in their country deteriorate is treated as having entered three years ago for C-12 purposes.

**Retroactivity to June 24, 2020.** The one-year cap reaches back to entries made on or after June 24, 2020. The retroactive scope is the central reason CARL and CILA argue the rule violates Charter section 7. People who arrived legally before the law existed are now told the door behind them has closed.

**A separate bar for irregular border crossers after June 2025.** People who crossed the Canada-US border irregularly on or after June 3, 2025 have lost the ability to make a refugee claim entirely. This is independent of the one-year rule and follows the Safe Third Country Agreement framework.

The bill leaves the [Pre-Removal Risk Assessment (PRRA)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/refugees/claim-protection-inside-canada.html) process intact, but PRRA is a narrower test with a much lower acceptance rate than a full refugee hearing. For people caught by the new bars, PRRA is what remains.

| Rule | Who it affects | Key threshold |
|------|---------------|---------------|
| One-year filing cap | Entered Canada on or after June 24, 2020 | File refugee claim within 12 months of first entry |
| Irregular border crossing bar | Crossed Canada-US border irregularly | On or after June 3, 2025 |
| PRRA | Barred from the refugee claim stream | Available, but acceptance rates are lower than a full IRB hearing |

## What did the Federal Court decide on the Bill C-12 constitutional challenges?

**Short answer:** By mid-May the Federal Court held roughly 36 constitutional challenges raising overlapping issues, today a Federal Court associate judge granted case-management coordination across the entire group (procedural, not merits); CARL expects oral hearings on constitutional questions in 12 to 18 months with appeals likely extending the timeline.

The constitutional challenges started landing within weeks of Royal Assent. By mid-May the Federal Court was holding roughly 36 separate files raising overlapping issues. Today an associate judge granted a motion to case-manage the entire group together, which is a procedural step that lets one judge coordinate scheduling, evidence, and shared legal questions across the files. It does not decide the merits.

The expected legal arguments:

- **Section 7 (life, liberty, security of the person).** Deporting a person to a country where they would face persecution, based on a clock rather than the merits of their claim, raises a serious section 7 issue. Refugee jurisprudence in Canada has consistently treated removal to persecution as engaging section 7. The challenge is whether the one-year cap is consistent with the principles of fundamental justice.

- **Section 15 (equality).** The rule falls disproportionately on people whose country conditions changed after they arrived in Canada. The countries where such changes are most common are not random in origin or demographic profile, and CARL has signalled that the equality argument will look at the disparate impact on specific national-origin groups.

- **Section 1 (justification).** The government will argue that the rule is a proportionate response to fraud in the refugee system. The court will assess whether the means chosen (a hard time cap) are rationally connected to that objective and whether they impair the right minimally.

CARL has indicated it expects oral hearings on the constitutional questions within roughly 12 to 18 months, with appeals likely to follow regardless of the outcome.

## What is the government's argument for Bill C-12?

**Short answer:** The government public framing of C-12 targets fraud, brokers coaching claimants on country-condition narratives, document mills recycling affidavits, IRB data showing wide country-of-origin acceptance variation; the dispute is whether a time cap is the right tool since it catches slow filers but not coordinated brokers, while alternatives like IRB front-end credibility hearings, per-country acceptance rate data, and CBSA broker prosecutions target fraud directly.

The government's public framing of Bill C-12 has been about combatting fraud. The framing is not invented. Brokers in source countries coach claimants on country-condition narratives. Document mills produce affidavit packages that recycle across multiple files with new names. The IRB tracks these patterns and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) publishes acceptance rate data showing wide variation by country of origin. Fraud in the refugee stream is a real problem.

The dispute is whether a time limit is the right tool against it. A time limit catches the slow filer. It does not catch a coordinated broker, who moves clients through the system fast and inside any window. The 1951 Refugee Convention measures protection against current country conditions, and conditions can change after a person has been in Canada for years. The critique CARL is making is that the one-year cap separates real claimants from the system without filtering the fraudulent ones.

Front-end credibility hearings at the IRB, public per-country acceptance rate data, and broker prosecutions by CBSA are the tools refugee lawyers and academics have pointed to as alternatives that target fraud directly without barring refugees whose persecution emerged on Canadian soil.

## Who does Bill C-12 affect under the new rules?

**Short answer:** Affected profiles, students or workers in Canada more than one year whose country deteriorated, family members who arrived legally and stayed past a year before persecution developed at home, irregular crossers on/after June 3, 2025 who lost the refugee option immediately, and failed claimants from earlier in the 2020s whose files were already in process when the law passed (one of the strongest section 7 fact patterns).

Several profiles are now affected:

- **Students or workers in Canada for more than one year whose country has deteriorated.** Authoritarian shifts, civil conflict, and targeted persecution of religious or political minorities have all produced post-arrival refugee fears in cases the IRB used to hear regularly. Many of those cases will now be barred from the refugee stream.

- **Family members who came to Canada legally and stayed past a year.** Spouses, adult children, and dependents who arrived on temporary status before persecution developed at home fall into the same bar.

- **Irregular crossers after June 2025.** People who entered between official ports of entry on or after June 3, 2025 lost the refugee claim option immediately and cannot recover it through delay or merit arguments.

- **Failed claimants from earlier in the 2020s whose claims are still in motion.** The retroactive provision creates particular concern for people whose files were already in process when the law passed. CARL has signalled this is one of the strongest section 7 fact patterns in the litigation.

## What should you do if Bill C-12 affects your refugee claim?

**Short answer:** Time-sensitive actions, if inside the one-year window from first entry, file now (do not wait for litigation); if past the window with deteriorated country conditions, consult on PRRA and H&C options; if a family member abroad with deteriorating situation might come to Canada, consult on sequencing since the one-year clock starts on first entry; get a written assessment from a regulated practitioner for uncertain cases.

The litigation will play out over a year or longer, with appeals likely. The law remains in force during that period.

For anyone in or near these categories, the practical decisions are time-sensitive:

- **If you are inside the one-year window from your first entry, file now.** Do not wait for the litigation to clarify. The window is hard.

- **If you are past the one-year window and your country conditions have changed, talk to a refugee lawyer about PRRA and any humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) options.** PRRA acceptance rates are low but it is not zero, and H&C decisions take a broader view of the file.

- **If you have a family member with a deteriorating situation abroad who might come to Canada, consult on sequencing.** The one-year clock starts on first entry. The order in which family members arrive and whether they remain continuously in Canada both matter.

- **If you are uncertain whether the law affects your case, get a written assessment from a regulated practitioner.** The fine print of C-12 carries more weight than the headline rule, and several of the categories interact with study permit, work permit, and permanent residence applications already in progress.

## What happens next with the Bill C-12 constitutional challenges?

**Short answer:** The Federal Court case-management order today is the first procedural milestone; evidence and oral argument schedules should follow over the summer; decisions on section 7 and section 15 questions are likely 12 to 18 months out with appeals to the Federal Court of Appeal and potentially the Supreme Court likely to extend the timeline further.

The Federal Court's case-management order today is the first procedural milestone. Schedules for evidence and oral argument should follow over the summer. Decisions on the section 7 and section 15 questions are likely 12 to 18 months out, with appeals to the Federal Court of Appeal and potentially the Supreme Court likely to extend the timeline further.

Bill C-12 is the most significant change to Canadian refugee law since the 2012 reforms. The constitutional questions it raises will shape how Canada handles asylum claims for years. People affected by it should not wait for the courts to decide.

[Book a consultation with Go Far Global](/appointment) if you have a file affected by Bill C-12 or are uncertain whether the new rules apply to you. Our team handles transition cases every week and can give you a written assessment of your options under the new law.

# Urgent PR Card Processing in Canada (2026): Who Qualifies and How to Apply

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/pr-card-urgent-processing
Category: Permanent Residence
Published: 2026-05-10
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Standard PR card renewal takes 30 to 95 days.

# Urgent PR Card Processing in Canada (2026): Who Qualifies and How to Apply

Standard Permanent Resident (PR) card renewal takes 30 to 95 days. If you have urgent travel coming up and your card has expired or will expire before you return, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) offers urgent processing at no extra cost. The catch is that you need to prove the urgency with documents.

*As of May 2026.*

This guide covers who qualifies, what to submit, and what happens if the request is refused.

## Who qualifies for urgent PR card processing?

**Short answer:** IRCC accepts urgent processing for three reasons within three months: family member death, serious illness, or critical condition; work travel your job depends on; or serious medical reason that cannot wait, and weddings, graduations, religious holidays, and family reunions do not qualify on their own.

IRCC accepts urgent processing requests for three reasons:

1. **A family member has died, is seriously ill, or is in critical condition** and you need to travel within three months to be with them.
2. **You need to travel for work** and your job depends on the trip happening within three months.
3. **You need to travel for a serious medical reason** that cannot wait.

These are the only accepted reasons. A vacation, a family event that is not a medical or bereavement emergency, or general inconvenience does not qualify. IRCC reviewers look for documents that match the stated reason.

The official criteria are at [canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/new-immigrants/pr-card/apply-renew-replace.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/new-immigrants/pr-card/apply-renew-replace.html). Full eligibility requirements for urgent processing are at [canada.ca, Apply urgently for a permanent resident card](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/permanent-residents/card/urgent.html).

## How long does urgent PR card processing take?

**Short answer:** Approved urgent requests process in roughly 30 calendar days, but IRCC does not guarantee a specific timeline. If your travel date is less than 30 days away, consider rebooking, applying for a PRTD abroad, or returning by land from the US which does not require a PR card.

Approved urgent requests are usually processed within 30 calendar days. IRCC does not guarantee a specific timeline. The actual time depends on the volume of urgent requests in the queue and whether your application package is complete.

If your travel date is less than 30 days away, urgent processing may not arrive in time. In that case, consider:

- Rebooking the trip
- Applying for a Permanent Resident Travel Document at a Canadian visa office abroad after you depart
- Returning by land from the United States, which does not require a PR card

## What documents do you need to submit?

**Short answer:** Submit the complete IMM 5444 renewal package plus a typed urgent-request letter, proof of travel (confirmed flight reservation), and reason-matching supporting documents: doctor letter or death certificate for family medical/bereavement, employer letter on company letterhead for work travel, or treating physician note for medical emergencies. Place a bold "URGENT PROCESSING REQUEST" cover sheet on top.

The urgent request is in addition to the standard renewal application (form IMM 5444). Submit the complete renewal package plus:

1. **A typed letter** explaining the reason for the urgent request. State the qualifying category, the date of travel, and why the trip cannot be postponed.
2. **Proof of travel**. A confirmed flight reservation, ticket, or booking confirmation showing your name and the travel date.
3. **Supporting documents that match the qualifying reason**:
   - **Family illness or death**: doctor's letter on letterhead, death certificate, or hospital confirmation. Include proof of the family relationship if it is not obvious from your existing IRCC file.
   - **Urgent work travel**: a letter from your employer on company letterhead stating the work obligation, the date, and why you specifically need to travel. The letter should include a contact phone number.
   - **Medical emergency**: a letter from your treating physician describing the condition, the recommended treatment location, and why the treatment cannot be received in Canada or postponed.

| Qualifying Reason | Required Supporting Documents |
|---|---|
| Family illness or death | Doctor's letter on letterhead, death certificate, or hospital confirmation; proof of family relationship |
| Work travel | Employer letter on company letterhead with contact number, stating the work obligation and travel date |
| Medical emergency | Treating physician's letter describing the condition, treatment location, and why treatment cannot be received in Canada or postponed |

Include a cover sheet that says "URGENT PROCESSING REQUEST" in bold at the top of the package. Place it on top of everything else.

## How do you submit an urgent PR card request?

**Short answer:** Mail the complete package via tracked courier (Canada Post Xpresspost, FedEx, UPS) to Case Processing Centre PR Card, P.O. Box 10020, Sydney NS B1P 7C1, Canada. Standard mail eats into your urgent window and the IRCC mailroom does not accept hand deliveries.

Mail the complete package to the same address as a regular PR card renewal:

> Case Processing Centre - PR Card
> P.O. Box 10020
> Sydney NS B1P 7C1
> Canada

Use a tracked courier service (Canada Post Xpresspost, FedEx, UPS). Standard mail can take a week to arrive at CPC-Sydney, which eats into your urgent processing window. The IRCC mailroom does not accept hand deliveries.

The IRCC Web Form is sometimes mentioned as an alternative for urgent requests already in progress. It is not a substitute for the initial mailed application. Use it only if you have already submitted and need to add supporting documents.

## What happens after you submit an urgent PR card request?

**Short answer:** CPC-Sydney reviews the urgent request before opening the standard renewal. You receive an Acknowledgement of Receipt confirming arrival, then within 5 to 10 business days a second letter confirming whether urgent processing was approved or refused; approved files process in 30 days, refused files drop back to the 30 to 95 day standard queue with no fee refund.

CPC-Sydney reviews the urgent request before opening the standard renewal. You receive an Acknowledgement of Receipt that confirms the package arrived. The acknowledgement does not confirm that urgent processing was approved.

A second letter follows, usually within 5 to 10 business days, telling you whether urgent processing was approved or refused.

**If approved**: Your card is processed within 30 days and mailed to you.

**If refused**: Your application drops back to the standard processing queue (30 to 95 days). The $50 fee is not refunded. You can request reconsideration by submitting additional documents through the IRCC Web Form, but reconsideration is not guaranteed and adds time.

## Why are urgent PR card requests refused?

**Short answer:** Frequent refusal causes: travel date more than 3 months away (hard cap), reason outside the three qualifying categories, insufficient supporting documents (flight booking alone is not enough), applicant outside Canada (apply for a PRTD instead), or open residency-obligation issues already flagged on the file.

The most common refusal reasons are:

- **Travel date more than three months away**. Three months is a hard cap. Trips planned six months out do not qualify.
- **Travel reason does not match a qualifying category**. Weddings, graduations, religious holidays, and family reunions are not qualifying reasons unless they tie to a documented serious illness or death.
- **Insufficient supporting documents**. A flight booking alone is not enough. The qualifying reason itself needs documentation.
- **The applicant is outside Canada**. Urgent PR card processing is for residents inside Canada. If you are abroad, apply for a Permanent Resident Travel Document instead.
- **The applicant has open residency obligation issues**. If your file already has a flagged residency obligation problem, urgent processing is unlikely until the underlying review is complete.

## What are the alternatives if urgent processing is not available?

**Short answer:** Three alternatives: Permanent Resident Travel Document ($50 fee, issued at a Canadian visa office abroad for one-time return), land re-entry from the US (no PR card required, prove status with IRCC documents and passport at the border), or postpone non-essential travel and apply normally.

If you do not qualify for urgent processing or the timing is too tight:

**Permanent Resident Travel Document (PRTD)**. Issued by a Canadian visa office abroad, lets you board a flight back to Canada one time. Apply after you depart. The PRTD costs $50 and is separate from the PR card fee. Details at [Permanent Resident Travel Document](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/permanent-residents/travel-document.html) on canada.ca.

**Land entry from the United States**. If your trip allows for a return by land from the U.S., you do not need a PR card. You need to prove your PR status to a CBSA officer at the border using your IRCC documents and passport.

**Postpone non-essential travel**. The standard 30 to 95 day processing time is reasonable for most situations. Pushing the trip back and applying normally is often the lowest-risk path.

## What are the most common questions about urgent PR card processing?

**Short answer:** Urgent processing costs the same $50 standard fee; approved files arrive in ~30 days from IRCC approval (not from submission); urgent processing is available for lost-card replacement using the same criteria; if your trip is sooner than 30 days, use a PRTD or land entry; IRCC may call your employer or doctor to verify urgency claims.

**Does urgent processing cost extra?**
No. The fee is the same $50 as a standard renewal. The full fee breakdown is in [the PR card renewal fees article](/news/pr-card-renewal-fees-2026).

**How quickly can I get a PR card if approved for urgent processing?**
Around 30 days from when IRCC approves the urgent request, not from when you submit.

**Can I request urgent processing for a lost card replacement?**
Yes. The same eligibility criteria and process apply. Use form IMM 5444 with the urgent cover letter. Full lost-card process is at [the lost PR card replacement guide](/news/lost-pr-card-replacement).

**What if my trip is sooner than 30 days?**
Urgent processing likely will not arrive in time. Look at PRTD or land-entry alternatives.

**Will IRCC contact me to confirm the urgency?**
Sometimes. They may call the employer listed on your employment letter or the doctor on the medical letter. Make sure contact details are accurate.

**What if my urgent request is refused but I still need to travel?**
Your application stays in the queue at standard processing speed. If you must travel before it arrives, apply for a PRTD from abroad after you leave Canada.

## What should you do next?

If your urgent travel falls within the qualifying categories and you have the documents ready, submit the complete package as soon as possible. Processing time starts from the date CPC-Sydney receives the application, not from when you mail it. Every day spent gathering documents or in transit reduces your window.

The full PR card renewal process, residency obligation calculations, and standard processing path are at [the PR card renewal pillar page](/immigration/extensions/pr-card-renewal). For Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) review of an urgent application before submission, [book a consultation](/appointment).

# Express Entry Tie-Breaking Rule: Profile Date and Time

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/crs-tie-breaking-rule
Category: Express Entry
Published: 2026-05-10
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Every Express Entry draw has a Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) cut-off. Candidates above the cut-off receive Invitations to Apply (ITAs); candidates below do not.

# Express Entry Tie-Breaking Rule: Profile Date and Time

*As of August 31, 2026.*

Every Express Entry round has a Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) cut-off. Candidates above that score receive an invitation to apply. Candidates below it do not. When more than one candidate sits at the lowest invited score, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) does not pick at random. It uses the date and time each person submitted their Express Entry profile.

## TL;DR

If more than one candidate has the lowest score, the cut-off is the date and time they submitted their Express Entry profiles | Earlier submission wins among people tied at the cut-off score | Updating a profile does not change the date and time IRCC received it, so you keep your tie rank | You have 60 days to finish and submit a new profile or you start again | IRCC publishes the tie-breaking timestamp with each round on the rounds of invitations page

## What is the Express Entry tie-breaking rule?

**Short answer:** When IRCC invites candidates and more than one person has the lowest score, the cut-off for that round is based on the date and time they submitted their Express Entry profiles. IRCC prints that sentence on the [rounds of invitations](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/rounds-invitations.html) page, under Tie-breaking rule. Candidates with a higher CRS than the cut-off are invited regardless of timestamp. Candidates below the cut-off are not invited, no matter how early they submitted. The rule only ranks people who are tied at the lowest invited score.

IRCC chooses the type of round, decides how many candidates to invite, identifies the highest-ranking eligible people in the pool, and invites them to apply for permanent residence. Each round has instructions posted at the time of the round. Those instructions include the date and time of the round, the number of invitations, the round type, and, where it applies, the program or category.

Do not treat a screenshot of last month's cut-off as a promise. The live number is the one IRCC publishes for that round. A recap site can lag a draw by hours.

## How does a round actually use the timestamp?

**Short answer:** IRCC ranks eligible profiles by CRS. It issues invitations from the top down until it fills the round. If the last invitations fall on a group of people with the same CRS, only those whose profiles were received at or before the published tie-breaking date and time are invited. A profile received one second later, at the same CRS, stays in the pool. IRCC states the tie-breaking timestamp on the round result. The latest-round box on the rounds page is filled when a round runs. Read that box, or the ministerial instructions for that round, rather than a third-party recap.

Round types, from the same IRCC page:

| Round type | Who is invited |
|---|---|
| General | Top-ranking candidates eligible for one of the three Express Entry programs |
| Program-specific | Top-ranking candidates eligible for one program, for example a Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) round |
| Category-based | Top-ranking candidates eligible for a category the Minister set to meet an economic goal |

You still have to be eligible for one of the three programs managed through Express Entry to sit in the pool: the Canadian Experience Class (CEC), the Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP), or the Federal Skilled Trades Program. Candidates with a provincial or territorial nomination continue to be invited through general and PNP-specific rounds.

This article does not invent a current cut-off or a fake round number. Cut-offs move. Confirm the latest round on the [official rounds page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/rounds-invitations.html) and, for the historical table, on [ministerial instructions respecting Express Entry rounds](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/ministerial-instructions/express-entry-rounds.html).

## Does editing your profile reset the tie-breaking clock?

**Short answer:** No. IRCC says updating your profile does not change the date and time that it received the profile, so you keep your rank if you are in a tie-breaker situation. That sentence is on the [create your Express Entry profile](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/create-profile.html) page. Improving language scores, adding a job offer, fixing education, or updating family status can change your CRS. It does not give you a new submission timestamp.

You must update the profile if your situation changes: a new career, a job offer gained or lost, a new language test, marriage or divorce, or a new child. Language results and an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) can expire while you sit in the pool. Work experience can age out of the program window. Proof of funds can fall below the current table. Those problems can make the profile ineligible. They still do not rewind the original received date.

Withdrawing the profile and creating a new one is a new submission. That is the step that would replace the timestamp. Most people have no reason to do it.

## When should you submit the profile?

**Short answer:** Submit once you meet the minimum eligibility for CEC, FSWP, or Federal Skilled Trades, rather than waiting to polish every optional field. IRCC gives you 60 days to complete and submit a new profile. After that you start again. That 60-day clock is the create-and-submit window, not the tie-breaking rule. The tie-breaking clock starts at the moment the complete profile is submitted to the pool.

IRCC ranks you on the information in the profile. If you are eligible for more than one program, the system invites you in this order: CEC, then FSWP, then Federal Skilled Trades. You cannot choose the program on the invitation. If you decline, you go back to the pool. A later invitation uses the same order.

Use the [CRS calculator](/tools/crs-calculator) to see how language, education, and Canadian work experience move the score. Then read [Express Entry](/immigration/express-entry) for program eligibility. A timestamp only matters if you are actually in the pool at the cut-off.

Incomplete profiles are not a shortcut. IRCC still needs a submitted, eligible profile. Entering the pool with a score you cannot support at application stage wastes the timestamp you were trying to protect. Fix the documents you will need after an invitation (language, ECA, work letters) while the profile sits, rather than delaying the submit itself.

## When does the tie-breaking rule not matter?

**Short answer:** If your CRS is well above recent cut-offs for the round type you are eligible for, you are invited on score alone. If you are well below, an early timestamp does not pull you into the round. The rule matters when you are at, or one point off, the lowest invited score. That is a small slice of the pool, and it is the slice that emails us after a draw.

Category-based and program-specific rounds use different cut-offs than general rounds. A CEC-only round can invite a score that a general round would skip. Check the round type before you decide the timestamp saved or cost you an invitation.

Keep the profile eligible while you wait. Expired language tests, an expired ECA, and stale proof of funds take people out of the pool even when the timestamp is excellent. IRCC listed those as common reasons a profile becomes ineligible on the create-profile page.

A category-based round can also look like a miss when it was never your category. If IRCC ran a French-language or healthcare round, a general-pool timestamp does not move you into that draw. Read the round type first, then the CRS, then the timestamp.

## What should you do after you are in the pool?

**Short answer:** Keep the profile accurate, raise CRS where you can, and watch official round results rather than rumours. IRCC's own list of score improvements is a valid job offer, a provincial nomination, better language scores, more education, and more skilled work experience. A PNP nomination is still the largest single CRS jump available through Express Entry. None of those updates reset the received date.

When a round runs, read the CRS of the lowest-ranked candidate invited and the tie-breaking timestamp together. If you were at that CRS, compare your submission time to the published cut-off time, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) as IRCC prints it. If you were above the CRS, you do not need the timestamp. If you were below, you need a higher score or a different round type, not an earlier clock.

The CRS distribution table on the rounds page is a snapshot of the pool a few days before a round. IRCC notes that the distribution changes as people submit new profiles and as other profiles expire. Use it as context, not as a guarantee that your band will be invited next week.

We are Go Far Global, a licensed Canadian immigration firm. If you want a file-specific read of CRS, program eligibility, and whether you should sit in the pool or fix documents first, [book a consultation](/book).

- [Express Entry rounds of invitations (tie-breaking rule wording)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/rounds-invitations.html)
- [Create your Express Entry profile (updates keep the received date; 60-day submit window)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/create-profile.html)

- [Express Entry overview](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry.html)

# Lost PR Card in Canada 2026: Replace It, Fee, Wait

URL: https://www.gofarglobal.com/news/lost-pr-card-replacement
Category: Permanent Residence
Published: 2026-05-10
Author: Go Far Global Team

> Lost your PR card? You can replace your PR card without affecting your status. Losing your Permanent Resident (PR) card does not change your PR status.

# Lost PR Card in Canada 2026: Replace It, Fee, Wait

*As of September 3, 2026.*

If your permanent resident (PR) card is lost, stolen, or damaged, what you do depends on where you are. Inside Canada, apply for a new card in the Permanent Residence Portal. Outside Canada, you cannot have a replacement card mailed abroad. You need a permanent resident travel document (PRTD) to board a commercial vehicle back. The Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) fee is $50.

## TL;DR

In Canada: replace a lost or stolen PR card through the Permanent Residence Portal (IMM 5444) | Outside Canada: apply for a PRTD, not a new plastic card | IRCC fee is $50 per person for a card or a PRTD | Urgent PR card processing cannot finish in less than 3 weeks | Police report: include it if you have one | IRCC mails cards only to Canadian addresses

## What to do if I lost my permanent residence card?

**Short answer:** If you are in Canada, IRCC's help answer [What should I do if my PR card has been lost, stolen or damaged?](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=047&top=12) says apply to have the card replaced. The [get, renew or replace](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/permanent-residents/card/apply.html) page is the how-to: start IMM 5444 in the [Permanent Residence Portal](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/pr-portal.html), upload IMM 5644, pay $50 on the [IRCC pay page](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/pay.asp), and upload the receipt. If you lost the card, include a police report or incident number if you have one. If you only want to report the loss and do not need a new card, IRCC offers a [solemn declaration](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/solemn-declaration-lost-stolen-destroyed-never-received-permanent-resident-card.html).

If you are outside Canada and will return on an airplane, bus, boat, or train, apply for a [PRTD](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/permanent-residents/travel-document.html). If you return in a private vehicle, IRCC says you can use other documents. [Who can apply](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/permanent-residents/card/eligibility.html) still requires you to be in Canada before IRCC will mail a PR card.

Do not use guide [IMM 5530](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/guide-5530-request-reissue-permanent-resident-card-card.html) for a lost card. That kit is for an IRCC error on a card you still hold.

## How much is a replacement PR card?

**Short answer:** $50 per person. IRCC's [How much does a permanent resident card cost?](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=059&top=10) and the [fee list](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/fees/fees.asp) use the same line for renew and replace. A PRTD is also $50. Pay outside the portal, then upload the receipt. Refunds are not possible while the application is in progress. Photo fees are extra.

| Document | IRCC fee (CAD) | Where IRCC sends it |
|---|---:|---|
| Replacement PR card | 50.00 | Canadian address only |
| Permanent resident travel document | 50.00 | Issued so you can travel back |

Renewal of a card that is simply expiring uses the same $50 and the same portal. That walkthrough is [PR card renewal](/news/pr-card-renewal-canada-2026-complete-guide).

## How long does it take to replace a lost PR card?

**Short answer:** There is no separate "lost card" clock. Use IRCC's [processing times](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html) tool, permanent resident cards, renewing or replacing. The figure is updated weekly and describes recent complete files. Urgent processing, if you qualify, still cannot finish a PR card in less than 3 weeks. IRCC says it cannot guarantee you will get the card on time even if the request is urgent.

After approval, IRCC usually mails the card. Check [after you apply](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/permanent-residents/card/after-next-steps.html). Do not file a second replacement because the first one is slow.

## Can I get my PR card urgently?

**Short answer:** Sometimes, and never faster than 3 weeks for a PR card. The [urgent processing](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/permanent-residents/card/urgent.html) page lists reasons: a job opportunity, work tied to your current job, your own serious illness, serious illness or death of a family member, loss or theft of the PR card while you were temporarily outside Canada, a crisis or vulnerable situation, and, for PRTD files only, other reasons an officer may accept. In the portal, check "Yes, my request is urgent." On paper, write "urgent" on the envelope. Include proof: itinerary, tickets, receipts, a letter, a doctor's note, a death certificate, or an employer letter, with translations if needed.

If you are leaving Canada in less than 3 weeks and have not applied for a PR card yet, IRCC cannot process the card in that window. Once you are outside Canada and your flight back is within 5 days, you can apply urgently for a PRTD. Without a card or a PRTD you may return only by land in a private vehicle.

## Can a PR card be tracked?

**Short answer:** IRCC does not give the public a courier tracking number as a standard step. You [check application status](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-status.html) in your account. The after-you-apply page says IRCC usually mails the card to a Canadian address, may ask you to pick it up at an office, and tells you to update your address if you move within 3 weeks. Bring your passport or other travel document if you are told to pick up. There is no public "where is my card on the truck" page.

If rural mail is not delivered to houses, IRCC mails to the arrangement described on that after page. Watch account messages rather than a shipping app.

## How do I check if my PR card is mailed?

**Short answer:** Open the IRCC account or Permanent Residence Portal and read the latest message. IRCC's after-you-apply page is the official "how you'll get your card" text: they mail it if they approve the file, they send cards only to Canadian addresses, and they may switch to office pickup. If you did not get the first card more than 180 days after you gave a Canadian address, that is a different problem, listed on [When should I apply](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=056&top=10). For a replacement after a loss, wait for the approval message, then watch the mail.

Cut the old card in half if it later turns up, so a found card cannot be used. We are Go Far Global, a licensed Canadian immigration firm. If the card vanished abroad and a flight is close, [book a consultation](/book) before you pay for a PRTD you do not need, or skip one that you do.

Photos for the new card must match the [PR card photo](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/permanent-residents/card/photos.html) specifications. A selfie will bounce the file.
